questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt:
A 70-YEAR-OLD PATIENT PRESENTED WITH COUGH, FATIGUABILITY, AND WEIGHT LOSS. HE WAS DIAGNOSED
WITH SQUAMOUS CELL CARCINOMA (SCC) ON BRONCHOSCOPY. THE RESECTED SPECIMEN HAD A HILAR
LYMPH NODE THAT WAS 1CM IN SIZE AND SHOWED A BLACK PIGMENT. WHAT IS THE BLACK PIGMENT
LIKELY TO BE?
questions.explanation:
THE BLACK-COLORED PIGMENT IN THE HILAR LYMPH NODE OF THE RESECTED BRONCHOSCOPIC SPECIMEN IS
LIKELY TO BE AN ANTHRACOTIC PIGMENT.
THE BLACK COLOR IS DUE TO THE DEPOSITION OF CARBON PARTICLES. THE INHALED CARBON PARTICLES ARE
ENGULFED BY THE LUNG MACROPHAGES AND THEN TRANSPORTED TO THE HILAR LYMPH NODES.
THIS ACCUMULATES AND CAUSES THE BLACKENING OF THE LUNG TISSUES OR ANTHRACOSIS.
IT IS COMMONLY SEEN IN PEOPLE WHO WORK IN ENVIRONMENTS WHERE THERE IS HIGH AIR POLLUTION WITH
CARBON PARTICLES, SUCH AS COAL MINES. IT IS ALSO THE MOST COMMON EXOGENOUS PIGMENT FOUND IN THE
HUMAN BODY AS A RESULT OF AIR POLLUTION IN URBAN AREAS. THE AGGREGATES OF THE CARBON DUST MAY
INDUCE FIBROBLASTIC REACTION OR EMPHYSEMA THAT MAY LEAD TO A CONDITION CALLED COAL WORKER'S
PNEUMOCONIOSIS.
THE FOLLOWING IMAGE SHOWS ANTHRACOSIS WITH DEPOSITION OF BLACK CARBON PARTICLES, WITHIN THE
CYTOPLASM OF MACROPHAGES.
2065
OPTION B: MELANIN IS BROWN-BLACK IN COLOR WHICH OCCURS AS A RESULT OF OXIDATION OF TYROSINE IN
MELANOCYTES, AS SHOWN IN THE FOLLOWING HISTOPATHOLOGY OF A LYMPH NODE.
2066
OPTION C: LIPOCHROME OR LIPOFUSCIN (BROWN LIPID) IS SEEN AS A YELLOW-BROWN PIGMENT IN
HISTOPATHOLOGICAL SECTIONS OF THE LIVER AND HEART OF NORMAL AGING PATIENTS, PATIENTS WITH SEVERE
MALNUTRITION, AND CANCER CACHEXIA. IT IS DERIVED THROUGH LIPID PEROXIDATION AND INDICATES FREE
RADICAL INJURY AND LIPID PEROXIDATION. THE FOLLOWING IMAGE SHOWS A CARDIAC MYOCYTE WITH FINE
YELLOW-BROWN LIPOFUSCIN GRANULES IN THE PERINUCLEAR REGION.

OPTION D: HEMOSIDERIN IS A HEMOGLOBIN-DERIVED GOLDEN-YELLOW COLORED PIGMENT SEEN IN CONDITIONS
ASSOCIATED WITH IRON OVERLOAD SUCH AS HEMOCHROMATOSIS. THE FOLLOWING IMAGE SHOWS EXTENSIVE
INTRA-ALVEOLAR HEMOSIDERIN DEPOSITION FOLLOWING PULMONARY HEMORRHAGE.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt:
A 34-YEAR-OLD FEMALE PATIENT PRESENTED TO THE OUTPATIENT DEPARTMENT WITH MIGRATORY ARTHRITIS
AND EXAMINATION REVEALED A PAN-SYSTOLIC MURMUR. AN ECHOCARDIOGRAPHY WAS PERFORMED WHICH
WAS SUGGESTIVE OF MITRAL REGURGITATION. A BIOPSY SPECIMEN WAS OBTAINED AND THE IMAGE IS
PROVIDED BELOW. WHAT IS THE MOST LIKELY LESION SHOWN IN THE HISTOPATHOLOGY SLIDE?
questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN CLINICAL FINDINGS OF MIGRATORY ARTHRITIS, PAN-SYSTOLIC MURMUR, AND MITRAL REGURGITATION
ARE SUGGESTIVE OF ACUTE RHEUMATIC FEVER. THE MOST LIKELY LESION SHOWN IN THE HISTOPATHOLOGICAL SLIDE
IS ASCHOFF'S BODIES.
ASCHOFF'S BODIES ARE THE LESIONS FOUND IN THE HEART DURING ACUTE RHEUMATIC FEVER. THEY ARE
COMPOSED OF FOCI OF T LYMPHOCYTES, OCCASIONAL PLASMA CELLS, AND PLUMP-ACTIVATED MACROPHAGES
CALLED ANITSCHKOW CELLS. ANITSCHKOW CELLS HAVE ABUNDANT CYTOPLASM AND CENTRAL ROUND-TO-OVOID
NUCLEI WITH CHROMATIN THAT IS CENTRALLY CONDENSED INTO A SLENDER, WAVY RIBBON. HENCE THEY ARE ALSO
2068
CALLED CATERPILLAR CELLS.
DURING ACUTE RHEUMATIC FEVER, ASCHOFF BODIES MAY BE FOUND IN ANY OF THE THREE LAYERS OF THE HEART
THAT RESULTS IN PERICARDITIS, MYOCARDITIS, OR ENDOCARDITIS.
FIBRINOID NECROSIS CAN OCCUR DUE TO INFLAMMATION OF THE ENDOCARDIUM AND THE LEFT-SIDED VALVES.
OVER THESE AREAS OF NECROSIS, SMALL VEGETATIONS CAN BE SEEN ALONG THE LINES OF CLOSURE, CALLED
VERRUCAE. IRREGULAR THICKENINGS CALLED MACCALLUM PLAQUES CAN BE PRESENT IN THE SUBENDOCARDIUM.
IN CHRONIC RHD, THE MITRAL VALVE SHOWS LEAFLET THICKENING, COMMISSURAL FUSION AND SHORTENING,
AND THICKENING AND FUSION OF THE TENDINOUS CORDS. CALCIFICATION AND FIBROUS BRIDGING OF THE VALVE
CAN LEAD TO NARROWING THE MITRAL ORIFICE AND GIVING IT A FISH MOUTH APPEARANCE.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt:
A 30-YEAR-OLD MALE COMPLAINED OF FATIGUE FOR THE PAST 1 YEAR. EXAMINATION REVEALED MASSIVE
SPLENOMEGALY. HIS BLOOD WORKUP SHOWS THE FOLLOWING FINDINGS. WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING IS THE
MOST SENSITIVE INVESTIGATION IN THIS CASE?
questions.explanation:
THE CLINICAL PRESENTATION WITH FATIGUE, SPLENOMEGALY, AND THE PERIPHERAL BLOOD SMEAR FINDINGS ARE
SUGGESTIVE OF CHRONIC MYELOGENOUS LEUKEMIA(CML). THE BCR-ABL GENE WHICH IS SPECIFIC FOR CML
IS DETECTED BY FLUORESCENCE IN SITU HYBRIDIZATION(FISH) OR POLYMERASE CHAIN REACTION(PCR) BASED
TESTS.
CHRONIC MYELOGENOUS LEUKEMIA (CML) IS A MYELOPROLIFERATIVE DISORDER WITH THE PEAK INCIDENCE IN
THE FIFTH TO SIXTH DECADE OF LIFE. THE CHIMERIC BCR-ABL GENE IS CREATED BY A RECIPROCAL
(9;22)(Q34;Q11) TRANSLOCATION(PHILADELPHIA CHROMOSOME). THIS BCR-ABL GENE DISTINGUISHES CML
FROM OTHER MYELOPROLIFERATIVE DISORDERS AND IS DETECTED BY FLUORESCENT IN SITU HYBRIDIZATION (FISH)
OR POLYMERASE CHAIN REACTION (PCR).
CLINICAL FEATURES:
MILD TO MODERATE ANEMIA AND HYPERMETABOLISM, FATIGABILITY, WEAKNESS, WEIGHT LOSS, AND ANOREXIA.
DRAGGING SENSATION IN THE ABDOMEN CAUSED BY SPLENOMEGALY, OR THE ACUTE ONSET OF LEFT UPPER
QUADRANT PAIN DUE TO SPLENIC INFARCTION. THE SPLEEN IS OFTEN GREATLY ENLARGED AS A RESULT OF
EXTENSIVE EXTRAMEDULLARY HEMATOPOIESIS. EXTRAMEDULLARY HEMATOPOIESIS CAN ALSO PRODUCE MILD
HEPATOMEGALY AND LYMPHADENOPATHY.
2069
PERIPHERAL BLOOD:
- LEUKOCYTOSIS WITH LEUKOCYTE COUNT, OFTEN EXCEEDING 100,000 CELLS/MM3, WHICH CONSISTS
PREDOMINANTLY OF NEUTROPHILS, BAND FORMS, METAMYELOCYTES, MYELOCYTES, EOSINOPHILS, AND
BASOPHILS.
- BLASTS ARE USUALLY LESS THAN 10% OF THE CIRCULATING CELLS.
- PLATELET COUNT IS USUALLY INCREASED
BONE MARROW:
- MARKEDLY HYPERCELLULAR MARROW BECAUSE OF MASSIVELY INCREASED NUMBERS OF MATURING
GRANULOCYTIC PRECURSORS. THERE IS USUALLY AN ELEVATED PROPORTION OF EOSINOPHILS AND BASOPHILS.
- THERE IS ALSO AN INCREASE IN MEGAKARYOCYTES AND USUALLY INCLUDE SMALL, DYSPLASTIC FORMS AND
ERYTHROID PROGENITORS ARE PRESENT IN NORMAL OR MILDLY DECREASED NUMBERS. TYPICALLY THERE IS AN
INCREASED RETICULIN DEPOSITION, BUT OVERT MARROW FIBROSIS IS RARE EARLY IN THE COURSE.
- SEA-BLUE HISTIOCYTES - THESE ARE SCATTERED MACROPHAGES WITH ABUNDANT WRINKLED,GREEN-BLUE
CYTOPLASM.
OTHER OPTIONS:
IMMUNOPHENOTYPING AND FLOW CYTOMETRY: FLOW CYTOMETRY REFERS TO THE MEASUREMENT OF CELLULAR
ANTIGENS AS THEY FLOW IN A FLUID STREAM. IMMUNOPHENOTYPING IS EMPLOYED USING LABELED ANTIBODIES
AGAINST SPECIFIC EPITOPES OF CELLULAR ANTIGENS. THE TECHNIQUE THAT IS USUALLY USED IN
IMMUNOPHENOTYPING IS FLOW CYTOMETRY. IT HAS A LIMITED ROLE IN THE DIAGNOSIS OF CML. IT IS MAINLY
USED IN IDENTIFYING CML BLAST TRANSFORMATION.
LAP SCORE: LEUCOCYTE ALKALINE PHOSPHATASE(LAP) SCORE IS DECREASED IN CASES OF CML. IT IS ONLY
A FIRST-LINE TEST IN THE DIAGNOSIS OF CML AND THE DIAGNOSIS NEEDS TO BE CONFIRMED BY OTHER TESTS
INCLUDING BONE MARROW BIOPSY, MOLECULAR DIAGNOSTICS, AND CYTOGENETIC ANALYSIS.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt:
A GIRL PRESENTS WITH SHORT STATURE, WEBBED NECK, THICK CALVES, SHIELD-SHAPED CHEST, SWELLING OF
THE ANKLE, AND INCREASED CARRYING ANGLE. WHAT IS THE LIKELY DIAGNOSIS?
questions.explanation:
THE CLINICAL PRESENTATION OF SHORT STATURE, WEBBED NECK, THICK CALVES, SHIELD-SHAPED CHEST, SWELLING
OF THE ANKLE, AND INCREASED CARRYING ANGLE IS SUGGESTIVE OF TURNER SYNDROME.
TURNER SYNDROME OCCURS DUE TO COMPLETE OR PARTIAL MONOSOMY OF X-CHROMOSOMES. IT PRODUCES
HYPOGONADISM IN PHENOTYPIC FEMALES. IT IS THE MOST COMMON SEX CHROMOSOME ABNORMALITY IN
FEMALES.
IMPORTANT FEATURES ASSOCIATED WITH TURNER'S SYNDROME:
- SHORT STATURE
- WEBBING OF NECK
- BROAD CHEST AND WIDELY SPACED NIPPLES
- CUBITUS VALGUS
- STREAK OVARIES, INFERTILITY, AMENORRHEA
- PERIPHERAL LYMPHEDEMA AT BIRTH
2070
- LOW POSTERIOR HAIRLINE
- POOR BREAST DEVELOPMENT
- PIGMENTED NEVI
- CARDIAC MANIFESTATIONS – COARCTATION OF AORTA, BICUSPID AORTIC VALVE
- HORSE SHOE KIDNEY
IMAGE SHOWING THE FEATURES OF TURNER SYNDROME
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION B: IMPORTANT FEATURES ASSOCIATED WITH DOWN’S SYNDROME (TRISOMY 21) INCLUDE
- INTELLECTUAL DISABILITY
- CONGENITAL HEART DEFECTS
- EPICANTHIC FOLDS AND FLAT FACIAL PROFILE
- SIMIAN CREASE
- UMBILICAL HERNIAS
- PREDISPOSITION TO LEUKEMIA
OPTION C: IMPORTANT FEATURES ASSOCIATED WITH PATAU SYNDROME (TRISOMY 13):
- MICROPHTHALMIA
- MICROCEPHALY AND INTELLECTUAL DISABILITY
- CLEFT LIP AND PALATE
- ROCKER-BOTTOM FEET
- CARDIAC AND RENAL DEFECTS
OPTION D: IMPORTANT FEATURES ASSOCIATED WITH EDWARD SYNDROME (TRISOMY 18):
- PROMINENT OCCIPUT, MICROGNATHIA, LOW SET EARS
2071
- INTELLECTUAL DISABILITY
- RENAL AND CARDIAC MALFORMATIONS
- LIMITED HIP ABDUCTION, ROCKER-BOTTOM FEET

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt:
A PATIENT WITH OCCUPATIONAL EXPOSURE TO BENZENE PRESENTS WITH REPEATED INFECTIONS, EASY
FATIGABILITY, WEIGHT LOSS, AND EVENING RISE OF TEMPERATURE. THIS OCCUPATIONAL EXPOSURE WILL
PREDISPOSE HIM TO WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING CANCERS?
questions.explanation:
OCCUPATIONAL EXPOSURE TO BENZENE PREDISPOSES TO LEUKEMIA. THE GIVEN CLINICAL HISTORY OF REPEATED
INFECTIONS, EASY FATIGABILITY, WEIGHT LOSS, AND EVENING RISE OF TEMPERATURE WITH BENZENE EXPOSURE
POINTS TOWARDS A DIAGNOSIS OF LEUKEMIA.
BENZENE IS OXIDIZED TO AN EPOXIDE THROUGH HEPATIC CYP2E1. THE EPOXIDE AND OTHER METABOLITES
DISRUPT PROGENITOR CELL DIFFERENTIATION IN THE BONE MARROW AND LEAD TO MARROW APLASIA AND ACUTE
MYELOID LEUKEMIA.
ACUTE MYELOID LEUKEMIA IS A TUMOR OF HEMATOPOIETIC PROGENITORS CAUSED BY ACQUIRED ONCOGENIC
MUTATIONS THAT IMPEDE DIFFERENTIATION. THIS LEADS TO THE ACCUMULATION OF IMMATURE MYELOID BLASTS
IN THE MARROW. THE REPLACEMENT OF THE MARROW WITH BLASTS PRODUCES MARROW FAILURE
AND COMPLICATIONS RELATED TO ANEMIA, THROMBOCYTOPENIA, AND NEUTROPENIA.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION B: EXPOSURE TO ARSENIC AND ITS COMPOUNDS, ASBESTOS, BERYLLIUM AND ITS COMPOUNDS,
CHROMIUM COMPOUNDS, NICKEL COMPOUNDS, RADON, AND ITS DECAY PRODUCTS CAN CAUSE LUNG CANCER.
OPTION C: EXPOSURE TO ARYL AMINES, PARTICULARLY 2-NAPHTHYLAMINE AND RELATED COMPOUNDS,
CYCLOPHOSPHAMIDE, CIGARETTE SMOKING, IRRADIATION CAN CAUSE BLADDER CANCER.
OPTION D: EXPOSURE TO UV RAYS, ARSENIC, AND ITS COMPOUNDS CAN CAUSE SKIN CANCER.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt: IN IRON DEFICIENCY ANEMIA, ALL OF THE FOLLOWING IS INCREASED EXCEPT
questions.explanation:
TRANSFERRIN SATURATION IS DECREASED IN IRON DEFICIENCY ANEMIA.
CLINICAL PRESENTATION MAY INCLUDE FATIGUE, PALLOR, REDUCED EXERCISE CAPACITY. CHEILOSIS (FISSURES AT
THE CORNERS OF THE MOUTH) AND KOILONYCHIA (SPOONING OF THE FINGERNAILS) ARE SIGNS OF ADVANCED
TISSUE IRON DEFICIENCY.
LABORATORY FINDINGS ARE:
- REDUCED HEMOGLOBIN AND HEMATOCRIT VALUES.
- HYPOCHROMIA, MICROCYTOSIS, AND POIKILOCYTOSIS.
- SERUM IRON AND FERRITIN LEVELS ARE LOW.
- THE TOTAL PLASMA IRON-BINDING CAPACITY THAT REFLECTS THE ELEVATED TRANSFERRIN LEVELS IS HIGH.
- LOW SERUM IRON WITH INCREASED IRON-BINDING CAPACITY RESULTS IN A REDUCTION OF TRANSFERRIN
SATURATION TO BELOW 15%.
- RBC PROTOPORPHYRIN LEVELS ARE INCREASED. PROTOPORPHYRIN IS AN INTERMEDIATE IN THE HEME
SYNTHESIS PATHWAY. UNDER CONDITIONS IN WHICH HEME SYNTHESIS IS IMPAIRED, PROTOPORPHYRIN
2072
ACCUMULATES WITHIN THE RED CELL.
- BONE MARROW REVEALS A MILD TO MODERATE INCREASE IN ERYTHROID PROGENITORS. THE ABSENCE OF
STAINABLE IRON IN MACROPHAGES IS A DIAGNOSTICALLY SIGNIFICANT FINDING.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING IS A POOR PROGNOSTIC MARKER OF MULTIPLE MYELOMA?
questions.explanation:
β-2 MICROGLOBULIN IS A POOR PROGNOSTIC MARKER OF MULTIPLE MYELOMA.
MULTIPLE MYELOMA IS A PLASMA CELL NEOPLASM COMMONLY ASSOCIATED WITH LYTIC BONE LESIONS,
HYPERCALCEMIA, RENAL FAILURE, AND ACQUIRED IMMUNE ABNORMALITIES.
POOR PROGNOSTIC FACTORS FOR MULTIPLE MYELOMA:
- SERUM β2-MICROGLOBULIN. IT IS THE SINGLE MOST POWERFUL PREDICTOR
2073
- DELETION OF 17PITP53 SEQUENCES AND THE TRANSLOCATIONS T(14;16) AND T(14;20)
- POLYCLONAL SERUM IMMUNOGLOBULINS
- ELEVATED LACTATE DEHYDROGENASE
- HIGH C-REACTIVE PROTEIN
- INCREASED PLASMA CELL PROLIFERATIVE ACTIVITY
- HIGH DEGREE OF BONE MARROW REPLACEMENT
- PRESENCE OF PLASMABLASTIC MORPHOLOGY
- ELEVATED SERUM SOLUBLE RECEPTOR FOR IL6
MULTIPLE MYELOMA USUALLY PRESENTS AS DESTRUCTIVE PLASMA CELL TUMORS INVOLVING THE AXIAL SKELETON.
THE BONES MOST COMMONLY AFFECTED IN DESCENDING ORDER OF FREQUENCY ARE THE VERTEBRAL COLUMN,
RIBS, SKULL, PELVIS, FEMUR, CLAVICLE, AND SCAPULA.
RADIOGRAPHICALLY, BONE LESIONS APPEAR AS PUNCHED-OUT DEFECTS, USUALLY 1 TO 4 CM IN DIAMETER,
AND CONSIST OF SOFT, GELATINOUS, RED TUMOR MASSES.
RADIOGRAPH OF THE SKULL SHOWING PUNCHED OUT LESIONS:
MORPHOLOGY:
- MALIGNANT PLASMA CELLS HAVE A PERINUCLEAR CLEARING DUE TO A PROMINENT GOLGI APPARATUS AND AN
ECCENTRICALLY PLACED NUCLEUS.
- RELATIVELY NORMAL-APPEARING PLASMA CELLS, PLASMABLASTS WITH VESICULAR NUCLEAR CHROMATIN AND A
PROMINENT SINGLE NUCLEOLUS, OR BIZARRE, MULTINUCLEATED CELLS MAY PREDOMINATE.
- OTHER CYTOLOGIC VARIANTS INCLUDE FLAME CELLS, MOTT CELLS.
- FLAME CELLS HAVE FIERY RED CYTOPLASM, MOTT CELLS CONTAIN MULTIPLE GRAPELIKE CYTOPLASMIC
DROPLETS, A VARIETY OF OTHER INCLUSIONS, INCLUDING FIBRILS, CRYSTALLINE RODS, AND GLOBULES. THE
GLOBULAR INCLUSIONS ARE REFERRED TO AS RUSSELL BODIES (IF CYTOPLASMIC) OR DUTCHER BODIES (IF NUCLEAR).
- ROULEAUX FORMATION IS CHARACTERISTIC BUT NOT SPECIFIC. HIGH LEVELS OF M PROTEIN IN THE BLOOD
CAUSES RED CELLS TO STICK TO ONE ANOTHER IN LINEAR ARRAYS IN SMEARS LEADING TO ROULEAUX FORMATION.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt:
A PAP SMEAR TAKEN FROM A PATIENT REVEALED HYPERCHROMATIC NUCLEI, IRREGULAR NUCLEAR BORDERS,
AND LOW MATURATION INDEX INVOLVING THE WHOLE THICKNESS BUT DID NOT BREACH THE BASEMENT
MEMBRANE. WHAT IS THE DIAGNOSIS?
questions.explanation:
THE HYPERCHROMATIC NUCLEI, IRREGULAR NUCLEAR BORDERS, AND INTACT BASEMENT MEMBRANE ARE ALL
SUGGESTIVE OF DYSPLASIA.
DYSPLASIA IS CHARACTERIZED BY THE LOSS IN THE UNIFORMITY OF THE INDIVIDUAL CELLS AND THEIR
ARCHITECTURAL ORIENTATION. THE FEATURES OF DYSPLASIA INCLUDE:
- PLEOMORPHISM
- HYPERCHROMATIC NUCLEI
- HIGH NUCLEAR-TO-CYTOPLASMIC RATIO
- INCREASED MITOTIC FIGURES
WHEN THE DYSPLASTIC CHANGES INVOLVE THE ENTIRE THICKNESS OF THE EPITHELIUM WITHOUT BREACHING THE
BASEMENT MEMBRANE IT IS CONSIDERED PREINVASIVE AND IS TERMED CARCINOMA-IN-SITU. IF THE TUMOR
INVADES THE BASEMENT MEMBRANE IT IS SAID TO BE INVASIVE.
DYSPLASIA CAN BE CONSIDERED AS A PRECURSOR TO MALIGNANT BUT IT DOES NOT ALWAYS PROGRESS TO CANCER.
DYSPLASIA USUALLY OCCURS IN THE METAPLASTIC EPITHELIUM BUT ALL METAPLASTIC EPITHELIUM IS NOT
DYSPLASTIC.
OTHER OPTIONS:
2076
METAPLASIA: IT REFERS TO THE REPLACEMENT OF ONE CELL TYPE WITH ANOTHER TYPE. IT IS ALMOST ALWAYS
ASSOCIATED WITH TISSUE DAMAGE, REPAIR, AND REGENERATION. THE MOST COMMON EPITHELIAL METAPLASIA
IS COLUMNAR TO SQUAMOUS.
CARCINOMA: IN CARCINOMA, THERE IS THE INVASION OF THE BASEMENT MEMBRANE.
HYPERPLASIA: IT REFERS TO THE INCREASE IN THE NUMBER OF CELLS IN A TISSUE OR ORGAN. IT CAN BE
PHYSIOLOGIC OR PATHOLOGICAL. ENLARGEMENT OF THE FEMALE BREAST DURING PREGNANCY IS PHYSIOLOGIC
HYPERPLASIA. ENDOMETRIAL HYPERPLASIA IS AN EXAMPLE OF PATHOLOGICAL HYPERPLASIA.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt:
THE MOTHER OF A 12-YEAR-OLD GIRL WAS WORRIED THAT HER DAUGHTER IS SHORTER WHEN COMPARED
WITH HER CLASSMATES. ON EXAMINATION, THE CHILD HAD A WEBBED NECK, LOW HAIRLINE, AND SHIELD
CHEST. A PROVISIONAL DIAGNOSIS OF TURNER'S SYNDROME WAS MADE. WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING IS A
LIKELY FINDING TO BE SEEN IN THIS PATIENT?
questions.explanation:
THE LIKELY FINDING SEEN IN A PATIENT WITH TURNER SYNDROME IS BILATERAL SMALL STREAK OVARIES.
TURNER SYNDROME RESULTS FROM COMPLETE OR PARTIAL MONOSOMY OF THE X CHROMOSOME. IT IS
CHARACTERIZED BY HYPOGONADISM IN PHENOTYPIC FEMALES. IT IS THE MOST COMMON SEX CHROMOSOME
ABNORMALITY IN FEMALES. THREE TYPES OF KARYOTYPIC ABNORMALITIES ARE SEEN
- MISSING AN ENTIRE X CHROMOSOME - THIS RESULTS IN A 45X KARYOTYPE.
- STRUCTURAL ABNORMALITIES OF THE X CHROMOSOMES - ISOCHROMOSOME OF THE LONG ARM AND LOSS OF THE
SHORT ARM, 46X,I(X)(Q10), DELETION OF PORTIONS OF BOTH LONG AND SHORT ARMS THAT LEAD TO
THE FORMATION OF A RING CHROMOSOME, 46X,R(X), DELETION OF PORTIONS OF THE SHORT OR LONG ARM,
46X,DEL(XQ) OR 46X,DEL(XP).
- MOSAICS - THEY WILL HAVE 45X ALONG WITH ONE OR MORE KARYOTYPICALLY NORMAL OR ABNORMAL CELL
TYPES. EXAMPLES ARE 45X/46XX, 45X/46XY, 45X/47XXX, 45X/46X,I(X)(Q10).
IMPORTANT FEATURES ASSOCIATED WITH TURNER'S SYNDROME:
- SHORT STATURE
- WEBBING OF NECK
- BROAD CHEST AND WIDELY SPACED NIPPLES
- CUBITUS VALGUS
- STREAK OVARIES
- INFERTILITY, AMENORRHEA
- PERIPHERAL LYMPHEDEMA AT BIRTH
- LOW POSTERIOR HAIRLINE
- BROAD CHEST AND WIDELY SPACED NIPPLES
- PIGMENTED NEVI
- COARCTATION OF AORTA
THERE IS FAILURE TO DEVELOP NORMAL SECONDARY SEX CHARACTERISTICS AT PUBERTY. THE GENITALIA
REMAIN INFANTILE, BREAST DEVELOPMENT IS INADEQUATE, AND THERE IS LITTLE PUBIC HAIR. SHORT STATURE
AND AMENORRHEA ARE OF PARTICULAR IMPORTANCE IN ESTABLISHING THE DIAGNOSIS IN AN ADULT.
OTHER OPTIONS:
2077
AORTIC DISSECTION, SUBLUXATION OF LENS, AND MITRAL VALVE PROLAPSE ARE SEEN IN MARFAN SYNDROME.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt:
AN 18-YEAR-OLD MALE PRESENTED TO THE OUTPATIENT DEPARTMENT WITH GUM BLEEDING AND FEVER FOR
THE PAST 2 MONTHS. GENERAL EXAMINATION SHOWED PALLOR AND THE SYSTEMIC EXAMINATION WAS
UNREMARKABLE. LABORATORY EXAMINATION REVEALED HB LEVEL- 3 GM/DL, TLC- 1500/MICROL,
PLATELET COUNT- 15000/MICROL. PERIPHERAL SMEAR SHOWS MACROCYTES AND THE RETICULOCYTE COUNT
IS 0.5. BONE MARROW EXAMINATION REVEALED FATTY STREAKS AND ABSENT MEGAKARYOCYTES BUT NO
IMMATURE CELLS. WHAT IS THE LIKELY DIAGNOSIS?
questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN CLINICAL SCENARIO SHOWING A YOUNG MALE WITH GUM BLEEDING, FEVER, PANCYTOPENIA, AND A
LOW RETICULOCYTE COUNT WITH BONE MARROW SHOWING FATTY STREAKS AND NO IMMATURE CELLS IS
SUGGESTIVE OF IDIOPATHIC ACQUIRED APLASTIC ANEMIA.
APLASTIC ANEMIA IS A SYNDROME CHARACTERIZED BY CHRONIC HEMATOPOIETIC FAILURE AND PANCYTOPENIA.
THE COMMON CAUSES INCLUDE:
- ACQUIRED
- IDIOPATHIC (MOST COMMON CAUSE, ABOUT 65% OF THE CASES)
- ACQUIRED STEM-CELL DEFECTS
- IMMUNE-MEDIATED
- CHEMICAL AGENTS
- DOSE-RELATED (ALKYLATING AGENTS, ANTIMETABOLITES, BENZENE, CHLORAMPHENICOL, INORGANIC ARSENALS)
- IDIOSYNCRATIC (CHLORAMPHENICOL, PHENYLBUTAZONE, ORGANIC ARSENICALS, CARBAMAZEPINE,
PENICILLAMINE, GOLD SALTS)
- PHYSICAL AGENTS
- WHOLE-BODY IRRADIATION
- VIRAL INFECTIONS (HEPATITIS, CYTOMEGALOVIRUS, EPSTEIN–BARR VIRUS, VARICELLA-ZOSTER VIRUS)
- INHERITED
- FANCONI ANEMIA
- TELOMERASE DEFECTS
2078
PATHOGENESIS INVOLVES AN EXTRINSIC IMMUNE-MEDIATED SUPPRESSION OF BONE MARROW AND AN
INTRINSIC ABNORMALITY OF THE STEM CELLS.
CLINICAL FEATURES AND DIAGNOSIS:
THERE IS NO AGE OR SEX PREDISPOSITION FOR APLASTIC ANEMIA. IT PRESENTS INSIDIOUSLY WITH FEATURES OF
PANCYTOPENIA SUCH AS PALLOR, PETECHIAE, AND ECCHYMOSIS. RECURRENT INFECTIONS AND FEVER OCCUR AS A
RESULT OF NEUTROPENIA. RETICULOCYTOPENIA IS SEEN AND SPLENOMEGALY IS CHARACTERISTICALLY ABSENT.
BONE MARROW BIOPSY IS USED FOR DIAGNOSIS.
HISTOLOGY:
BONE MARROW ASPIRATE USUALLY RESULTS IN A DRY TAP. EXAMINATION SHOWS A HYPOCELLULAR MARROW
DEVOID OF HEMATOPOIETIC CELLS WITH REMNANT FAT CELLS, FIBROUS STROMA, AND SCATTERED LYMPHOCYTES.
RED CELLS ARE USUALLY SLIGHTLY MACROCYTIC AND NORMOCHROMIC. THE FOLLOWING IMAGE SHOWS A
HYPOCELLULAR BONE MARROW WITH LITTLE HEMATOPOIESIS AND SEVERAL FAT CELLS.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION B - PAROXYSMAL NOCTURNAL HEMOGLOBINURIA (PNH) IS AN ACQUIRED DISORDER RESULTING FROM
THE MUTATION IN THE PHOSPHATIDYLINOSITOL GLYCAN COMPLEMENTATION GROUP A GENE (PIGA), AN
ENZYME THAT IS ESSENTIAL FOR THE SYNTHESIS OF MEMBRANE-ASSOCIATED COMPLEMENT REGULATORY
PROTEINS. RED CELLS DEFICIENT IN THESE PROTEINS ARE SUSCEPTIBLE TO INTRAVASCULAR HEMOLYSIS. PATIENTS
WITH PNH USUALLY PRESENT WITH PANCYTOPENIA AND RETICULOCYTOSIS WITH BONE MARROW BIOPSY
SHOWING A CELLULAR MARROW WITH MARKED TO MASSIVE ERYTHROID HYPERPLASIA.
OPTION C - MYELODYSPLASTIC SYNDROMES (MDS) ARE A GROUP OF CLONAL STEM CELL DISORDERS. IT IS A
CONSEQUENCE OF MATURATION DEFECTS THAT RESULT IN INEFFECTIVE HEMATOPOIESIS WITH A HIGH
PREDISPOSITION TO CONVERSION TO AML. THEY ARE CHARACTERIZED BY A HYPERCELLULAR MARROW WITH
DYSPLASTIC CELLS ON BONE MARROW ASPIRATE. MARROW CHANGES SEEN IN MDS ARE GIVEN IN THE PEARL
BELOW.
OPTION D - PULMONARY TUBERCULOSIS (TB) IS CAUSED BY MYCOBACTERIUM TUBERCULOSIS AND PATIENTS
OFTEN PRESENT WITH FEVER, PRODUCTIVE COUGH, BLOOD-STREAKED SPUTUM, NIGHT SWEATS, MALAISE, LOSS OF
APPETITE, AND WEIGHT LOSS.
2079

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt:
A CHILD IS PRESENTING WITH PALPABLE BLANCHING PURPURA, ABDOMINAL PAIN, AND PAIN IN THE KNEE
JOINT RESULTING FROM ARTHRITIS. URINE EXAMINATION SHOWED HEMATURIA AND PROTEINURIA. WHAT IS
THE MOST LIKELY DIAGNOSIS?
questions.explanation:
THE CLINICAL PRESENTATION AND THE INVESTIGATIONS ARE SUGGESTIVE OF HENOCH-SCHONLEIN PURPURA.
HENOCH-SCHöNLEIN PURPURA IS A SYSTEMIC IMMUNE DISORDER CHARACTERIZED BY A PURPURIC RASH,
ABDOMINAL PAIN, POLYARTHRALGIA, AND RENAL ABNORMALITIES. IT IS MOST COMMONLY SEEN IN THE AGE
GROUP OF 3-8 YEARS. THE PATIENT MAY PRESENT WITH THE FOLLOWING CLINICAL FEATURES:
- SKIN LESIONS- CHARACTERISTICALLY INVOLVE THE EXTENSOR SURFACES OF ARMS AND LEGS, AND ALSO THE
BUTTOCKS
- ABDOMINAL MANIFESTATIONS- INCLUDE PAIN, VOMITING, AND INTESTINAL BLEEDING.
- RENAL MANIFESTATIONS- INCLUDE GROSS OR MICROSCOPIC HEMATURIA, NEPHRITIC SYNDROME, OR NEPHROTIC
SYNDROME. RENAL MANIFESTATIONS ARE MORE SEVERE IN ADULTS. A RAPIDLY PROGRESSIVE FORM OF
GLOMERULONEPHRITIS IS SEEN IN SOME CASES.
THIS CONDITION USUALLY OCCURS FOLLOWING AN UPPER RESPIRATORY TRACT INFECTION AND THERE IS A HISTORY
OF ATOPY IN ONE-THIRD OF THE CASES. IGA IS DEPOSITED IN THE GLOMERULAR MESANGIUM IN A DISTRIBUTION
SIMILAR TO THAT OF IGA NEPHROPATHY.
MICROSCOPIC FINDINGS:
- IGA DEPOSITION IN THE MESANGIAL REGION. SOMETIMES THERE IS THE DEPOSITION OF IGG AND C3 ALONG
WITH IGA.
- RENAL LESIONS SHOW FOCAL OR DIFFUSE MESANGIAL PROLIFERATION, AND/OR ENDOCAPILLARY PROLIFERATION TO
CRESCENTIC GLOMERULONEPHRITIS.
- SKIN LESIONS SHOW SUBEPIDERMAL HEMORRHAGES AND NECROTIZING VASCULITIS OF SMALL VESSELS.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION A: IMMUNE THROMBOCYTOPENIC PURPURA(ITP): IT OCCURS DUE TO ANTIBODY-MEDIATED
DESTRUCTION OF PLATELETS. IT CAN BE ACUTE OR CHRONIC. ACUTE ITP IS USUALLY SELF-LIMITING IN NATURE.
CUTANEOUS BLEEDING CAN BE IN THE FORM OF PETECHIAE AND ECCHYMOSES. THE PATIENT CAN ALSO HAVE
HEMATURIA, MELENA, OR EXCESSIVE MENSTRUAL FLOW.
OPTION B: DENGUE: IT IS A VIRAL ILLNESS CAUSED BY THE DENGUE VIRUS. THE CLINICAL MANIFESTATIONS
INCLUDE FEVER, HEADACHE, MUSCULOSKELETAL PAIN, AND RASH. THE RASH WHICH IS MACULOPAPULAR IN
NATURE BEGINS ON THE TRUNK AND THEN SPREADS CENTRIFUGALLY TO THE FACE AND EXTREMITIES.
OPTION C: CHURG- STRAUSS SYNDROME (EOSINOPHILIC GRANULOMATOSIS WITH POLYANGIITIS): IT IS
CHARACTERIZED BY EOSINOPHILIC VASCULITIS OF MULTIPLE ORGANS. THE FEATURES OF THIS CONDITION
INCLUDE ASTHMA, PERIPHERAL EOSINOPHILIA, PULMONARY INFILTRATES, NEUROPATHY, PARANASAL SINUS
ABNORMALITY, AND THE PRESENCE OF EOSINOPHILIC VASCULITIS.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt:
A 54-YEAR-OLD PATIENT PRESENTS TO THE OUTPATIENT DEPARTMENT WITH FATIGUE, TIREDNESS AND
CERVICAL LYMPHADENOPATHY. THE TLC AND DLC WERE NORMAL. NO IMMATURE CELLS. A LYMPH NODE
BIOPSY WAS PERFORMED WHICH SHOWS DIFFUSE EFFACEMENT OF THE LYMPH NODE ARCHITECTURE, CELLS
WITH AN INDENTED NUCLEUS, PROMINENT NUCLEOLUS, AND ARE ATYPICAL. CD10 AND BCL2 ARE
POSITIVE. WHAT IS THE LIKELY DIAGNOSIS?
questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN CLINICAL SCENARIO SHOWING FATIGUE, TIREDNESS AND CERVICAL LYMPHADENOPATHY WITH CD10
POSITIVE BCL2 POSITIVE CELLS IS HIGHLY SUGGESTIVE OF FOLLICULAR LYMPHOMA.
2080
FOLLICULAR LYMPHOMA PRESENTS AT MIDDLE AGE WITH NO SEX PREDILECTION. THE MOST COMMON
PRESENTING SYMPTOM IS PAINLESS GENERALIZED LYMPHADENOPATHY. A LYMPH NODE BIOPSY IS ADEQUATE
FOR THE DIAGNOSIS OF FOLLICULAR LYMPHOMA. IMMUNOPHENOTYPING OF THE CELLS SHOWING CD19, CD20,
CD10, BCL2 POSITIVE, AND CD5 NEGATIVE IS SUGGESTIVE THAT THE CELLS ORIGINATE FROM THE GERMINAL
CENTRE.
THE MAJORITY OF FOLLICULAR LYMPHOMAS HAVE CHARACTERISTIC (14;18) TRANSLOCATION. THIS JUXTAPOSES THE
IGH LOCUS ON CHROMOSOME 14 AND THE BCL2 LOCUS ON CHROMOSOME 18. THIS CHROMOSOMAL
REARRANGEMENT RESULTS IN THE OVEREXPRESSION OF BCL2 PROTEIN, WHICH IS AN INHIBITOR OF APOPTOSIS
THAT CONTRIBUTES TO LYMPHOMA CELL SURVIVAL.
HISTOPATHOLOGY:
LYMPH NODES EXHIBIT A NODULAR OR NODULAR AND DIFFUSE GROWTH PATTERN. TWO CELL TYPES ARE
PREDOMINANTLY PRESENT IN VARYING PROPORTIONS:
- CENTROCYTES (SMALL CLEAVED CELLS) - SMALL CELLS WITH A CLEAVED NUCLEUS AND SCANT CYTOPLASM
- CENTROBLASTS - LARGE CELLS WITH OPEN NUCLEAR CHROMATIN, SEVERAL NUCLEOLI, AND MODEST AMOUNTS OF
CYTOPLASM
IN MOST CASES, THERE IS A MAJORITY OF CENTROCYTES.
THE PERIPHERAL BLOOD SMEAR SHOWS LYMPHOCYTOSIS AND BONE MARROW TAP REVEALS PARATRABECULAR
LYMPHOID AGGREGATES.
THE FOLLOWING IMAGE SHOWS A LYMPH NODE BIOPSY IN FOLLICULAR LYMPHOMA:
OTHER OPTIONS -
OPTION B - BURKITT LYMPHOMA IS AN AGGRESSIVE TYPE OF NON-HODGKIN LYMPHOMA (NHL). IT IS ALSO
KNOWN AS SMALL NON-CLEAVED-CELL LYMPHOMA AND IS CHARACTERIZED BY THE TRANSLOCATION AND
DEREGULATION OF THE C-MYC GENE ON CHROMOSOME 8 TO CHROMOSOME 14 OR 22 - T(8:14) OR
T(8:22). HISTOPATHOLOGY OF THE TUMOR REVEALS A STARRY SKY APPEARANCE CREATED BY APOPTOTIC CELLS AND
MACROPHAGES CONTAINING CLEAR CYTOPLASM.
OPTION C - MYCOSIS FUNGOIDES IS THE MOST COMMON TYPE OF CUTANEOUS T-CELL LYMPHOMA. THE
HISTOLOGICAL HALLMARK OF CUTANEOUS T-CELL LYMPHOMA (MYCOSIS FUNGOIDES TYPE) IS THE PRESENCE
2081
OF PAUTRIER MICROABSCESS. THE PRESENCE OF B-CELL MARKERS IN THE QUESTION RULES OUT THE DIFFERENTIAL
OF MYCOSIS FUNGOIDES.
OPTION D - CHRONIC MYELOID LEUKEMIA (CML) IS A MYELOPROLIFERATIVE NEOPLASM CHARACTERIZED BY
THE PRESENCE OF CHIMERIC BCR-ABL GENE WHICH IS A RESULT OF A RECIPROCAL (9;22)(Q34;Q11)
TRANSLOCATION (PHILADELPHIA CHROMOSOME). THE PRESENCE OF LYMPHADENOPATHY IN THE GIVEN SCENARIO
RULES OUT THE POSSIBILITY OF CML AS IT IS A MYELOID DISORDER.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt:
A SOFTWARE ENGINEER PRESENTS TO THE OUTPATIENT DEPARTMENT WITH EASY FATIGUABILITY. HE GIVES A
HISTORY OF SITTING IN FRONT OF THE COMPUTER FOR 12 - 14 HOURS. HE CONSUMES A LOT OF JUNK FOOD
WITH VERY LESS FRUITS AND VEGETABLES. HB IS 9GM/DL AND MCV 120 FL. WHAT IS THE MOST LIKELY
CAUSE OF THIS PATIENT'S ANEMIA?
questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN LABORATORY VALUES SHOWING ANEMIA AND INCREASED MCV ARE SUGGESTIVE OF MEGALOBLASTIC
ANEMIA. THIS COULD BE DUE TO CYANOCOBALAMIN DEFICIENCY OR FOLIC ACID DEFICIENCY. THE HISTORY OF
INADEQUATE INTAKE OF FRUITS AND VEGETABLES POINTS TOWARDS FOLIC ACID DEFICIENCY.
DIETARY SOURCES OF VIT-B12 ARE ANIMAL PRODUCTS SUCH AS MEAT, FISH, MILK, AND EGGS. DIETARY SOURCES
OF FOLIC ACID ARE GREEN VEGETABLES SUCH AS LETTUCE, SPINACH, ASPARAGUS, AND BROCCOLI.
MEGALOBLASTIC ANEMIA CAN OCCUR DUE TO VIT-B12 OR FOLIC ACID DEFICIENCY. INADEQUATE INTAKE,
INTRINSIC FACTOR DEFICIENCY, PERNICIOUS ANEMIA, GASTRECTOMY, MALABSORPTION, ILEAL
RESECTION, ALCOHOLISM, ANTICONVULSANTS, ORAL CONTRACEPTIVES, PREGNANCY, INFANCY, DISSEMINATED
CANCER, MARKEDLY INCREASED HEMATOPOIESIS, FOLIC ACID ANTAGONISTS ARE SOME OF THE CAUSES.
PATIENT CAN PRESENT WITH ANOREXIA, WEIGHT LOSS, DIARRHEA, CONSTIPATION, GLOSSITIS, ANGULAR
CHEILOSIS, REVERSIBLE MELANIN SKIN HYPERPIGMENTATION, PARESTHESIAS, MUSCLE WEAKNESS, DEMENTIA,
OR PSYCHOTIC DISTURBANCES.
IN MEGALOBLASTIC ANEMIA, DNA SYNTHESIS IS IMPAIRED THAT LEADING TO INEFFECTIVE HEMATOPOIESIS AND
DISTINCTIVE MORPHOLOGIC CHANGES.
PERIPHERAL BLOOD EXAMINATION SHOWS OVAL MACROCYTES, USUALLY WITH ANISOCYTOSIS AND POIKILOCYTOSIS.
MCV IS USUALLY >100 FL. THE NORMAL VALUE OF MCV IS BETWEEN 80-100 FL. MOST MACROCYTES LACK
THE CENTRAL PALLOR OF NORMAL RED CELLS AND EVEN APPEAR HYPERCHROMIC, BUT THE MCHC IS NOT
ELEVATED. THE RETICULOCYTE COUNT IS LOW. NEUTROPHILS ARE LARGER THAN NORMAL AND SHOW NUCLEAR
HYPERSEGMENTATION WITH FIVE OR MORE NUCLEAR LOBULES.
MARROW IS MARKEDLY HYPERCELLULAR. MEGALOBLASTIC CHANGES ARE SEEN AT ALL STAGES OF ERYTHROID
DEVELOPMENT. THERE IS NUCLEAR-TO-CYTOPLASMIC ASYNCHRONY, WHERE NUCLEAR MATURATION IS SLOWER
THAN CYTOPLASMIC MATURATION. GRANULOCYTIC PRECURSORS ARE SEEN IN THE FORM OF GIANT
METAMYELOCYTES AND BAND FORMS. MEGAKARYOCYTES MAY BE ABNORMALLY LARGE WITH BIZARRE,
MULTILOBATE NUCLEI.
PERIPHERAL BLOOD SMEAR SHOWING HYPERSEGMENTED NEUTROPHIL:
2082
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION A - IN CYANOCOBALAMIN DEFICIENCY, MCV WILL BE INCREASED. BUT THE DIETARY SOURCES
OF CYANOCOBALAMIN ARE MAINLY OF ANIMAL PRODUCTS. IN THE GIVEN CLINICAL SCENARIO THERE
IS INADEQUATE INTAKE OF FRUITS AND VEGETABLES. HENCE, THIS IS NOT THE ANSWER.
OPTION C - IN IRON DEFICIENCY ANEMIA, MCV WILL BE DECREASED.
OPTION D - IN HEREDITARY SPHEROCYTOSIS, MCV WILL BE NORMAL.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt:
A CHRONIC ALCOHOLIC PATIENT PRESENTED WITH INCREASING ABDOMINAL GIRTH. ON EXAMINATION,
SHIFTING DULLNESS WAS PRESENT AND THE LIVER SPAN WAS LESS THAN 7CM. HISTOPATHOLOGICAL
EXAMINATION REVEALED THE PRESENCE OF INTRACYTOPLASMIC EOSINOPHILIC INCLUSIONS IN HEPATOCYTES.
WHAT IS THE CONTENT OF THESE INCLUSIONS?
questions.explanation:
THE CLINICAL SCENARIO GIVEN HERE DESCRIBES ALCOHOLIC HEPATITIS. IN THIS CONDITION, THERE ARE
INTRACYTOPLASMIC EOSINOPHILIC INCLUSIONS CALLED MALLORY DENK BODIES AND THEY CONTAIN
INTERMEDIATE FILAMENTS.
THE LIVER UNDERGOES INFLAMMATION AND FIBROSIS IN ALCOHOLIC HEPATITIS. THIS LEADS TO INJURED AND
SWOLLEN HEPATOCYTES WITH CLEARED-OUT CYTOPLASM AND CYTOSKELETAL DAMAGE. THESE HEPATOCYTES ARE
CALLED BALLOONED HEPATOCYTES. WHEN THE CYTOSKELETAL DAMAGE IS EXTENSIVE, THERE IS THE FORMATION OF
MALLORY DENK/ MALLORY HYALINE BODIES. THESE ARE REMNANTS OF PARTIALLY DEGRADED INTERMEDIATE
FILAMENTS AND ARE COMPOSED OF KERATIN FILAMENTS.
CYTOSKELETAL PROTEINS INCLUDE INTERMEDIATE FILAMENTS, MICROFILAMENTS (MADE UP OF ACTIN - OPTION
B), AND MICROTUBULES (OPTION - C).
INTERMEDIATE FILAMENTS PROVIDE A FLEXIBLE SCAFFOLD TO ORGANIZE CYTOPLASM AND PREVENT EXTERNAL
FORCES FROM ACTING ON THE CELL. THEY ARE OF FIVE TYPES:
- KERATIN FILAMENTS (EPITHELIAL CELLS)
- NEURO FILAMENTS (NEURONS)
- DESMIN FILAMENTS (MUSCLES)
- VIMENTIN FILAMENTS (CONNECTIVE TISSUES)
2083
- GLIAL FILAMENTS (GLIAL CELLS)
FIBRONECTIN (OPTION D) IS AN ADHESIVE GLYCOPROTEIN. ITS PRESENCE IN CERVICOVAGINAL SECRETIONS BEFORE
RUPTURE OF MEMBRANES IS A POSSIBLE MARKER FOR IMPENDING PRETERM LABOR.
THE GIVEN IMAGE SHOWS INTRACYTOPLASMIC EOSINOPHILIC MALLORY BODIES.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt:
A 65-YEAR-OLD FEMALE PATIENT IS DIAGNOSED WITH PURE RED CELL APLASIA AND A MEDIASTINAL MASS.
WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING CAN BE THE LIKELY CAUSE?
options:
GERM CELL TUMOR
Answer Key

Question No. Correct Option
questions.explanation:
THE MOST PROBABLE DIAGNOSIS FOR THE CLINICAL PRESENTATION OF MEDIASTINAL MASS WITH PURE RED CELL
APLASIA IS THYMOMA.
THYMOMA REFERS TO THE TUMORS OF THE THYMIC EPITHELIAL CELLS. MOST OF THE THYMIC TUMORS OCCUR IN
THE ANTERIOR MEDIASTINUM. CLINICAL FEATURES CAN BE CHEST PAIN, DYSPNEA, COUGH, OR SUPERIOR VENA
CAVA SYNDROME.
IT IS ASSOCIATED WITH PARANEOPLASTIC SYNDROMES LIKE MYASTHENIA GRAVIS, PURE RED CELL APLASIA, OR
HYPOGAMMAGLOBULINEMIA. IT IS RARELY ASSOCIATED WITH LIMBIC ENCEPHALITIS, HEMOLYTIC ANEMIA,
APLASTIC ANEMIA, AND OTHER AUTOIMMUNE CONDITIONS LIKE SJOGREN'S SYNDROME.
PURE RED CELL APLASIA: IT IS A MARROW DISORDER WHERE THE ERYTHROID PROGENITORS ARE ONLY SUPPRESSED.
THE COMPLETE ABSENCE OF RED CELL PROGENITORS IS SEEN IN SEVERE CASES.
CAUSES OF PURE RED CELL APLASIA: IT CAN BE HEREDITARY OR ACQUIRED. DIAMOND-BLACKFAN ANEMIA OR
CONGENITAL PURE RED CELL APLASIA IS THE HEREDITARY CAUSE. CAUSES OF ACQUIRED PURE RED CELL APLASIA
ARE GIVEN BELOW:
- CANCER
- THYMOMA
- LYMPHOID MALIGNANCIES (EG. NON-HODGKIN'S LYMPHOMA, LARGE GRANULAR LYMPHOCYTOSIS)
- PARANEOPLASTIC TO SOLID TUMORS
- CONNECTIVE TISSUE DISORDERS WITH IMMUNOLOGIC ABNORMALITIES
2084
- SYSTEMIC LUPUS ERYTHEMATOSUS, RHEUMATOID ARTHRITIS
- VIRUSES
- PERSISTENT B19 PARVOVIRUS, HEPATITIS, ADULT T CELL LEUKEMIA VIRUS, EPSTEIN-BARR VIRUS
- DRUGS
- PHENYTOIN, AZATHIOPRINE, CHLORAMPHENICOL, PROCAINAMIDE, ISONIAZID
- MULTIPLE ENDOCRINE GLAND INSUFFICIENCY
- ANTIBODIES TO ERYTHROPOIETIN
- IDIOPATHIC
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION B: NON-HODGKIN'S LYMPHOMA CAN CAUSE PURE RED CELL APLASIA BUT IT COMMONLY PRESENTS AS
PERIPHERAL ADENOPATHY RATHER THAN MEDIASTINAL MASS.
OPTIONS C AND D: GERM CELL TUMORS AND BRONCHOGENIC CARCINOMA ARE NOT COMMONLY KNOWN TO BE
ASSOCIATED WITH RED CELL APLASIA.
2085

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt: ALL OF THE FOLLOWING ARE SEEN IN ANEMIA OF CHRONIC DISEASE EXCEPT:
questions.explanation:
LOW SERUM FERRITIN LEVELS ARE NOT SEEN IN ANEMIA OF CHRONIC DISEASE.
ANEMIA OF CHRONIC DISEASE IS ANEMIA RESULTING DUE TO CHRONIC DISEASES WHICH PRODUCE SYSTEMIC
INFLAMMATION. DURING CHRONIC INFLAMMATION, INFLAMMATORY MEDIATORS LIKE INTERLEUKIN - 6(IL-6)
STIMULATE THE PRODUCTION OF HEPCIDIN FROM THE LIVER. HEPCIDIN IS AN ACUTE PHASE REACTANT THAT
2107
INHIBITS FERROPORTIN ON MACROPHAGES AND ALSO DECREASES IRON FROM STORES TO DEVELOPING RBC
PRECURSORS. THIS RESULTS IN DECREASED PROLIFERATION OF ERYTHROID PROGENITORS DUE TO IMPAIRED IRON
UTILIZATION.
BY DECREASING AVAILABLE SERUM IRON, THE BODY DEFENDS ITSELF FROM CERTAIN BACTERIA(EG, HEMOPHILUS
INFLUENZA) THAT REQUIRE IRON FOR THEIR PATHOGENICITY. THE LAB FINDINGS SEEN IN ANEMIA OF CHRONIC
DISEASE ARE:
- LOW SERUM IRON
- DECREASED TOTAL IRON-BINDING CAPACITY
- ABUNDANT STORED IRON
- INCREASED HEPCIDIN LEVELS
- INCREASED SERUM FERRITIN
THE CHRONIC ILLNESSES ASSOCIATED WITH ANEMIA OF CHRONIC DISEASE CAN BE GROUPED INTO THREE
CATEGORIES:
- CHRONIC MICROBIAL INFECTIONS, SUCH AS OSTEOMYELITIS, BACTERIAL ENDOCARDITIS, AND LUNG ABSCESS
- CHRONIC IMMUNE DISORDERS, SUCH AS RHEUMATOID ARTHRITIS AND REGIONAL ENTERITIS
- NEOPLASMS, SUCH AS CARCINOMAS OF THE LUNG AND BREAST AND HODGKIN LYMPHOMA
NOTE: HEPCIDIN IS THE MAIN REGULATOR OF IRON ABSORPTION WHICH IS ENCODED BY THE HAMP GENE AND
IS DEFECTIVE IN HEMOCHROMATOSIS.
GIVEN BELOW IS AN IMAGE OF IRON ABSORPTION THAT SHOWS FERROPORTIN BEING INHIBITED BY HEPCIDIN AT
INTESTINAL MUCOSAL CELLS

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt: NEUROSECRETORY BODIES ARE SEEN IN ALL EXCEPT
questions.explanation:
NEUROSECRETORY BODIES ARE NOT SEEN IN ADRENAL CORTICAL TUMOURS.
2108
MOST OF THE ADRENOCORTICAL NEOPLASMS ARE ALDOSTERONE-PRODUCING ADENOMAS. CONN SYNDROME
IS PRIMARY HYPERALDOSTERONISM CAUSED BY A SOLITARY ALDOSTERONE-SECRETING ADENOMA.
THE CLINICAL FEATURES OF HYPERALDOSTERONISM ARE SECONDARY HYPERTENSION AND
VARIOUS NEUROMUSCULAR MANIFESTATIONS RESULTING FROM HYPOKALEMIA.
MICROSCOPICALLY, ALDOSTERONE-PRODUCING ADENOMAS ARE FOUND TO HAVE EOSINOPHILIC, LAMINATED
CYTOPLASMIC INCLUSIONS, KNOWN AS SPIRONOLACTONE BODIES, FOUND AFTER TREATMENT WITH THE
ANTIHYPERTENSIVE DRUG SPIRONOLACTONE.
THE IMAGE GIVEN BELOW SHOWS A MICROSCOPIC IMAGE OF SPIRONOLACTONE BODIES FOUND IN ADRENAL
ADENOMAS
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION A: MEDULLARY THYROID CARCINOMA ARISES FROM PARAFOLLICULAR C CELLS AND THEY PRODUCE
CALCITONIN. THEY ARE ASSOCIATED WITH A POINT MUTATION IN THE RET PROTO-ONCOGENE AND MULTIPLE
ENDOCRINE NEOPLASIAS (MEN 2A AND 2B). MICROSCOPICALLY, POLYGONAL CELLS IN AN AMYLOID STROMA ARE
SEEN. ELECTRON MICROSCOPY REVEALS NEUROSECRETORY GRANULES WITHIN THE CYTOPLASM.
OPTION B: PITUITARY ADENOMA MAY PRESENT WITH VISUAL FIELD ABNORMALITIES OR PITUITARY APOPLEXY
(ACUTE HAEMORRHAGE INTO AN ADENOMA). PROLACTINOMA IS THE MOST COMMON TYPE OF
HYPERFUNCTIONING PITUITARY ADENOMA. HISTOLOGICALLY, PROLACTINOMAS ARE COMPOSED OF CHROMOPHOBE
CELLS WITH CYTOPLASMIC NEUROSECRETORY GRANULES.
OPTION C: ADRENAL MEDULLARY PHEOCHROMOCYTOMAS ARE THE MOST COMMON PARAGANGLIOMA.
EXTRA-ADRENAL PARAGANGLIOMAS OCCUR IN THE HEAD AND NECK AT CAROTID BODIES. MICROSCOPICALLY,
CAROTID BODY TUMOURS CONTAIN NESTS (ZELLBALLEN) OF CHIEF CELLS. ELECTRON MICROSCOPY SHOWS
WELL-DEMARCATED NEUROSECRETORY GRANULES.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt: IDENTIFY THE TRUE STATEMENT/S REGARDING CLEAR CELL CARCINOMA OF THE KIDNEY
questions.explanation:
TRUE STATEMENTS REGARDING CLEAR CELL CARCINOMA OF THE KIDNEY ARE 1, 4. CLEAR CELL CARCINOMA IS
THE MOST COMMON SPORADIC RENAL CELL CANCER AND CELLS SHOW INTRACELLULAR ACCUMULATION OF GLYCOGEN
2109
AND FAT.
CLEAR CELL CANCER ARISES FROM THE PROXIMAL TUBULAR EPITHELIUM AND USUALLY OCCURS AS SOLITARY
UNILATERAL LESIONS.
MOST OF THE CASES ARE SPORADIC, BUT CAN ALSO OCCUR EITHER IN FAMILIAL FORMS OR IN ASSOCIATION
WITH VON HIPPEL-LINDAU (VHL) DISEASE. THEY ARE ASSOCIATED WITH THE LOSS OF SEQUENCE OF THE SHORT
ARM OF CHROMOSOME 3. THOSE WITH VHL DISEASE INHERIT A GERMLINE MUTATION OF THE VHL GENE ON
CHROMOSOMAL BAND 3P25 AND LOSE THE SECOND ALLELE BY SOMATIC MUTATION.
THE VHL PROTEIN CAUSES THE DEGRADATION OF HYPOXIA-INDUCED FACTORS (HIFS), WHICH ARE
TRANSCRIPTION FACTORS THAT CONTRIBUTE TO CARCINOGENESIS BY STIMULATING THE EXPRESSION OF VASCULAR
ENDOTHELIAL GROWTH FACTOR (VEGF) THAT HELPS DRIVE TUMOUR CELL GROWTH.
HISTOLOGICALLY, THE TUMOUR CELLS HAVE A ROUNDED OR POLYGONAL SHAPE AND ABUNDANT CLEAR OR
GRANULAR CYTOPLASM, WHICH CONTAINS GLYCOGEN AND LIPIDS.
GIVEN BELOW IS THE HISTOPATHOLOGICAL IMAGE OF CLEAR CELL CARCINOMA.
CANCEROUS CELLS PRODUCE VARIOUS ABNORMAL HORMONES RESULTING IN PARANEOPLASTIC SYNDROME. THESE
INCLUDE POLYCYTHEMIA, HYPERCALCEMIA, CUSHING SYNDROME, AMYLOIDOSIS AND HYPERTENSION.
THE MOST COMMON SITE OF METASTASIS IS THE LUNGS AND BONES. RADICAL NEPHRECTOMY IS THE TREATMENT
OF CHOICE. BUT T1A(SIZE LESS THAN 4CM) TUMOURS ARE TREATED BY NEPHRON-SPARING SURGERY OR PARTIAL
NEPHRECTOMY TO PRESERVE RENAL FUNCTION. DRUGS THAT INHIBIT VEGF AND TYROSINE KINASE INHIBITORS
ARE USED AS AN ADJUNCT THERAPY FOR METASTATIC DISEASE.

GENOMIC IMPRINTING REFERS TO GENE SILENCING/ INACTIVATION. HERE EITHER THE MATERNAL OR THE
PATERNAL ALLELE IS INACTIVATED RESULTING IN ONLY ONE FUNCTIONAL ALLELE. IT OCCURS BY THE PROCESS OF
2110

- DNA METHYLATION
- HISTONE DEACETYLATION

questions.prompt: MATCH THE MICROSCOPIC APPEARANCE IN COLUMN A WITH THE TYPE OF TUMOR IN COLUMN B
questions.explanation:
THE CORRECTLY MATCHED OPTION OF THE MICROSCOPIC APPEARANCE WITH THE TYPE OF TUMOR IS 1-C, 2-D,
3-A, 4-B.
- SCHILLER DUVAL BODIES - YOLK SAC TUMOR
- PRESENCE OF TEETH, HAIR, ETC - TERATOMA
- SIGNET RING CELLS - KRUCKENBERG TUMOR
- CALL-EXNER BODIES - GRANULOSA CELL TUMOR
SCHILLER DUVAL BODIES ARE SEEN IN YOLK SAC TUMORS. A YOLK SAC TUMOR/ENDODERMAL SINUS TUMOR IS AN
AGGRESSIVE MALIGNANT GERM CELL TUMOR OF THE OVARIES. MOST OF THE YOLK SAC TUMORS
HAVE SCHILLER-DUVAL BODIES AND THEY ARE PATHOGNOMONIC. THESE ARE GLOMERULUS-LIKE STRUCTURES
CONSISTING OF A CENTRAL VESSEL SURROUNDED BY TUMOR CELLS WITHIN A SPACE THAT IS ALSO LINED BY TUMOR
CELLS.
THE IMAGE GIVEN BELOW SHOWS SCHILLER-DUVAL BODIES SEEN IN YOLK SAC TUMORS.

CONTAIN EMBRYONIC TISSUES LEADING TO THE DIFFERENTIATION OF CELLS ALONG THESE PATHWAYS. APART
FROM TEETH, HAIR MAY ALSO CONTAIN SKIN, SEBACEOUS GLANDS, FAT, BONE, CARTILAGE, ETC.
2113
THERE ARE THREE CLASSES OF TERATOMAS:
- MATURE TERATOMAS (EG - DERMOID CYST)
- IMMATURE TERATOMAS (EG - SOLID TERATOMA)
- MONODERMAL HIGHLY SPECIALIZED TUMORS (EG - STRUMA OVARII)

SIGNET-RING CELLS ARE SEEN IN THE KRUKENBERG TUMOR. KRUKENBERG TUMOR IS THE CARCINOMA OF THE
STOMACH THAT METASTASIZE TO THE OVARY. SIGNET RING CELLS ARE MUCIN-PRODUCING CELLS. THE
APPEARANCE OF A SIGNET RING OFTEN ORIGINATES FROM THE GASTRIC MUCOSA.
THE IMAGE BELOW SHOWS SIGNET-RING CELLS IN THE KRUCKENBERG TUMOR.
OPTION D: GRANULOSA CELL TUMOURS ARISE FROM GRANULOSA CELLS WHICH FORM PART OF THE DEVELOPING

2114
BODIES ARE SEEN IN GRANULOSA CELL TUMORS. THESE ARE GLAND LIKE SMALL STRUCTURES WITH ACIDOPHILIC
MATERIAL AND IMMATURE FOLLICLES.

GALLBLADDER POLYP IS A PRE-MALIGNANT CONDITION THAT USUALLY PRESENTS WITH BILIARY COLIC AND

POTENTIAL.
RISK FACTORS OF MALIGNANCY IN ADENOMATOUS POLYP:
- AGE >60 YEARS
- COEXISTENCE OF GALL STONES
- THE DOCUMENTED INCREASE IN SIZE
- SIZE OF >10 MM.
POLYPS LESS THAN 1 CM CAN BE FOLLOWED WITH SERIAL ULTRASONOGRAPHY. THE USG GIVEN BELOW DEPICTS

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt:
A 15-YEAR-OLD BOY PRESENTS WITH SWELLING IN THE UPPER DIAPHYSEAL PART OF THE TIBIA. X-RAY OF THE
SWELLING SHOWED A PERIOSTEAL REACTION. A HISTOPATHOLOGICAL IMAGE OF THE BIOPSY IS GIVEN BELOW.
IMMUNOHISTOCHEMISTRY WAS POSITIVE FOR SYNAPTOPHYSIN AND MIC 2. WHAT IS THE LIKELY
DIAGNOSIS?
questions.explanation:
2117
THE GIVEN CLINICAL SCENARIO ALONG WITH THE IMAGE SHOWING SMALL ROUND BLUE CELLS
AND IMMUNOHISTOCHEMISTRY (IHC) POSITIVE FOR SYNAPTOPHYSIN AND MIC-2 POINT TO A LIKELY DIAGNOSIS
OF EWING SARCOMA.
EWING SARCOMA IS THE 2ND MOST COMMON BONE SARCOMA IN CHILDREN. THE MAJORITY OF THE PATIENTS
AFFECTED ARE USUALLY <20 YEARS OF AGE. IT HAS A SLIGHT MALE PREDOMINANCE.
IT COMMONLY INVOLVES THE DIAPHYSIS OF THE LONG BONES LIKE THE FEMUR, TIBIA, FIBULA, AND HUMERUS
AND FLAT BONES OF THE PELVIS. THE MAJORITY OF EWING SARCOMAS HAVE A BALANCED TRANSLOCATION
BETWEEN THE EWSR1 GENE ON CHROMOSOME 22 AND THE FLI1 GENE ON CHROMOSOME 11.
PATIENTS PRESENT WITH PAINFUL ENLARGING MASS, FEVER, AND ANEMIA. THE AFFECTED AREA IS USUALLY
TENDER, SWOLLEN, AND WARM. LABORATORY FINDINGS MAY SHOW AN ELEVATED WBC COUNT AND ERYTHROCYTE
SEDIMENTATION RATE (ESR).
A HISTOPATHOLOGICAL EXAMINATION OF EWING SARCOMA SHOWS SHEETS OF UNIFORM, ROUND CELLS ARRANGED
IN HOMER-WRIGHT ROSETTES. THESE CELLS ARE OF NEUROECTODERMAL ORIGIN AND HAVE MINIMAL CYTOPLASM
AND ABUNDANT GLYCOGEN. WHEN THEY ARE ARRANGED AROUND A CENTRAL FIBRILLARY CORE IN THE FORM OF
CLUSTERS, THE APPEARANCE IS TERMED HOMER-WRIGHT ROSETTES. IMMUNOHISTOCHEMISTRY IS
USUALLY POSITIVE FOR SYNAPTOPHYSIN AND MIC-2.
GIVEN BELOW IS THE HISTOPATHOLOGICAL APPEARANCE OF EWING SARCOMA.
AS TUMOR CELLS ARE RICH IN GLYCOGEN, THEY STAIN POSITIVE FOR PERIODIC ACID SCHIFF (PAS) STAIN
HOWEVER, THEY STAIN NEGATIVELY FOR RETICULIN.
THE IMAGE GIVEN BELOW SHOWS PAS STAINING DONE IN EWING'S SARCOMA:

BONES. DEPOSITION OF PERIOSTEAL REACTION IN LAYERS GIVES AN ONION-PEEL APPEARANCE (SHOWN BELOW).
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION A: OSTEOSARCOMA IS THE MOST COMMON PRIMARY MALIGNANCY OF BONE. THE HISTOLOGICAL
FEATURES OF OSTEOSARCOMA INCLUDE PLEOMORPHIC CELLS WITH HYPERCHROMATIC NUCLEI AND ABUNDANT
MITOSES. THE DIAGNOSIS IS DEFINITIVE WITH THE PRESENCE OF MALIGNANT TUMOR CELLS PRODUCING
UNMINERALIZED OSTEOID OR MINERALIZED BONE ARRANGED IN A TYPICALLY FINE, LACELIKE PATTERN.
GIVEN BELOW IS THE HISTOPATHOLOGICAL IMAGE OF OSTEOSARCOMA:

X-RAY SHOWS PERIOSTEAL REACTION AND IT MAY TAKE THE FORM OF A CODMAN'S TRIANGLE OR IT MAY HAVE A
SUNRAY APPEARANCE AS SHOWN BELOW.
OPTION C: NEUROBLASTOMA IS A TUMOR OF THE SYMPATHETIC GANGLIA AND ADRENAL MEDULLA. IT IS DERIVED
FROM PRIMORDIAL NEURAL CREST CELLS. IT IS THE MOST COMMON EXTRACRANIAL SOLID TUMOR IN CHILDHOOD.

A FAINTLY EOSINOPHILIC FIBRILLARY MATERIAL (NEUROPIL). THIS APPEARANCE IS CALLED HOMER-WRIGHT

OPTION D: OSTEOCLASTOMA IS ALSO KNOWN AS A GIANT CELL TUMOUR. THE TUMOR CELLS ARE PRIMITIVE
OSTEOBLAST PRECURSORS AND EXPRESS HIGH LEVELS OF RANKL. HISTOLOGICALLY, THE TUMORS CONSIST OF
OSTEOCLAST-TYPE GIANT CELLS WITH 100 OR MORE NUCLEI. THESE CELLS ARE USUALLY PRESENT AGAINST A
BACKDROP OF MONONUCLEAR STROMAL CELLS.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING IS A MARKER OF NATURAL KILLER CELL?
questions.explanation:
THE MARKER OF THE NATURAL KILLER CELLS IS CD94. IT IS EXPRESSED IN NATURAL KILLER CELLS AND A SMALL
SUBSET OF T LYMPHOCYTES.
NATURAL KILLER CELLS (NK CELLS) ARE ESSENTIAL CELLS OF INNATE IMMUNITY. THEY ACT AGAINST MALIGNANT
AND VIRUS-INFECTED CELLS. NK CELLS ARE IDENTIFIED BY CD16 AND CD56 CELL SURFACE RECEPTORS.
NK CELLS' ACTIVITY IS AUGMENTED BY INTERFERONS AND UPON ACTIVATION, THEY BIND TO GLYCOPROTEIN
RECEPTORS ON THE SURFACE OF TARGET CELLS AND RELEASE PERFORINS. PERFORINS CREATE PORES IN THE
MEMBRANE OF THE TARGET CELLS. THROUGH THESE PORES, CYTOTOXIC FACTORS LIKE TUMOR NECROSIS
FACTOR-BETA (TNF-β) ENTER THE CELLS AND DESTROY THEM BY APOPTOSIS.
NK CELLS EXPRESS A PHENOMENON KNOWN AS ANTIBODY-DEPENDENT CELLULAR CYTOTOXICITY (ADCC). HERE,
NK CELLS HAVE THE CAPABILITY OF KILLING TARGET CELLS THAT ARE COATED BY IGG ANTIBODIES.
THE IMAGE GIVEN BELOW SHOWS THE ACTIONS OF NK CELLS ON CANCER CELLS.
2122
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION A: CD68 IS EXPRESSED ON MACROPHAGES AND MONOCYTES.
OPTION B: CD 3 IS A T-CELL RECEPTOR MARKER. THEY ARE INVOLVED IN THE TRANSDUCTION OF SIGNALS TO THE
T CELLS WHEN AN ANTIGEN BINDS TO THE T CELL RECEPTOR.
OPTION C: CD 25 IS A COMPONENT OF THE IL2 RECEPTOR AND IS IMPORTANT IN T CELL PROLIFERATION AND
ACTIVATION.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt:
WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING CONDITIONS IS NOT CAUSED BY HIGH-RISK STRAINS OF HUMAN
PAPILLOMAVIRUS?
questions.explanation:
LARYNGEAL PAPILLOMATOSIS IS NOT CAUSED BY HIGH-RISK STRAINS OF HUMAN PAPILLOMAVIRUS (HPV). IT IS
CAUSED BY LOW-RISK HPV STRAINS 6 AND 11.
LARYNGEAL PAPILLOMATOSIS OR JUVENILE PAPILLOMATOSIS IS THE MOST COMMON BENIGN NEOPLASM OF
THE LARYNX IN CHILDREN. IT IS CAUSED BY HPV 6 AND 11. IT INVOLVES SUPRAGLOTTIC AND GLOTTIC REGIONS OF
THE LARYNX. ADULT-ONSET LARYNGEAL PAPILLOMATOSIS INVOLVES THE ANTERIOR PART OF THE VOCAL CORDS.
IT USUALLY OCCURS BETWEEN THE AGES 3–5 YEARS, BUT LESS COMMONLY CAN ALSO OCCUR IN MEN AGED
BETWEEN 30-50 YEARS. CLINICAL FEATURES INCLUDE HOARSENESS OR APHONIA AND RESPIRATORY
DIFFICULTY. THE RECURRENCE RATE IS HIGH BUT THEY RARELY TRANSFORM TO SCC.
DIAGNOSIS IS CONFIRMED BY DIRECT LARYNGOSCOPY AND BIOPSY. TREATMENT CONSISTS OF MICRO
LARYNGOSCOPY, CO2 LASER EXCISION, AND TOPICAL CIDOFOVIR.
THE IMAGE GIVEN BELOW SHOWS LARYNGEAL PAPILLOMA.
2123
OTHER OPTIONS:
CERVICAL CANCER, ANAL CANCER AND OROPHARYNGEAL CANCERS ARE CAUSED BY HIGH RISK HPV TYPES 16 AND
18.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt:
A BOY PRESENTS WITH RECURRENT EPISODES OF MELENA. ON EXAMINATION, THERE WAS ECZEMA OF THE
SKIN WITH MULTIPLE PETECHIAE. HIS PLATELET COUNT WAS LOW BUT RBC AND WBC COUNTS WERE
WITHIN NORMAL LIMITS. WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING IS THE DIAGNOSTIC INVESTIGATION IN THIS PATIENT?
questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN SCENARIO OF RECURRENT EPISODES OF MELENA, ECZEMA, AND MULTIPLE PETECHIAE ALONG WITH
LOW PLATELET COUNTS IS SUGGESTIVE OF WISKOTT-ALDRICH SYNDROME. THE DIAGNOSTIC INVESTIGATION IN THIS
PATIENT IS WASP GENE MUTATION TESTING.
WISKOTT-ALDRICH SYNDROME(WAS) IS AN X-LINKED RECESSIVE IMMUNODEFICIENCY DISORDER. IT IS CAUSED
BY MUTATIONS IN THE WISKOTT-ALDRICH SYNDROME PROTEIN (WASP) THAT PRIMARILY AFFECTS THE T
LYMPHOCYTES.
NORMALLY, WASP REGULATES THE ACTIN CYTOSKELETON AND THUS HELPS IN CELL ADHESION, MIGRATION, AND
THE FORMATION OF SYNAPSES BETWEEN ANTIGEN-PRESENTING AND TARGET CELLS. IN WAS, THERE IS A
PROGRESSIVE LOSS OF T LYMPHOCYTES IN THE PERIPHERAL BLOOD RESULTING IN DEFECTS IN CELLULAR
IMMUNITY.
THE CLINICAL FEATURES OF WAS ARE RECURRENT BACTERIAL INFECTIONS, ECZEMA, AND BLEEDING DUE
TO THROMBOCYTOPENIA. PATIENTS WITH WAS ARE PRONE TO DEVELOP B-CELL LYMPHOMAS AND AUTOIMMUNE
DISORDERS.
THE IMAGE GIVEN BELOW SHOWS ECZEMA SEEN IN WAS
2124
DIAGNOSIS IS BASED ON INTRACELLULAR IMMUNOFLUORESCENCE ANALYSIS OF WAS PROTEIN (WASP)
EXPRESSION IN BLOOD CELLS. IGM LEVELS IN THE SERUM ARE LOW, BUT LEVELS OF IGG ARE USUALLY NORMAL.
REDUCED-SIZED PLATELET IS A TYPICAL FEATURE OF WAS.
THE ONLY CURATIVE TREATMENT IS AN ALLOGENEIC HEMATOPOIETIC STEM CELL TRANSPLANT. PROPHYLACTIC
ANTIBIOTICS, IMMUNOGLOBULIN G (IGG) SUPPLEMENTATION, AND TOPICAL TREATMENT FOR ECZEMA CAN BE
TRIED. GENE THERAPY TRIALS ARE ALSO UNDER RESEARCH.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING IS NOT A PART OF INNATE IMMUNITY?
questions.explanation:
B LYMPHOCYTES ARE NOT A PART OF INNATE IMMUNITY. B LYMPHOCYTES ARE PART OF ADAPTIVE IMMUNITY.
INNATE IMMUNITY IS AN INTRINSIC MECHANISM THAT PROVIDES THE FIRST LINE OF DEFENCE AGAINST
INFECTIONS. IT IS NON-SPECIFIC, PROVIDES IMMEDIATE DEFENCE AGAINST MICROBES, AND HELPS ELIMINATE
DAMAGED CELLS.
COMPONENTS OF INNATE IMMUNITY ARE:
- EPITHELIAL CELLS - THESE PRODUCE ANTIMICROBIAL MOLECULES SUCH AS ALPHA-DEFENSINS
- MACROPHAGES AND NEUTROPHILS
- DENDRITIC CELLS - THESE HAVE RECEPTORS THAT SENSE MICROBES AND CELL DAMAGE. THEY STIMULATE
SECRETION OF CYTOKINES, WHICH PLAY IMPORTANT ROLE IN INFLAMMATION AND ANTIVIRAL DEFENCE
- INNATE LYMPHOID CELLS (ILCS) - THESE ARE LOCAL TISSUE LYMPHOCYTES THAT LACK T-CELL ANTIGEN
RECEPTORS. THEY PRODUCE INFLAMMATORY CYTOKINES DURING THE EARLY PHASES OF IMMUNE
REACTIONS. GAMMA DELTA T LYMPHOCYTES AND NATURAL KILLER (NK) CELLS BELONG TO THIS CLASS
- MAST CELLS
- COMPLEMENT PATHWAY - IT INCLUDE COMPLEMENT PROTEINS OF ALTERNATIVE AND LECTIN PATHWAYS.
2125

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING DISORDERS IS INHERITED IN AN X-LINKED DOMINANT PATTERN?
questions.explanation:
RETT SYNDROME IS INHERITED IN AN X-LINKED DOMINANT PATTERN.
RETT SYNDROME IS A NEURODEVELOPMENTAL DISORDER. IT IS CAUSED DUE TO MUTATION IN THE MECP-2
GENE. THE DISORDER IS MOSTLY SEEN IN GIRLS BECAUSE AFFECTED BOYS USUALLY DIE IN INFANCY DUE TO A
DEFECTIVE SINGLE X CHROMOSOME.
SYMPTOMS OF RETT SYNDROME ARE MICROCEPHALY, DEVELOPMENTAL DELAY, AUTISTIC-LIKE BEHAVIOR,
COGNITIVE DYSFUNCTION, SEIZURES, AND REPETITIVE MOTOR ACTIONS.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION B: DUCHENNE MUSCULAR DYSTROPHY (DMD) IS INHERITED IN X LINKED RECESSIVE PATTERN. IT
OCCURS DUE TO A MUTATION IN THE DYSTROPHIN GENE. TYPICAL FEATURES INCLUDE CALF MUSCLE
PSEUDOHYPERTROPHY AND GOWER'S SIGN (USING ARMS TO LIFT THEMSELVES FROM A SEATED POSITION).
LABORATORY INVESTIGATIONS SHOW ELEVATED SERUM CREATINE KINASE LEVELS. CASIMERSEN HAS BEEN
RECENTLY APPROVED BY THE FDA FOR THE TREATMENT OF DMD.
OPTION C: HUNTINGTON'S DISEASE IS INHERITED IN AN AUTOSOMAL DOMINANT PATTERN. IT IS A TRINUCLEOTIDE
(CAG) REPEAT DISORDER AND SHOWS GENETIC ANTICIPATION (EARLIER ONSET OF DISEASE OR INCREASED
SEVERITY IN SUCCEEDING GENERATIONS). PATIENTS PRESENT WITH INVOLUNTARY MOVEMENTS KNOWN AS
CHOREA. TETRABENAZINE IS USED FOR TREATMENT.
OPTION D: TUBEROUS SCLEROSIS ALSO KNOWN AS BOURNVILLE DISEASE IS INHERITED IN AN AUTOSOMAL
DOMINANT PATTERN. IT OCCURS DUE TO MUTATION IN TSC1 AND TSC2 GENES. IT IS CHARACTERIZED BY
SUBEPENDYMAL NODULES, ANGIOMYOLIPOMAS, CAFE AU LAIT SPOTS, SHAGREEN PATCHES, AND CARDIAC
RHABDOMYOMAS.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt: CELL IN CELL APPEARANCE IS SEEN IN:
questions.explanation:
CELL IN CELL APPEARANCE IS SEEN IN ENTOSIS.
ENTOSIS IS A PHENOMENON WHERE A CELL ENGULFS A CELL OF THE SAME TYPE. WHILE CELLS THAT ARE
INTERNALISED BY THIS MECHANISM ARE INITIALLY VIABLE. BUT, THE MAJORITY OF THEM UNDERGO A
NON-APOPTOTIC FORM OF CELL DEATH. IT PLAYS A PHYSIOLOGICAL ROLE IN THE ELIMINATION OF CELLS DETACHED
FROM A SURFACE.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION A: NECROSIS IS A PATHOLOGIC PROCESS OF IRREVERSIBLE CELL DEATH FOLLOWING SEVERE INJURY. IT IS
ASSOCIATED WITH LOCAL INFLAMMATION DUE TO DAMAGED CELL MEMBRANES. SOME MICROSCOPIC FEATURES OF
NECROSIS ARE AS FOLLOWS:
- DILATION OF MITOCHONDRIA
- NUCLEAR CHANGES: KARYOLYSIS, PYKNOSIS, AND KARYORRHEXIS.
- MYELIN FIGURES REPLACING DEAD CELLS.
OPTION B: APOPTOSIS IS A PATHWAY OF PROGRAMMED CELL DEATH. IN APOPTOSIS, MITOCHONDRIAL AND
DEATH RECEPTOR PATHWAYS ACTIVATE CASPASES RESULTING IN THE FORMATION OF APOPTOTIC BODIES WHICH
ARE THEN PHAGOCYTOSED.
2126
OPTION C: NECROPTOSIS IS A TYPE OF CELL DEATH WHICH IS A HYBRID OF BOTH NECROSIS AND APOPTOSIS. IT IS
ALSO CALLED PROGRAMMED NECROSIS/CASPASE-INDEPENDENT PROGRAMMED CELL DEATH(SINCE IT DOES NOT
RESULT IN CASPASE ACTIVATION).

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt: IDENTIFY THE CELL MARKED IN THE IMAGE BELOW
questions.explanation:
THE CELL MARKED IN THE IMAGE IS A MAST CELL STAINED WITH TOLUIDINE BLUE. MAST CELL GRANULES CONTAIN
ACID PROTEOGLYCAN THAT BINDS BASIC BLUE SUCH AS TOLUIDINE BLUE.
MAST CELLS MAY BE DIFFICULT TO DIFFERENTIATE FROM LYMPHOCYTES IN ROUTINE, HEMATOXYLIN, AND
EOSIN-STAINED SECTIONS, AND SPECIAL METACHROMATIC STAINS (TOLUIDINE BLUE OR GIEMSA) ARE USED TO
VISUALIZE THEIR GRANULES.
MAST CELLS ARE A PART OF INNATE IMMUNITY AND ARE WIDELY DISTRIBUTED IN CONNECTIVE TISSUES. THEY
PLAY AN IMPORTANT ROLE IN IMMEDIATE HYPERSENSITIVITY AND BOTH ACUTE AND CHRONIC INFLAMMATION.
MAST CELLS EXPRESS A RECEPTOR ON THEIR SURFACE THAT BINDS TO THE FC PORTION OF THE IGE ANTIBODY.
WHEN AN ANTIGEN BINDS TO IGE ANTIBODIES ON THE SURFACE OF THE MAST CELL, THEY GET ACTIVATED AND
DEGRANULATE. THIS RESULTS IN THE RELEASE OF:
- GRANULE CONTENTS: HISTAMINE, CHYMASE, TRYPTASE, HEPARIN.
- LIPID MEDIATORS: LEUCOTRIENE C4, D4, PROSTAGLANDIN D2, PLATELET-ACTIVATING FACTOR.
- CYTOKINES: TUMOR NECROSIS FACTOR, INTERLEUKIN-1
THESE MEDIATORS RELEASED FROM MAST CELLS PLAY AN IMPORTANT ROLE IN THE PATHOGENESIS OF
IMMEDIATE/TYPE 1 HYPERSENSITIVITY.
THE IMAGE GIVEN BELOW SHOWS THE SEQUENCE OF EVENTS IN IMMEDIATE (TYPE 1) HYPERSENSITIVITY.
SOME OF THE IMPORTANT DISORDERS ASSOCIATED WITH MAST CELL ACTIVITY ARE BRONCHIAL ASTHMA, URTICARIA,
MASTOCYTOSIS, INTERSTITIAL CYSTITIS AND NEUROFIBROMA.
2127

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt: MATCH THE MALIGNANCIES IN COLUMN A WITH THE GENES IN COLUMN B
questions.explanation:
THE CORRECTLY MATCHED OPTION IS OPTION C 1-D, 2-C, 3-B, AND 4-A.
PLEOMORPHIC ADENOMA IS ASSOCIATED WITH CHROMOSOMAL REARRANGEMENTS THAT INDUCE
OVEREXPRESSION OF PLAG1. IT IS THE MOST COMMON SALIVARY GLAND AND LACRIMAL GLAND NEOPLASM.
MICROSCOPICALLY, IT CONTAINS A MIXTURE OF DUCTAL (EPITHELIAL), MYOEPITHELIAL, AND MESENCHYMAL CELLS.
BURKITT'S LYMPHOMA IS A NON-HODGKIN LYMPHOMA (NHL). IT IS ASSOCIATED WITH THE
TRANSLOCATION CMYC GENE ON CHROMOSOME 8 TO CHROMOSOME 14 OR 22 - T(8:14) OR T(8:22).
HISTOPATHOLOGY OF THE TUMOUR REVEALS A STARRY SKY APPEARANCE.
NEUROBLASTOMA IS A TUMOUR DERIVED FROM PRIMORDIAL NEURAL CREST CELLS. IT IS THE MOST COMMON
EXTRACRANIAL SOLID TUMOUR IN CHILDHOOD. THEY ARE ASSOCIATED WITH THE TRANSLOCATION NMYC GENE. ON
HISTOPATHOLOGY SMALL ROUND BLUE CELLS AND HOMER-WRIGHT PSEUDOROSETTES ARE SEEN.
RETINOBLASTOMA IS THE MOST COMMON PRIMARY INTRAOCULAR MALIGNANCY IN CHILDREN. IT IS ASSOCIATED
WITH CHROMOSOMAL REARRANGEMENTS OF THE RB GENE. MICROSCOPILLAY, FLEXNER-WINTERSTEINER ROSETTES
ARE SEEN.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt: HOW DOES PHAGOLYSOSOME CAUSE CELL DEATH?
options: IS BOTH INTRA AND EXTRA CELLULAR
CAN FUSE WITH OTHER ORGANELLES DIRECTLY
FUSES WITH LYSOSOME TO FORM AUTOPHAGOLYSOSOME
questions.answer: FUSES WITH LYSOSOME TO FORM AUTOPHAGOLYSOSOME
questions.explanation:
PHAGOLYSOSOMES CAUSE CELL DEATH BY THE FUSION OF LYSOSOMES TO FORM AUTOPHAGOLYSOSOMES.
AUTOPHAGY IS A PROCESS IN WHICH A CELL EATS ITS OWN CONTENTS. CYTOPLASMIC MATERIALS ARE DELIVERED
AND DEGRADED BY THE LYSOSOME. IT IS A SURVIVAL TECHNIQUE OF THE CELL IN NUTRIENT DEPRIVATION STATES.
THE STEPS ARE:
- AN ISOLATION MEMBRANE CALLED PHAGOPHORE IS FORMED AND NUCLEATED.
- PHAGOPHORE IS DERIVED FROM THE ER WITH THE HELP OF PLASMA MEMBRANE AND MITOCHONDRIA
- A DOUBLE MEMBRANE-BOUND VESICLE IS FORMED FROM THE ISOLATION MEMBRANE CALLED THE
AUTOPHAGOSOME
- MATURATION OF THE AUTOPHAGOSOME BY FUSION WITH LYSOSOMES, CALLED AUTOPHAGOLYSOSOME.
APOPTOSIS IS A REGULATED MECHANISM OF ELIMINATING UNWANTED AND DAMAGED CELLS. IT IS INITIATED BY
ENZYMES CALLED CASPASES AND IS EXECUTED BY TWO DIFFERENT PATHWAYS. THE MITOCHONDRIAL
PATHWAY WHICH IS ALSO KNOWN AS THE INTRINSIC PATHWAY CARRIES OUT THE MAJORITY OF THE APOPTOSIS.
THE DEATH RECEPTOR PATHWAY OR THE EXTRINSIC PATHWAY IS INITIATED BY PLASMA MEMBRANE DEATH
RECEPTORS. BOTH THESE PATHWAYS COMBINE TOGETHER AND ACTIVATE THE CASPASE CASCADE WHICH RESULTS
2128
IN THE FINAL PHASE OF APOPTOSIS.
PYROPTOSIS IS A FORM OF APOPTOSIS MEDIATED BY FEVER-INDUCING CYTOKINE IL-1. A MULTIPROTEIN
COMPLEX CALLED INFLAMMASOME IS ACTIVATED WHEN MICROORGANISMS ENTER THE CELL. IT WILL IN TURN
ACTIVATE CASPASE 1 WHICH CLEAVES THE IL-1 PRECURSOR AND RELEASES ITS BIOLOGICALLY ACTIVE FORM.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING FEATURES IS NOT OBSERVED IN PLEOMORPHIC ADENOMA?
questions.explanation:
PERINEURAL INVASION IS NOT OBSERVED IN PLEOMORPHIC ADENOMA. PERINEURAL INVASION IS SEEN IN
MALIGNANT SALIVARY GLAND TUMOURS LIKE ADENOID CYSTIC CARCINOMA.
PLEOMORPHIC ADENOMA IS THE MOST COMMON SALIVARY GLAND AND LACRIMAL GLAND NEOPLASM. THEY ARE
COMMONLY SEEN IN THE PAROTID. THEY ARE PAINLESS, SLOW-GROWING, MOBILE, DISCRETE MASSES WITHIN
THE PAROTID.
HISTOLOGICALLY, PLEOMORPHIC ADENOMA CONSISTS OF EPITHELIAL AND MESENCHYMAL COMPONENTS.
- EPITHELIAL COMPONENTS CONSIST OF
- DUCTAL CELLS, MYOEPITHELIAL CELLS ORGANIZED AS DUCTS, ACINI, IRREGULAR TUBULES, OR SHEETS OF CELLS
- SQUAMOUS METAPLASIA WITH THE FORMATION OF KERATIN PEARLS MAY BE PRESENT
- MESENCHYMAL COMPONENTS CONSIST OF
- LOOSE MYXOID AND HYALINE TISSUE CONTAINING CARTILAGE (DUE TO CHONDROID DIFFERENTIATION) AND BONE
THE IMAGE BELOW SHOWS PLEOMORPHIC ADENOMA OF THE SALIVARY GLAND CONSISTING OF MIXED EPITHELIAL
(LEFT) AND MESENCHYMAL CELL COMPONENTS (RIGHT).
CLINICAL FEATURES
- PAINLESS, SLOW-GROWING SWELLING
- LOBULATED, FIRM, ELASTIC-TO-HARD IN CONSISTENCY
- LIFT THE EAR LOBE
2129
- FREE FROM DEEPER STRUCTURES
FNAC IS THE INVESTIGATION OF CHOICE IN DIAGNOSING PLEOMORPHIC ADENOMA. OPEN BIOPSY
CONTRAINDICATED DUE TO CHANCES OF INJURY TO THE FACIAL NERVE. SURGERY IS THE MAINSTAY OF TREATMENT
BY PERFORMING SUPERFICIAL PAROTIDECTOMY.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt:
A 60-YEAR-OLD WOMAN PRESENTS WITH COMPLAINTS OF FATIGUE AND DYSPNEA FOR 2 WEEKS. ON
EXAMINATION, PALLOR WAS SEEN AND HEMOGLOBIN WAS FOUND TO BE 6 GM/DL. WHAT FINDING WILL BE
SEEN ON PERIPHERAL SMEAR?
questions.explanation:
MICROCYTIC HYPOCHROMIC CELLS WILL BE SEEN ON THE PERIPHERAL SMEAR. AN ELDERLY FEMALE PRESENTING
WITH FATIGUE AND DYSPNEA WITH SEVERE ANAEMIA IS SUGGESTIVE OF IRON DEFICIENCY ANAEMIA(IDA). THE
PERIPHERAL SMEAR OF IDA SHOWS MICROCYTIC HYPOCHROMIC RED BLOOD CELLS.
IRON DEFICIENCY IS THE MOST COMMON NUTRITIONAL DISORDER IN THE WORLD. IDA RESULTS FROM DIETARY
DEFICIENCY, IMPAIRED ABSORPTION, INCREASED REQUIREMENT AND, CHRONIC BLOOD LOSS. THE CAUSE OF IRON
DEFICIENCY ANAEMIA IN AN OLDER MAN OR POST-MENOPAUSAL WOMAN IS ALWAYS GASTROINTESTINAL CANCER
UNTIL PROVEN OTHERWISE.
CLINICAL PRESENTATION MAY INCLUDE FATIGUE, PALLOR, DYSPNEA, CHEILOSIS (FISSURES AT THE CORNERS OF THE
MOUTH) AND KOILONYCHIA (SPOONING OF THE FINGERNAILS).
PERIPHERAL SMEAR IN IDA SHOWS:
- MICROCYTIC HYPOCHROMIC RED BLOOD CELLS WITH AN ENLARGED ZONE OF CENTRAL ONE-THIRD PALLOR.
- POIKILOCYTES: PENCIL-SHAPED RBCS AND, TARGET CELLS.
THE IMAGE GIVEN BELOW SHOWS A MICROCYTIC HYPOCHROMIC BLOOD PICTURE IN A PERIPHERAL SMEAR
IDA IS TREATED BY GIVING ORAL, PARENTERAL AND PACKED CELL TRANSFUSIONS DEPENDING ON THE SEVERITY OF
ANAEMIA.
FOR ORAL IRON REPLACEMENT THERAPY,
- UP TO 200MG OF ELEMENTAL IRON IS GIVEN.
2130
- ACCORDING TO THE ANEMIA MUKT BHARAT INITIATIVE, ADULT WOMEN NEED TO TAKE 60 MG ELEMENTAL IRON
+ 500 MCG FOLIC ACID TABLETS ONCE A WEEK.
FOR PARENTERAL IRON THERAPY, THE AMOUNT OF IRON NEEDED BY AN INDIVIDUAL IS CALCULATED BY THE
FORMULA:
BODY WEIGHT(KG) X 2.3 X (15 - PATIENT'S HEMOGLOBIN, G/DL) + 500 OR 1000MG (FOR STORES)

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt: THE IMAGE BELOW IS INDICATIVE OF WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING TUMORS?
questions.explanation:
THE IMAGE SHOWS THE CHARACTERISTIC SCHILLER DUVAL BODY CONSISTENT WITH A YOLK SAC TUMOR.
A YOLK SAC TUMOR/ENDODERMAL SINUS TUMOR IS AN AGGRESSIVE MALIGNANT GERM CELL TUMOR OF THE
OVARIES. IT ORIGINATES FROM EMBRYONAL STRUCTURES OF THE YOLK SAC BY SELECTIVE DIFFERENTIATION.
IT IS MOST OFTENLY SEEN IN CHILDREN AND YOUNG WOMEN. IT USUALLY PRESENTS AS ABDOMINAL
DISTENTION AND A PALPABLE PELVIC MASS.
GROSSLY, THE YOLK-SAC TUMOR APPEARS YELLOW, FRIABLE (HEMORRHAGIC), AND FORMS SOLID MASS.
MOST OF THE YOLK SAC TUMORS HAVE SCHILLER-DUVAL BODIES AND THEY ARE PATHOGNOMONIC. THESE ARE
GLOMERULUS-LIKE STRUCTURES CONSISTING OF A CENTRAL VESSEL SURROUNDED BY TUMOR CELLS WITHIN A SPACE
THAT IS ALSO LINED BY TUMOR CELLS.
THE IMAGE GIVEN BELOW SHOWS SCHILLER-DUVAL BODIES SEEN IN YOLK SAC TUMORS.
YOLK-SAC TUMORS ARE RICH IN ALPHA-FETOPROTEIN. THEREFORE, SERUM LEVELS OF ALPHA-FETOPROTEIN CAN
SERVE AS A RELIABLE TUMOR MARKER IN POST TREATMENT SURVEILLANCE.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION B: DYSGERMINOMA IS THE OVARIAN COUNTERPART OF SEMINOMA. THEY ARE UNILATERAL TUMORS
COMPOSED OF VESICULAR CELLS AND CLEAR CYTOPLASM. THE TUMOR CELLS GROW IN CORDS OR SHEETS THAT ARE
SEPARATED BY SCANTY FIBROUS STROMA. THEY ARE USUALLY INFILTRATED BY LYMPHOCYTES.
2131
OPTION C: KRUKENBERG TUMOR IS THE CARCINOMA OF THE STOMACH THAT METASTASIZE TO THE OVARY. IT IS
CHARACTERIZED BY MUCIN-PRODUCING SIGNET RING CELLS. THE APPEARANCE OF A SIGNET RING OFTEN
ORIGINATES FROM THE GASTRIC MUCOSA.
THE IMAGE BELOW SHOWS SIGNET-RING CELLS IN KRUCKENBERG TUMOR.
OPTION D: GRANULOSA CELL TUMOURS ARISE FROM GRANULOSA CELLS WHICH FORM PART OF THE DEVELOPING
OVARIAN FOLLICLE. THEY ARE UNILATERAL IN NATURE AND THE MASS IS CYSTIC AND ENCAPSULATED. CALL-EXNER
BODIES ARE SEEN IN GRANULOSA CELL TUMOURS. THESE ARE GLAND LIKE SMALL STRUCTURES WITH ACIDOPHILIC
MATERIAL AND IMMATURE FOLLICLES.
THE IMAGE GIVEN BELOW SHOWS CALL-EXNER BODIES SEEN IN GRANULOSA CELL TUMOURS.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt: IN A PATIENT WITH BARE LYMPHOCYTIC DISEASE, GRAFT VS HOST REACTION DOES NOT OCCUR DUE TO:
options: MHC CLASS II DEFICIENCY ON LYMPHOCYTES
MHC CLASS I DEFICIENCY ON LYMPHOCYTES
questions.answer: MHC CLASS II DEFICIENCY ON LYMPHOCYTES
questions.explanation:
2132
IN A PATIENT WITH BARE LYMPHOCYTIC DISEASE, GRAFT VS HOST REACTION DOES NOT OCCUR DUE TO MHC CLASS
II DEFICIENCY ON THE LYMPHOCYTES.
BARE LYMPHOCYTE DISEASE OCCURS DUE TO MUTATIONS IN TRANSCRIPTION FACTORS REQUIRED FOR CLASS II
MHC GENE EXPRESSION. THIS RESULTS IN THE LACK OF CLASS II MHC MOLECULES, LEADING TO THE IMPAIRED
DEVELOPMENT OF CD4+ T CELLS. AS THESE CD 4+ T CELLS ARE REQUIRED FOR BOTH FOR CELLULAR IMMUNITY
AND FOR ASSISTING B CELLS, CLASS II MHC DEFICIENCY RESULTS IN A COMBINED IMMUNO- DEFICIENCY.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt:
A CHILD PRESENTS WITH MULTIPLE SKIN LESIONS OVER THE INNER THIGH AND GENITAL AREAS. IT INITIALLY
STARTED AS MACULE AND LATER DEVELOPED TO BECOME NODULES. SOME NODULES HAVE CENTRAL
UMBILICATION. THE HISTOLOGY OF THE LESION IS SHOWN BELOW. WHAT WOULD BE FOUND ON BIOPSY?
questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN CLINICAL SCENARIO AND HISTOLOGICAL IMAGE ARE DIAGNOSTIC OF MOLLUSCUM CONTAGIOSUM
LESIONS, WHICH SHOW INTRACYTOPLASMIC INCLUSION BODIES, CALLED HENDERSON–PATTERSON BODIES OR
MOLLUSCUM BODIES.
INFECTION IS USUALLY SPREAD BY DIRECT CONTACT, PARTICULARLY AMONG CHILDREN AND YOUNG ADULTS.
MULTIPLE LESIONS OCCUR ON THE SKIN AND MUCOUS MEMBRANES, WITH A PREDILECTION FOR THE TRUNK AND
ANOGENITAL AREAS. INDIVIDUAL LESIONS ARE FIRM, PRURITIC, PINK TO SKIN-COLORED UMBILICATED PAPULES. A
CURD-LIKE MATERIAL CAN BE EXPRESSED FROM THE CENTRAL UMBILICATION.
SMEARING THIS MATERIAL ONTO A GLASS SLIDE AND GIEMSA STAINING SHOWS DIAGNOSTIC MOLLUSCUM
BODIES, WHICH ARE ELLIPSOID, HOMOGENEOUS, CYTOPLASMIC INCLUSIONS THAT ARE FOUND IN THE CELLS OF THE
STRATUM GRANULOSUM AND THE STRATUM CORNEUM AND ARE UP TO 35 µM IN SIZE.
2133
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION A: MULTINUCLEATE GIANT CELLS (CALLED TZANCK CELLS) ARE SEEN IN HERPES SIMPLEX VIRUS
INFECTIONS. THEY ARE FORMED WHEN INDIVIDUAL EPIDERMAL CELLS CONTAINING VIRAL INCLUSIONS FUSE TO
PRODUCE GIANT CELLS. THESE CAN BE DEMONSTRATED BY THE DIAGNOSTIC TZANCK TEST, WHICH IS BASED ON
THE MICROSCOPIC EXAMINATION OF THE VESICLE FLUID.
OPTION B: DONOVAN BODIES ARE SEEN IN DONOVANOSIS, CAUSED BY KLEBSIELLA GRANULOMATIS. DONOVAN
BODIES ARE MINUTE, ENCAPSULATED COCCOBACILLI IN MACROPHAGES, WHICH CAN BE DEMONSTRATED IN
GIEMSA-STAINED SMEARS OF THE EXUDATE.
OPTION D: KOILOCYTES ARE CHARACTERISTICALLY SEEN IN HPV INFECTIONS, SUCH AS CONDYLOMATA
ACUMINATA. KOILOCYTES ARE LINING CELLS THAT HAVE PERINUCLEAR CYTOPLASMIC VACUOLIZATION.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt:
INVESTIGATIONS OF A PATIENT BEING EVALUATED FOR LEUKEMIA REVEALED A WBC COUNT OF
4,50,000/µL, WITH EOSINOPHILIA AND BASOPHILIA. WHAT IS THE LIKELY DIAGNOSIS IN THIS CASE?
questions.explanation:
A WBC COUNT OF 4,50,000/µL WITH EOSINOPHILIA AND BASOPHILIA INDICATES A PROBABLE DIAGNOSIS OF
CHRONIC MYELOGENOUS LEUKEMIA.
CML IS A MYELOPROLIFERATIVE NEOPLASM. IT IS CAUSED BY THE TRANSLOCATION OF ABL GENE ON
CHROMOSOME 9 ONTO BCR GENE ON CHROMOSOME 22, RESULTING IN THE FORMATION OF THE BCR-ABL
FUSION GENE. THIS CHROMOSOMAL ABNOMALITY, CALLED PHILADELPHIA CHROMOSOME, IS CHARACTERISTIC OF
CML.
THE RESULTING BCR-ABL TRANSLOCATION RESULTS IN THE ACTIVATION OF TYROSINE KINASE THAT SIGNALS
PRO-GROWTH AND PRO-SURVIVAL PATHWAYS LIKE RAS AND JAK/STAT PATHWAYS RESULTING IN THE
PROLIFERATION OF HEMATOPOIETIC STEM CELLS.
PATIENTS TYPICALLY PRESENT WITH A DRAGGING SENSATION ABDOMEN DUE TO SPLENOMEGALY OR SPLENIC
INFARCT, FATIGUE, MALAISE, AND WEIGHT LOSS.
ON PERIPHERAL SMEAR THERE IS LEUKOCYTOSIS WITH LEUKOCYTE COUNT, OFTEN EXCEEDING 100,000
CELLS/MM3 (NEUTROPHILS, BAND FORMS, METAMYELOCYTES, MYELOCYTES, EOSINOPHILS, AND BASOPHILS),
BLASTS ARE USUALLY LESS THAN 10% OF THE CIRCULATING CELLS, THE PLATELET COUNT IS USUALLY INCREASED.
2134
BASOPHILS AND EOSINOPHILS ARE OFTEN INCREASED.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION D: ACUTE MYELOID LEUKEMIA (AML) IS A HEMATOPOIETIC PROGENITOR MALIGNANCY THAT CAUSES
IMMATURE MYELOBLAST ACCUMULATION IN THE BONE MARROW. INCIDENCE INCREASES WITH AGE AND PEAKS
AFTER 60 YEARS OF AGE.
THE WBC COUNT IS ABOUT 15,000/µL. FEW CASES HAVE EITHER <5000 OR >1,00,000/µL WBC
COUNT. CLINICALLY, THE PATIENTS PRESENT WITH SYMPTOMS RESULTING DUE TO PANCYTOPENIA (ANEMIA,
NEUTROPENIA, THROMBOCYTOPENIA). FOR ACUTE MYELOBLASTIC LEUKEMIA (AML) DIAGNOSIS, THE BLAST CELL
COUNT SHOULD BE ≥20% IN THE PERIPHERAL BLOOD OR BONE MARROW
OTHER DISTINCTIVE FEATURES OF AML INCLUDE
- BONE MARROW/ PERIPHERAL SMEAR SHOWS A LARGE, UNIFORM POPULATION OF CELLS (MYELOBLASTS) WITH
PROMINENT NUCLEOLI (YELLOW ARROW). IT SHOWS THE PRESENCE OF PRIMARY CYTOPLASMIC GRANULES
- AUER RODS: NEEDLE-SHAPED AZUROPHILIC INTRACYTOPLASMIC INCLUSION BODIES FORMED BY THE FUSION OF
LYSOSOMES. (BLACK ARROW)
- MULTIPLE AUER RODS CLUSTERED TOGETHER WITHIN A SINGLE CELL RESEMBLING A BUNDLE OF STICKS KNOWN AS
FAGGOT CELLS (SEEN IN PERIPHERAL SMEAR).
2135
OPTION A: ACUTE LYMPHOBLASTIC LEUKEMIA (ALL) ARISES FROM IMMATURE B (PRE-B) OR T (PRE-T) CELLS
CALLED LYMPHOBLASTS. MOST CASES PRESENT WITH A REDUCED OR NORMAL LYMPHOCYTE COUNT. BLOOD
COUNTS SHOW ANEMIA, THROMBOCYTOPENIA, AND NEUTROPENIA.
IMMUNOHISTOCHEMISTRY FOR TERMINAL DEOXYNUCLEOTIDYL TRANSFERASE (TDT) IS POSITIVE IN PRE-B AND
PRE-T LYMPHOBLASTS. PERIPHERAL SMEAR SHOWS LYMPHOBLASTS THAT HAVE CONDENSED CHROMATIN, LESS
CONSPICUOUS NUCLEOLI, AND SMALLER AMOUNTS OF CYTOPLASM WHICH LACKS GRANULES AS SHOWN BELOW.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt:
WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING MOLECULES HELPS THE LEUKOCYTES ROLL OVER THE ENDOTHELIAL CELLS IN THE
VESSELS?
questions.explanation:
E-SELECTIN, WHICH IS PRESENT OVER THE ENDOTHELIUM, HELPS THE LEUKOCYTE ROLL OVER THE ENDOTHELIUM.
SELECTINS ARE OF 3 TYPES: L-SELECTIN PRESENT ON LEUKOCYTES, E-SELECTIN PRESENT ON THE ENDOTHELIUM,
AND P-SELECTIN PRESENT IN PLATELETS AND ON THE ENDOTHELIUM.
THE WEAK ROLLING ACTION SLOWS DOWN THE LEUKOCYTES AND ALLOWS THEM TO BIND MORE FIRMLY TO THE
ENDOTHELIUM WITH THE HELP OF INTEGRINS.
THE RECRUITMENT OF LEUKOCYTES TO THE SITE OF INJURY INVOLVES THE FOLLOWING STEPS:
- LUMEN OF THE VESSEL TO THE ENDOTHELIUM:
- MARGINATION: LEUKOCYTES ASSUME A PERIPHERAL POSITION ALONG THE ENDOTHELIAL SURFACE BECAUSE OF
THE STASIS OF BLOOD FLOW.
- ROLLING: LEUKOCYTES START ROLLING ON THE VESSEL WALL BECAUSE OF SIGNALING MOLECULES FROM THE
ENDOTHELIUM.
- ADHESION: LEUKOCYTES ARE ATTACHED TO THE ENDOTHELIUM BECAUSE OF ADHESION MOLECULES THAT ARE
ACTIVATED BY CYTOKINES.
- TRANSMIGRATION OF THE LEUKOCYTES ACROSS THE VASCULAR ENDOTHELIUM.
- MIGRATION TOWARDS A CHEMOTACTIC STIMULUS IN THE EXTRAVASCULAR TISSUES.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION A: CADHERINS ARE A TYPE OF GLYCOPROTEIN CELL ADHESION MOLECULE THAT ALLOWS CELLS TO ADHERE
TOGETHER.
OPTION B: PLATELET ENDOTHELIAL CELL ADHESION MOLECULE-1 (PECAM-1), AIDS IN DIAPEDESIS, WHICH IS THE
MOVEMENT OF LEUKOCYTES THROUGH INTACT ENDOTHELIUM OF THE CAPILLARIES TO REACH THE SITE OF INJURY.
OPTION D: CD11A, A MOLECULE FROM THE INTEGRIN FAMILY, HELPS FIRMLY ADHERE THE LEUKOCYTE TO THE
ENDOTHELIAL CELL.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING STATEMENTS ARE TRUE ABOUT HEREDITARY SPHEROCYTOSIS?
options: GALL STONES DEVELOP BY 4-5 YEARS OF AGE.
SPLENECTOMY DOES NOT PROTECT AGAINST DEVELOPING GALL STONES.
AT LEAST 25 % CASES HAVE A FAMILY HISTORY OF HS.
HIGH MCH IS PATHOGNOMONIC OF HS.
questions.answer: AT LEAST 25 % CASES HAVE A FAMILY HISTORY OF HS.
questions.explanation:
AMONG THE GIVEN STATEMENTS ABOUT HEREDITARY SPHEROCYTOSIS, THE TRUE STATEMENT IS OPTION C– AT
LEAST 25% OF CASES HAVE A FAMILIAL INHERITANCE (AS 75% OF CASES SHOW AN AUTOSOMAL DOMINANT
INHERITANCE PATTERN)
HEREDITARY SPHEROCYTOSIS IS A TYPE OF HEREDITARY HEMOLYTIC ANEMIA THAT IS MOSTLY INHERITED IN AN
AUTOSOMAL DOMINANT PATTERN. SOME OF THE CASES CAN BE AUTOSOMAL RECESSIVE OR
SPORADIC. MUTATIONS OF THE RED BLOOD CELL SURFACE PROTEINS SPECTRIN AND ANKYRIN CAN RESULT IN
2142
UNSTABLE CELL MEMBRANES, LEADING TO HEMOLYSIS.
THE FOLLOWING MUTATIONS HAVE BEEN IDENTIFIED IN HEREDITARY SPHEROCYTOSIS:
AUTOSOMAL DOMINANT (MORE COMMON):
- ANKYRIN - MOST COMMON
- BAND 3
- β-SPECTRIN
AUTOSOMAL RECESSIVE:
- α-SPECTRIN
- BAND 4.2
THIS DISORDER CAN PRESENT AT A YOUNG AGE WITH SEVERE JAUNDICE AND FATIGUE. THE UNCONJUGATED
HYPERBILIRUBINEMIA PREDISPOSES THE PATIENT TO DEVELOP GALLSTONES IN EARLY ADULTHOOD. PIGMENT
STONES ARE FOUND IN 40-50% OF THE AFFECTED ADULTS.
LABORATORY FINDINGS INCLUDE NORMOCYTIC ANEMIA WITH UNCONJUGATED HYPERBILIRUBINEMIA. THE
PERIPHERAL SMEAR WILL SHOW LARGE SPHERICAL RED BLOOD CELLS WITHOUT CENTRAL PALLOR.
MCHC (NOT, MCH) IS INCREASED IN HEREDITARY SPHEROCYTOSIS; HOWEVER, IT IS NOT PATHOGNOMONIC AS IT
COULD BE FOUND IN OTHER CONDITIONS AS WELL. MCV IS MILDLY DECREASED BECAUSE OF CELL
SHRINKAGE. THERE IS MILD TO MODERATE ANEMIA, THEREFORE, MCH COULD BE SLIGHTLY LOWER.
THE DIAGNOSIS CAN BE CONFIRMED BY THE ACID GLYCEROL LYSIS TEST AND THE EOSIN-5′-MALEIMIDE
(EMA)–BINDING TEST.
THERE IS NO SPECIFIC TREATMENT AVAILABLE BESIDES SPLENECTOMY. SPLEEN IS THE MAJOR SITE WHERE
SPHEROCYTES UNDERGO HEMOLYSIS. HENCE, SPLENECTOMY CORRECTS THE ANEMIA AND ITS ASSOCIATED
COMPLICATIONS, THEREBY PLAYING A ROLE IN PREVENTING GALLSTONES. IT IS DONE AT 4–6 YEARS OF AGE IN
SEVERE CASES AND AFTER PUBERTY IN MODERATE CASES. IT SHOULD BE FOLLOWED UP WITH THE APPROPRIATE
ANTIBIOTIC AND VACCINE PROPHYLAXIS.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt: B CELLS EXPRESS IGM AND IGD ANTIBODIES AT THE SAME TIME DUE TO WHICH PHENOMENON?
questions.explanation:
B CELLS EXPRESS IGM AND IGD ANTIBODIES AT THE SAME TIME DUE TO ALTERNATIVE RNA SPLICING.
ALTERNATIVE RNA SPLICING IS THE PROCESS BY WHICH DIFFERENT PROTEINS ARE PRODUCED FROM THE SAME
RNA TRANSCRIPT BY SPLICING IT IN DIFFERENT WAYS.
MATURE CIRCULATING B CELLS INITIALLY EXPRESS IGM AND IGD ANTIBODIES ON THEIR SURFACES BEFORE THEY
ARE STIMULATED TO PRODUCE SPECIFIC ANTIBODIES. THE HEAVY CHAINS IN IGM AND IGD ARE MU (µ)
AND DELTA (δ), RESPECTIVELY. THE MU AND DELTA GENES FOR THESE HEAVY CHAINS ARE LOCATED PROXIMAL TO
THE VDJ ENCODING REGIONS (I.E., VARIABLE, DIVERSITY, AND JOINING REGIONS) OF THE HEAVY CHAIN LOCUS. A
PRIMARY RNA TRANSCRIPT OF THIS ENTIRE REGION IS PRODUCED, WHICH THEN UNDERGOES ALTERNATIVE RNA
PROCESSING, ENABLING THE PRODUCTION OF BOTH TRANSMEMBRANE IGM AND IGD ON B CELLS.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTIONS A AND C: SOMATIC HYPERMUTATION IS A CELLULAR RESPONSE BY WHICH THE IMMUNE SYSTEM
ADAPTS TO THE NEW FOREIGN ELEMENTS THAT CONFRONT IT. THEY DO SO BY ADDING NUCLEOTIDES IN V GENE
2143
REGIONS OF HEAVY AND LIGHT CHAINS, RESULTING IN A BETTER FIT OF ANTIGEN WITH THE ANTIBODIES. THIS
HENCE INCREASES THE AFFINITY OF ANTIBODIES TO ANTIGENS. DUE TO THIS, THE SUBSET OF PLASMA CELLS WITH
THESE IMPROVED HYPERVARIABLE REGIONS ARE MORE STRONGLY SELECTED BY THE ANTIGEN AND THEREFORE
CONSTITUTE A LARGER PART OF THE POPULATION OF ANTIBODY-PRODUCING CELLS. THIS PROCESS IS CALLED
AFFINITY MATURATION.
OPTION D: ALLELIC EXCLUSION IS THE PROCESS BY WHICH A CELL EXPRESSES ONE OF THE TWO ALLELES OF THE
GENE AND EXCLUDES THE OTHER ALLELE.
B CELLS ARE DIPLOID, THEREFORE, EACH B CELL HAS SIX GENE SEGMENT POOLS RELATED TO ANTIBODY CHAINS:
- TWO HEAVY-CHAIN POOLS (ONE FROM EACH PARENT) AND
- FOUR LIGHT-CHAIN POOLS (ONE κ AND ONE λ FROM EACH PARENT).
HOWEVER, EACH B CELL USES ONLY TWO OF THE SIX GENE SEGMENT POOLS: ONE OUT OF THE TWO HEAVY-CHAIN
POOLS (MATERNAL AND PATERNAL) AND ONE OUT OF THE FOUR LIGHT-CHAIN POOLS. THUS, EACH B CELL MUST
CHOOSE NOT ONLY BETWEEN ITS κ AND λ LIGHT-CHAIN POOLS BUT ALSO BETWEEN ITS MATERNAL AND PATERNAL
LIGHT-CHAIN AND HEAVY-CHAIN POOLS. THIS PROCESS OF CHOOSING IS BY ALLELIC EXCLUSION.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING ARE TRUE REGARDING SIRTUINS?
questions.explanation:
THE TRUE STATEMENTS REGARDING SIRTUINS ARE 1, 2, 3, AND 4 (OPTION B).
SIRTUINS ARE A CLASS OF PROTEINS THAT POSSESS EITHER MONO-ADP-RIBOSYLTRANSFERASE OR DEACETYLASE
ACTIVITY. THEY HAVE BEEN SHOWN TO SLOW DOWN THE AGING PROCESS.
SIRTUINS PROMOTE THE EXPRESSION OF SEVERAL GENES WHOSE PRODUCTS INCREASE LONGEVITY. THESE INCLUDE
PROTEINS THAT:
- INHIBIT METABOLIC ACTIVITY
- REDUCE APOPTOSIS
- STIMULATE PROTEIN FOLDING
- INHIBIT THE HARMFUL EFFECTS OF OXYGEN-FREE RADICALS
- INCREASE INSULIN SENSITIVITY AND GLUCOSE METABOLISM (MAYBE TARGETED FOR THE TREATMENT OF
DIABETES)
- ENSURE THAT DAMAGED DNA IS NOT PROPAGATED, PREVENTING THE ACCUMULATION OF MUTATIONS
- PROMOTES REPLICATIVE SENESCENCE UNDER CHRONIC STRESS
SIRTUINS LEVEL INCREASES BY CALORIC RESTRICTION AND ARE PRESENT IN RED WINE.
SIRTUINS ARE RESPONSIBLE FOR AN INCREASE IN INSULIN SENSITIVITY. HENCE, THEY CAN PLAY AN IMPORTANT
ROLE IN THE TREATMENT OF DIABETES.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt: MATCH THE FOLLOWING CELLS WITH THEIR LOCATIONS.
questions.explanation:
THE CORRECTLY MATCHED SET OF THE CELLS AND THEIR LOCATIONS IS 1-B, 2-A, 3-C, 4-D.
2144
KUPFFER CELLS ARE A COMPONENT OF THE MONONUCLEAR PHAGOCYTIC SYSTEM AND ARE LOCATED IN THE LIVER.
PARIETAL CELLS, ALSO CALLED OXYNTIC CELLS, ARE FOUND IN THE UPPER HALF OF THE GASTRIC GLANDS. THEY HAVE
NUMEROUS MITOCHONDRIA AND ARE ACTIVELY INVOLVED IN THE SECRETION OF HYDROCHLORIC ACID AND
INTRINSIC FACTOR - A GLYCOPROTEIN THAT AIDS IN THE ABSORPTION OF VITAMIN B12 FROM THE ILEUM.
DUST CELLS ARE MACROPHAGES IN THE WALLS OF THE ALVEOLI. THEY PHAGOCYTOSE DUST PARTICLES IN THE
ALVEOLI. IN CHF THESE MACROPHAGES PHAGOCYTOSE ERYTHROCYTES THAT ESCAPE FROM THE CAPILLARIES. THE
CELLS ACQUIRE A BRICK-RED COLOR AND ARE CALLED HEART FAILURE CELLS.
CLARA CELLS ARE NON-CILIATED CUBOIDAL EPITHELIAL CELLS THAT SECRETE IMPORTANT DEFENSE MARKERS AND
SERVE AS STEM CELLS AFTER INJURY. THESE CELLS MAKE UP A LARGER PORTION OF THE EPITHELIAL LINING IN THE
LATER PORTIONS OF THE CONDUCTING AIRWAY.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING CYTOKINES IS NOT INVOLVED IN TH1 RESPONSE?
questions.explanation:
THE CYTOKINE NOT INVOLVED IN TH1 RESPONSE IS IL-4.
DENDRITIC CELLS AND MACROPHAGES PRESENT ANTIGENS TO T HELPER CELLS (TH) AFTER WHICH THEY
DIFFERENTIATE INTO TH1 AND TH2 CELLS. THEY ARE RESPONSIBLE FOR CELL-MEDIATED AND HUMORAL IMMUNE
RESPONSES, RESPECTIVELY. IL-12 IS SECRETED BY MACROPHAGES AND PROMOTES THE PROLIFERATION OF TH1
CELLS.
TH1 CELLS SECRETE:
- IL-2 WHICH ACTIVATES NATURAL KILLER CELLS (NK CELLS) AND CYTOTOXIC T CELLS
- IFN GAMMA WHICH STIMULATES MACROPHAGES AND IS ALSO RESPONSIBLE FOR DELAYED HYPERSENSITIVITY
ALONG WITH TGF BETA.
TH2 CELLS SECRETE:
- IL- 4 STIMULATES IGE PRODUCTION FROM B CELLS
- IL- 5 STIMULATES PROLIFERATION OF EOSINOPHILS AND TOGETHER PLAY A ROLE IN HELMINTHIC AND ALLERGIC
REACTIONS
- IL- 6 PROMOTES PROLIFERATION OF B CELLS AND PRODUCTION OF ANTIBODIES.

questions.subject: Pathology
questions.prompt:
A 19-YEAR-OLD GIRL PRESENTS WITH A MIDLINE NECK SWELLING THAT MOVES ON DEGLUTITION. USG
REVEALED A 2 CM X 2 CM NODULE ON THE LEFT LOBE OF THE THYROID, EXTENDING INTO THE STRAP
MUSCLES. THE HISTOPATHOLOGY IMAGE IS GIVEN BELOW. WHAT IS THE MOST LIKELY DIAGNOSIS?
questions.explanation:
THE CLINICAL SCENARIO AND THE IMAGE SHOWING PAPILLAE LINED BY CELLS WITH OVERLAPPING NUCLEI
AND ORPHAN ANNIE EYE NUCLEI INDICATE A DIAGNOSIS OF PAPILLARY CARCINOMA OF THYROID.
PAPILLARY CARCINOMA OF THYROID PRESENTS AS A PAINLESS NODULE OR MASS IN THE NECK OR CERVICAL NODE
IN WOMEN OF REPRODUCTIVE AGE. THE RISK FACTORS INCLUDE EXPOSURE TO IONIZING
RADIATION AND HASHIMOTO THYROIDITIS.
IT USUALLY PRESENTS AS A COLD NODULE ON A SCAN. HISTOPATHOLOGICAL EXAMINATION SHOWS BRANCHING
PAPILLAE AND FOLLICLES WITH FIBROVASCULAR STALK. NUCLEAR CHANGES INCLUDE GROUND GLASS OR ORPHAN
ANNIE EYE NUCLEI, PSEUDO-INCLUSIONS, AND NUCLEAR GROOVES. PSAMMOMA BODIES ARE OFTEN PRESENT.
2145
DIAGNOSIS CAN BE MADE BASED ON THESE NUCLEAR FEATURES, EVEN IN THE ABSENCE OF PAPILLARY
ARCHITECTURE. THE PROGNOSIS IS EXCELLENT, WITH A 10-YEAR SURVIVAL RATE IN EXCESS OF 95%.
THE IMAGE BELOW SHOWS ORPHAN ANNIE EYE NUCLEI WITH CENTRAL CLEARING AND MARGINATION OF
CHROMATIN:
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION A: MEDULLARY CARCINOMA OF THE THYROID IS A NEUROENDOCRINE TUMOR THAT IS DERIVED FROM
PARAFOLLICULAR C CELLS, THAT SECRETE CALCITONIN.
MOST OF THESE TUMORS OCCUR SPORADICALLY. SOME ARE ASSOCIATED WITH FAMILIAL MULTIPLE ENDOCRINE
NEOPLASIA (MEN) SYNDROME: MEN 2A AND MEN 2B. THEY FREQUENTLY PRESENT AS A NECK MASS THAT
MAY BE ASSOCIATED WITH CERVICAL LYMPHADENOPATHY. WITH THE ENLARGEMENT OF THE NODULE, PATIENTS
MAY HAVE DYSPHAGIA AND DYSPNEA.
HISTOPATHOLOGY SHOWS POLYGONAL TO SPINDLE-SHAPED CELLS WHICH FORM NESTS, TRABECULAE, OR FOLLICLES.
AMYLOID DEPOSITS THAT ARE DERIVED FROM THE ALTERED CALCITONIN MOLECULES ARE PRESENT IN THE STROMA.
2146
CALCITONIN IN THE TUMOR CELLS AND STROMA IS EASILY DEMONSTRATABLE BY IMMUNOHISTOCHEMISTRY.
OPTION B: FOLLICULAR CARCINOMA THYROID ON HISTOPATHOLOGY MAY SHOW UNIFORM CELLS FORMING SMALL
FOLLICLES CONTAINING COLLOID (RESEMBLING NORMAL THYROID GLAND) OR SHEETS OF CELLS WITHOUT COLLOID.
ANAPLASTIC CARCINOMAS ARE POORLY DIFFERENTIATED THYROID CARCINOMAS WITH VARIED MORPHOLOGY
INCLUDING GIANT CELLS OR SPINDLE-SHAPED CELLS OR BOTH. THERE IS MINIMAL FOLLICULAR DIFFERENTIATION
WITH INTRATUMORAL NECROSIS.
2147
OPTION C: A THYROGLOSSAL DUCT CYST IS A CONGENITAL MIDLINE NECK SWELLING THAT TYPICALLY PRESENTS
DURING CHILDHOOD OFTEN NOTICED AFTER AN UPPER RESPIRATORY INFECTION.
IT REPRESENTS THE PERSISTENCE OF THE TRACK OF THE THYROID GLAND AND CAN BE FOUND ADJACENT TO
THE MIDLINE. IT PRESENTS AS SMOOTH, FLUCTUANT (CYSTIC) SWELLING THAT IS OFTEN TRANSILLUMINANT.
CLASSICALLY, THE CYST MOVES UPWARDS ON SWALLOWING AND ON TONGUE PROTRUSION.
SISTRUNK’S OPERATION IS PERFORMED TO EXCISE THE CYST AND PREVENT A RECURRENCE.
