questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING NERVE IS LEAST INJURED DURING THYROID SURGERY?
questions.explanation:
THE MARGINAL MANDIBULAR NERVE IS LEAST LIKELY TO BE INJURED DURING THYROID SURGERY AS IT IS HIGH UP
(MANDIBULAR MARGIN) THAN THE DISSECTION PLANE OF THE APPROACH TO THYROID SURGERY.
OTHER NERVES THAT MIGHT BE AT RISK OF INJURY INCLUDE:
- RECURRENT LARYNGEAL NERVE MAY BE INJURED IF DISSECTION IS DONE BELOW THE CRICOID CARTILAGE OR NEAR
THE TRACHEOESOPHAGEAL GROOVE (OPTION A).
- ANSA CERVICALIS MAY BE INJURED IF STRAP MUSCLES ARE NOT CUT HIGH ENOUGH. (OPTION B)
- EXTERNAL LARYNGEAL NERVE MAY BE INJURED DURING LIGATION OF SUPERIOR THYROID VESSELS AS IT LIES VERY
CLOSE TO THE SUPERIOR THYROID ARTERY (OPTION C).
COMPLICATIONS OF THYROIDECTOMY:
- HEMORRHAGE - MOST COMMON COMPLICATION OVERALL; DUE TO SLIPPING OF LIGATURE
- NERVE INJURY
- EXTERNAL LARYNGEAL NERVE - HOARSENESS (MORE COMMON)
- RECURRENT LARYNGEAL NERVE - HOARSENESS IF UNILATERAL, LIFE-THREATENING ASPIRATION AND APHONIA IF
BILATERAL
4750
- RESPIRATORY OBSTRUCTION
- LARYNGEAL EDEMA - THE MOST COMMON CAUSE OF RESPIRATORY OBSTRUCTION
- BILATERAL RECURRENT LARYNGEAL NERVE PALSY
- LARYNGOMALACIA
- TENSION HEMATOMA
- HYPOPARATHYROIDISM - INFARCTION OF PARATHYROIDS
- THYROID STORM - INADEQUATELY PREPARED FOR SURGERY
- HYPOTHYROIDISM
- RECURRENT THYROTOXICOSIS
- WOUND INFECTION, STITCH GRANULOMA, KELOID.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: EFAST IS LEAST HELPFUL IN DIAGNOSING WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING CONDITIONS?
questions.explanation:
AMONG THE GIVEN OPTIONS, EFAST (FOCUSSED ASSESSMENT WITH SONOGRAPHY IN TRAUMA) IS THE LEAST
USEFUL IN DIAGNOSING RETROPERITONEAL HEMATOMA AS THE SENSITIVITY OF ULTRASOUND FOR THE DETECTION OF
RETROPERITONEAL HEMATOMAS IS EXTREMELY POOR.
COMPUTED TOMOGRAPHY (CT SCAN) IS THE INVESTIGATION OF CHOICE FOR RETROPERITONEAL INJURY, BUT IT
CAN ONLY BE DONE IN A HEMODYNAMICALLY STABLE PATIENT.
FAST STANDS FOR FOCUSSED ASSESSMENT WITH SONOGRAPHY FOR TRAUMA. IT IS A RAPID, NON-INVASIVE
BEDSIDE TEST FOR DETECTING FREE FLUID USING SONOGRAPHY USED TO ASSESS PATIENTS FOR POTENTIAL
THORACOABDOMINAL INJURIES.
TECHNIQUE:
- THE PATIENT IS PLACED IN A SUPINE POSITION AND THE FOLLOWING REGIONS ARE SCANNED:
- SUBXIPHOID TRANSVERSE VIEW: ASSESS FOR PERICARDIAL EFFUSION AND LEFT LOBE LIVER INJURIES
- LONGITUDINAL VIEW OF THE RIGHT UPPER QUADRANT: ASSESS FOR RIGHT LIVER INJURIES, RIGHT KIDNEY INJURY,
AND MORISON POUCH
- LONGITUDINAL VIEW OF THE LEFT UPPER QUADRANT: ASSESS FOR SPLENIC INJURY AND LEFT KIDNEY INJURY
- TRANSVERSE AND LONGITUDINAL VIEWS OF THE SUPRAPUBIC REGION: ASSESS THE BLADDER AND POUCH OF
DOUGLAS
EFAST STANDS FOR EXTENDED FAST AND INCORPORATES LEFT AND RIGHT THORACIC VIEWS TO ASSESS FOR
PNEUMOTHORAX AND HAEMOTHORAX.
LIMITATIONS OF EFAST ARE:
- OPERATOR-DEPENDENT
- BOWEL GAS AND SUBCUTANEOUS AIR DISTORT IMAGES.
- CAN MISS DIAPHRAGM, BOWEL, AND PANCREATIC INJURIES
- UNRELIABLE FOR ASSESSMENT OF THE RETROPERITONEUM
4751
- CANNOT RELIABLY EXCLUDE INJURY IN PENETRATING TRAUMA
- MAY NEED REPEATING OR SUPPLEMENTING WITH OTHER INVESTIGATIONS

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
A 23-YEAR-OLD MAN PRESENTED WITH BURN INJURY. HE IS COVERED WITH BURNS ON HIS HEAD &
NECK, BOTH UPPER LIMBS, FRONT AND BACK OF THE CHEST. CALCULATE THE PERCENTAGE OF BURNS.
questions.explanation:
THE PERCENTAGE OF BURNS CALCULATED IN THE GIVEN PATIENT IS 45% ACCORDING TO WALLACE’S RULE OF NINE.
CALCULATION:
- BURNS ON THE HEAD&NECK WOULD ACCOUNT FOR 9% OF BURNS.
- BURNS ON BOTH UPPER LIMBS (9% FOR EACH LIMB) WOULD ADD TO 18%
- BURNS ON BOTH SIDES OF THE CHEST WOULD ACCOUNT FOR 18%
THEREFORE THE TOTAL PERCENTAGE OF BURNS IN THE GIVEN PATIENT IS 9+18+18 = 45%

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: A PATIENT WITH UNILATERAL BREAST CANCER IS STARTED ON TAMOXIFEN. THIS WILL INCREASE THE RISK OF?
questions.explanation:
TAMOXIFEN INCREASES THE RISK OF ENDOMETRIAL CANCER BY 1-2%.
THE BENEFIT OF TAMOXIFEN IN BREAST CANCER OUTWEIGHS THE RISK OF ENDOMETRIAL CANCER.
TAMOXIFEN IS A SELECTIVE ESTROGEN RECEPTOR MODULATOR, APPROVED FOR THE TREATMENT OF ESTROGEN
RECEPTOR-POSITIVE (ER) BREAST CANCER. IT IS USED ONLY IN PREMENOPAUSAL WOMEN FOR 5 YEARS IN
LOW-RISK PATIENTS AND FOR 10 YEARS IN PATIENTS WITH A HIGH RISK OF RELAPSE (NODE-POSITIVE, TUMOR
>5 CM, LYMPHOVASCULAR INVASION). IT IS ALSO KNOWN TO REDUCE THE INCIDENCE OF SECOND PRIMARY
BREAST CANCER IN THE CONTRALATERAL BREAST.
TAMOXIFEN INCREASES THE RISK OF ENDOMETRIAL CANCER IN POSTMENOPAUSAL WOMEN; HENCE AROMATASE
INHIBITORS ARE USED IN POSTMENOPAUSAL WOMEN. TAMOXIFEN IS ALSO NOT RECOMMENDED IN PATIENTS
WHO HAVE HAD BILATERAL MASTECTOMIES WITH ER-POSITIVE DUCTAL CARCINOMA IN SITU. OTHER SIDE EFFECTS
OF TAMOXIFEN INCLUDE BONE PAIN, HOT FLASHES, NAUSEA, VOMITING, FLUID RETENTION AND RARELY
4753
THROMBOSIS AND CATARACT.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING IS THE MOST APPROPRIATE MESH FOR USE IN HERNIOPLASTY?
questions.explanation:
THE MOST APPROPRIATE MESH USED IN HERNIOPLASTY IS A LIGHTWEIGHT MESH WITH LARGE PORES.
LIGHTWEIGHT MESHES GENERALLY CONTAIN LESS MATERIAL AND INDUCE A LESS-PRONOUNCED FOREIGN BODY
REACTION AND DECREASED INFLAMMATORY RESPONSE, WHICH RESULTS IN BETTER TISSUE INCORPORATION,
INCREASED PROSTHESIS COMPLIANCE, AND DECREASED PATIENT DISCOMFORT AND PAIN.
MESHES WITH LARGE PORES EXHIBIT LESS INFLAMMATORY INFILTRATE, CONNECTIVE TISSUE, AND SCAR BRIDGING,
WHICH ALLOWS INCREASED SOFT TISSUE INGROWTH. THEY HAVE GREATER ELASTICITY AND FLEXIBILITY AND ALSO
SHRINK LESS RESULTING IN LESSER ADHESIONS, BETTER TISSUE INCORPORATION, AND DECREASED PATIENT
DISCOMFORT AND PAIN. SO THE BEST MESH TYPE AMONG THE GIVEN OPTIONS IS LIGHTWEIGHT MESH WITH
LARGE PORES.
MESHES USED IN HERNIOPLASTY CAN BE SYNTHETIC OR BIOLOGICAL DEPENDING ON THEIR COMPOSITION.
SYNTHETIC MESHES ARE MADE FROM POLYPROPYLENE, POLYESTER, OR PTFE (POLYTETRAFLUOROETHYLENE).
PTFE MESHES ARE HYDROPHOBIC WITH A LOWER RISK OF ADHESION.
BIOLOGICAL MESHES ARE ACELLULAR MATRIX MATERIALS DERIVED FROM HUMANS OR ANIMALS AND HAVE LESSER
COMPLICATIONS. BUT DUE TO POOR COLLAGEN DEPOSITION AND ABSORPTION, THEY RAPIDLY LOSE MECHANICAL
STRENGTH AND HENCE THEIR USE IS RESTRICTED TO INFECTED ENVIRONMENTS.
NOTE: TO PROMOTE BETTER TISSUE INTEGRATION, A COMPOSITE MESH WAS DEVELOPED WHICH COMBINES THE
ATTRIBUTES OF POLYPROPYLENE AND PTFE BY LAYERING THE TWO SUBSTANCES ON TOP OF ONE ANOTHER.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
A 30-YEAR-OLD TEACHER UNDERWENT PAROTIDECTOMY FOLLOWING WHICH SHE DEVELOPED LOWER LIP
PARALYSIS. THIS PROBABLY OCCURRED BECAUSE OF AN INJURY TO WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING STRUCTURES?
options: BUCCAL BRANCH OF THE FACIAL NERVE
questions.explanation:
LOWER LIP PARALYSIS OCCURS WHEN THERE IS AN INJURY TO THE MARGINAL MANDIBULAR BRANCH OF THE FACIAL
NERVE.
BRANCHES OF THE FACIAL NERVE ARE:
- TEMPORAL
- ZYGOMATIC
- BUCCAL
4754
- MARGINAL MANDIBULAR
- CERVICAL
THE FACIAL NERVE PASSES THROUGH THE PAROTID GLAND, HENCE IT MIGHT BE INJURED DURING
PAROTIDECTOMY.
IN CONTRAST TO THIS, THE UPPER LIP IS SUPPLIED BY BUCCAL BRANCHES OF THE FACIAL NERVE.
COMPLICATIONS OF PAROTIDECTOMY INCLUDE HEMATOMA FORMATION, INFECTION, DEFORMITY (UNSIGHTLY
SCARRING AND RETROMANDIBULAR HOLLOWING), TEMPORARY/PERMANENT FACIAL WEAKNESS, SIALOCELE, FACIAL
NUMBNESS, PERMANENT NUMBNESS OF THE EARLOBE DUE TO GREAT AURICULAR NERVE TRANSECTION AND
FREY'S SYNDROME.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING IS NOT AN ADVERSE EFFECT SEEN AFTER A MASSIVE BLOOD TRANSFUSION?
questions.explanation:
HYPERCALCEMIA IS NOT AN ADVERSE EFFECT OF MASSIVE BLOOD TRANSFUSION.
MASSIVE BLOOD TRANSFUSION INSTEAD LEADS TO HYPOCALCEMIA AS THE ANTICOAGULANT CITRATE BINDS TO
CALCIUM. THE LETHAL TRIAD OF MASSIVE BLOOD TRANSFUSION IS ACIDOSIS, HYPOTHERMIA, AND COAGULOPATHY.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING GENE MUTATIONS ARE INVOLVED IN CARCINOMA OF THE COLON?
questions.explanation:
APC, K-RAS, AND P53 GENE MUTATIONS ARE IMPLICATED IN CARCINOMA OF THE COLON.
IN THE ADENOMA TO CARCINOMA SEQUENCE, THE LOSS OF ONE NORMAL COPY OF THE TUMOR SUPPRESSOR GENE
APC IS THE FIRST HIT, FOLLOWED BY THE LOSS OF THE INTACT SECOND COPY OF THE APC GENE (SECOND HIT).
OTHER CHANGES IN THE SEQUENCE INCLUDE THE MUTATION OF K-RAS AND THE INACTIVATION OF THE TUMOR
SUPPRESSOR GENE P53, LEADING TO THE EMERGENCE OF CARCINOMA. THE ACCUMULATION OF THESE
MUTATIONS IS MORE IMPORTANT THAN THEIR OCCURRENCE IN A SPECIFIC ORDER. THIS IS KNOWN AS THE
FEARON-VOGELSTEIN ADENOMA-CARCINOMA MULTISTEP MODEL OF COLORECTAL NEOPLASIA.
4755
A NUMBER OF OTHER GENES ON CHROMOSOME 18Q ARE IMPLICATED IN COLORECTAL CANCER, INCLUDING
SMAD2, SMAD4, AND DCC.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: WHICH AMONG THE FOLLOWING IS CORRECT REGARDING ADEQUATE THYROID FNAC SAMPLING?
questions.explanation:
6 FOLLICULAR CLUSTERS EACH WITH 10 CELLS ARE CONSIDERED ADEQUATE THYROID FNAC SAMPLING.
THERE ARE DIFFERENT CRITERIA FOR THE ADEQUACY OF THYROID FNAC:
- SIX GROUPS WITH AT LEAST 10 CELLS IN EACH GROUP, OR
- TEN GROUPS WITH AT LEAST 20 CELLS IN EACH GROUP, ARE CONSIDERED ADEQUATE.
CYSTIC GOITRE MAY NOT YIELD THYROID FOLLICULAR CELLS, HENCE, THE ASPIRATION SHOULD BE REPEATED UNDER
USG GUIDANCE.
FNAC IS THE INVESTIGATION OF CHOICE IN DISCRETE THYROID SWELLINGS; IT HAS EXCELLENT PATIENT
COMPLIANCE, SIMPLE AND QUICK TO PERFORM IN THE OUTPATIENT DEPARTMENT AND IS READILY REPEATED.
BETHESDA CRITERIA FOR REPORTING THYROID CYTOPATHOLOGY:
4756

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING ARE USED TO STOP ESOPHAGEAL VARICEAL BLEED?
questions.explanation:
ALL THE GIVEN OPTIONS CAN BE USED TO STOP ESOPHAGEAL VARICEAL BLEEDING.
IMAGE A SHOWS THE SENGSTAKEN-BLAKEMORE TUBE. IT HAS 3 LUMENS - ONE ASPIRATION PORT AND 2
INFLATION BALLOONS. THEY ARE:
- GASTRIC ASPIRATION PORT
- GASTRIC BALLOON PORT
- ESOPHAGEAL BALLOON PORT
THE GASTRIC BALLOON IS INFLATED AND TENSION IS APPLIED TO THE GASTROESOPHAGEAL JUNCTION. IF THIS DOES
NOT CONTROL THE HAEMORRHAGE, THE ESOPHAGEAL BALLOON IS INFLATED AS WELL, COMPRESSING THE VENOUS
PLEXUS BETWEEN THEM. ONLY GASTRIC CONTENTS CAN BE ASPIRATED.
4757
IMAGE B SHOWS THE MINNESOTA TUBE. IT HAS 4 OPENINGS - 2 INFLATION TUBES AND 2 SUCTION TUBES I.E.
BOTH GASTRIC AND OESOPHAGEAL ASPIRATION PORTS ARE PRESENT, WHICH ALLOWS THE ASPIRATION OF BOTH
GASTRIC AND ESOPHAGEAL CONTENTS.
IMAGES C AND D BOTH SHOW AN UPPER GI ENDOSCOPE. THEY ARE USED TO IDENTIFY THE SOURCE OF
BLEEDING AND ONCE IDENTIFIED, SCLEROTHERAPY AND ENDOSCOPIC VARICEAL BANDING ARE PERFORMED, WHICH
HAVE BEEN SHOWN TO CONTROL HEMORRHAGE EFFECTIVELY.
BANDING HAS A LOWER RATE OF COMPLICATIONS. IF BLEEDING DOES NOT STOP BY BANDING/SCLEROTHERAPY,
BALLOON TAMPONADE SHOULD BE TRIED.
THE PROTOCOL FOR THE MANAGEMENT OF ESOPHAGEAL VARICES IS GIVEN BELOW.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
A 25-YEAR-OLD MALE PATIENT WAS BROUGHT TO THE ER AFTER RTA, HIS RR IS 25/MIN, BP IS
80/45MMHG. ON EXAMINATION, HYPER-RESONANCE IS HEARD OVER THE LEFT SIDE OF THE CHEST. THE
CHEST X-RAY PERFORMED IS GIVEN BELOW. WHAT WOULD BE THE APPROPRIATE MANAGEMENT IN THIS
CASE?
options: WIDE BORE NEEDLE INSERTION IN THE 5TH INTERCOSTAL SPACE (ICS)
WIDE BORE NEEDLE INSERTION IN THE 5TH ICS FOLLOWED BY AN INTERCOSTAL DRAIN IN THE 5TH ICS
questions.answer: WIDE BORE NEEDLE INSERTION IN THE 5TH ICS FOLLOWED BY AN INTERCOSTAL DRAIN IN THE 5TH ICS
questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN CLINICAL SCENARIO OF HEMODYNAMIC INSTABILITY, HYPER-RESONANCE ON THE LEFT SIDE OF THE
CHEST, AND THE X-RAY FINDINGS ARE SUGGESTIVE OF TENSION PNEUMOTHORAX. IT IS MANAGED BY INSERTING A
WIDE-BORE NEEDLE IN THE 5TH INTERCOSTAL SPACE (ICS) FOLLOWED BY PLACING AN INTERCOSTAL DRAIN IN THE
5TH ICS.
TRAUMATIC PNEUMOTHORAX CAN BE:
- SIMPLE PNEUMOTHORAX: WITHOUT HEMODYNAMIC INSTABILITY
- TENSION PNEUMOTHORAX: WITH HEMODYNAMIC INSTABILITY
THE X-RAY GIVEN BELOW IS SHOWING A LEFT-SIDED TENSION PNEUMOTHORAX. A LARGE, WELL-DEMARCATED
AREA IS DEVOID OF LUNG MARKINGS ON THE LEFT SIDE. THE YELLOW ARROWS ARE POINTING TO THE TRACHEAL
DEVIATION AND THE MEDIASTINAL SHIFT TO THE RIGHT SIDE.
4758
MANAGEMENT:
- SIMPLE PNEUMOTHORAX: TUBE THORACOSTOMY OR CHEST TUBE INSERTION IN THE 5TH ICS IN THE TRIANGLE
OF SAFETY
- TENSION PNEUMOTHORAX:
- IMMEDIATE MANAGEMENT: URGENT NEEDLE DECOMPRESSION OR NEEDLE THORACOSTOMY I.E. INSERTION OF
A WIDE-BORE NEEDLE IN THE 5TH ICS, ANTERIOR TO THE MIDAXILLARY LINE
- DEFINITIVE MANAGEMENT: TUBE THORACOSTOMY OR CHEST TUBE INSERTION IN THE 5TH ICS IN THE TRIANGLE
OF SAFETY
NOTE: ACCORDING TO ATLS 10TH EDITION
- IN ADULTS, NEEDLE THORACOSTOMY OR NEEDLE DECOMPRESSION LOCATION IS CHANGED TO 5TH ICS ANTERIOR
TO THE MIDAXILLARY LINE FROM 2ND ICS MIDCLAVICULAR LINE.
- IN THE PEDIATRIC AGE GROUP, THE NEEDLE THORACOSTOMY LOCATION REMAINS AT THE 2ND ICS
MIDCLAVICULAR LINE.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
A PATIENT PRESENTS WITH PAIN IN THE RIGHT UPPER QUADRANT ON THE SECOND POSTOPERATIVE DAY
FOLLOWING A CHOLECYSTECTOMY. EVALUATION REVEALS A COLLECTION IN THE SUBHEPATIC SPACE. A BILE
LEAK WAS SUSPECTED. WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING IS THE BEST INVESTIGATION FOR THIS PATIENT?
questions.explanation:
ENDOSCOPIC RETROGRADE CHOLANGIOPANCREATOGRAPHY (ERCP) IS THE BEST INVESTIGATION IN A PATIENT
SUSPECTED OF POST-CHOLECYSTECTOMY BILIARY LEAKS.
PATIENTS WITH POST-CHOLECYSTECTOMY BILIARY LEAK USUALLY PRESENT WITH FEVER, JAUNDICE AND
ABDOMINAL PAIN. USG IS USED FOR AN INITIAL EVALUATION IN SUCH CASES AND CAN SHOW A COLLECTION IN
THE SUB-HEPATIC SPACE.
THE MOST COMMON BILE LEAK FOLLOWING CHOLECYSTECTOMY IS FROM THE CYSTIC DUCT. THIS CAN BE TREATED
BY PLACING A BILIARY ENDOPROSTHESIS (STENT) IN THE COMMON BILE DUCT ACROSS THE ORIGIN OF THE CYSTIC
DUCT.
4759
MRCP SHOWS FLUID COLLECTIONS ARISING FROM BILE LEAKS BUT CANNOT DIFFERENTIATE THESE FROM OTHER
CAUSES OF FLUID COLLECTIONS.
ERCP IS THE BEST INVESTIGATION AS IT HAS THE ADVANTAGE OF BEING BOTH DIAGNOSTIC AND
THERAPEUTIC. ERCP IS USEFUL POST-CHOLECYSTECTOMY AS THERE IS A HIGH LIKELIHOOD OF A RETAINED STONE
AND STONE EXTRACTION AND/OR TEMPORARY STENTING MAY BE REQUIRED.
HIDA SCAN IS THE MOST SENSITIVE INVESTIGATION FOR BILIARY LEAKAGE.
CT SCAN CAN SHOW FOCAL FLUID COLLECTIONS, ASCITES, BILIARY OBSTRUCTION, HEPATIC ATROPHY, SIGNS OF
SECONDARY BILIARY CIRRHOSIS AND ANY VASCULAR INJURY.

DIABETIC NEUROPATHY, B12 DEFICIENCY, ALCOHOLISM, HYPOTHYROIDISM, LEPROSY, PERIPHERAL NERVE INJURY,
TRANSVERSE MYELITIS AND MYELOMENINGOCELE.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
A 35-YEAR-OLD CHRONIC SMOKER PRESENTS WITH BLUISH DISCOLORATION OF THE TOE ALONG WITH
INTERMITTENT CLAUDICATION. WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING WILL BE THE NEXT APPROPRIATE INVESTIGATION IN
THIS PATIENT?
questions.explanation:
CHRONIC SMOKER PRESENTING WITH BLUISH DISCOLORATION OF THE TOE ALONG WITH INTERMITTENT
CLAUDICATION IS SUGGESTIVE OF PERIPHERAL ARTERIAL DISEASE AND DUPLEX SCANNING WILL BE THE NEXT
APPROPRIATE INVESTIGATION.
DUPLEX SCANNING IS A MAJOR NON-INVASIVE TECHNIQUE THAT USES B-MODE ULTRASOUND TO PROVIDE AN
IMAGE OF THE VESSEL. MOST SCANNERS NOW HAVE COLOR CODING, WHICH ALLOWS DETAILED VISUALIZATION OF
BLOOD FLOW IN A VESSEL. DIFFERENT COLORS INDICATE CHANGES IN THE DIRECTION AND VELOCITY OF FLOW, WITH
AREAS OF HIGH FLOW USUALLY INDICATING STENOTIC LESIONS.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION A: CT ANGIOGRAPHY (CTA) IS MORE USEFUL IN THE EVALUATION OF VISCERAL ARTERIAL DISEASE (EG.
MESENTERIC ISCHEMIA). IT CAN BE BENEFICIAL IN PERIPHERAL ARTERY DISEASES WHERE A DUPLEX SCAN SHOWS
POOR IMAGES (AORTOILIAC SEGMENT INVOLVEMENT). CTA IS NOT ROUTINELY RECOMMENDED IN PERIPHERAL
ARTERY DISEASE BECAUSE OF CONCOMITANT RENAL DYSFUNCTION IN THESE PATIENTS WHICH CAN LEAD TO
CONTRAST-INDUCED NEPHROPATHY.
OPTION B: MR ANGIOGRAPHY IS TIME-CONSUMING AND EXPENSIVE, HENCE NOT DONE AS THE NEXT
INVESTIGATION. IT IS CONTRAINDICATED IN PATIENTS WITH CLAUSTROPHOBIA AND METALLIC IMPLANTS.
OPTION C: DIGITAL SUBTRACTION ANGIOGRAPHY (DSA) IS AN INVASIVE AND EXPENSIVE
PROCEDURE COMPARED TO OTHER INVESTIGATIONS. THE BENEFITS OF DSA ARE THAT IT PROVIDES DYNAMIC
ARTERIAL FLOW INFORMATION AND CAN BE COMBINED WITH A DEFINITIVE ENDOVASCULAR INTERVENTION WHEN
INDICATED. DSA IS INDICATED ONLY WHEN THERE IS A DISCREPANCY IN DIAGNOSIS OR INTERVENTION IS
PLANNED. COMPLICATIONS ASSOCIATED WITH DSA INCLUDE BLEEDING, HEMATOMA, FALSE ANEURYSM
FORMATION, THROMBOSIS, ARTERIAL DISSECTION, DISTAL EMBOLISATION, RENAL DYSFUNCTION, AND ALLERGIC
REACTION.
4763

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
A 40-YEAR-OLD WOMAN PRESENTS WITH COMPLAINTS OF SWELLING OF THE RIGHT BREAST OVER THE PAST 15
DAYS. ON EXAMINATION, THERE WAS LOCAL RISE OF TEMPERATURE, AND THE SWELLING WAS MOBILE OVER
THE CHEST WALL. WHAT IS THE LIKELY DIAGNOSIS?
questions.explanation:
IN THE GIVEN SCENARIO, THE RAPID ONSET OF THE DISEASE AND THE EXAMINATION FINDINGS ARE SUGGESTIVE
OF INFLAMMATORY CARCINOMA OF THE BREAST.
INFLAMMATORY BREAST CANCER IS THE MOST AGGRESSIVE SUBTYPE OF BREAST CANCER. IT MIMICS ACUTE
MASTITIS. THE HALLMARK OF INFLAMMATORY BREAST CARCINOMA IS THE DIFFUSE TUMOR INVOLVEMENT OF THE
DERMAL LYMPHATICS WITHIN THE BREAST AND THE OVERLYING SKIN, OFTEN WITHOUT A DISCRETE UNDERLYING
TUMOR MASS (PEAU D' ORANGE APPEARANCE). THE PATIENT PRESENTS WITH RAPIDLY PROGRESSIVE SWELLING OF
THE BREAST, WARMTH, ERYTHEMA AND EDEMA. A BREAST LUMP MAY OR MAY NOT BE PRESENT.
A DIAGNOSIS OF INFLAMMATORY BREAST CARCINOMA SHOULD BE SUSPECTED WHEN A PATIENT WITH RAPIDLY
PROGRESSIVE SWELLING WITH INFLAMMATORY SKIN CHANGES DOES NOT RESPOND TO ANTIBIOTICS. THE IMAGING
FEATURES WITH ULTRASOUND AND A MAMMOGRAPH IS NON-SPECIFIC DUE TO THE UNDERLYING ERYTHEMA AND
EDEMA. A BIOPSY SHOULD BE DONE TO CONFIRM THE DIAGNOSIS.
TREATMENT INCLUDES COMBINED-MODALITY TREATMENT:
- NEOADJUVANT CHEMOTHERAPY
- MASTECTOMY
- RADIATION THERAPY
- HORMONAL THERAPY- FOR ER-POSITIVE TUMORS
- TRASTUZUMAB FOR HER-2-POSITIVE TUMORS
OPTION B: GIANT FIBROADENOMAS OCCASIONALLY OCCUR DURING PUBERTY. THESE ARE BENIGN SOLID
ENCAPSULATED SLOW-GROWING TUMORS OVER 5 CM IN DIAMETER. IT PRESENTS AS A PAINLESS LUMP IN THE
BREAST. THEY ARE MANAGED BY EXCISION VIA A SUBMAMMARY INCISION.
OPTION C: PHYLLODES TUMORS USUALLY OCCUR IN WOMEN OVER THE AGE OF 40 YEARS BUT CAN APPEAR IN
YOUNGER WOMEN. PHYLLODES TUMOR IS MOSTLY BENIGN EVEN THOUGH IT IS ALSO CALLED CYSTOSARCOMA
PHYLLODES. IT PRESENTS AS A LARGE TUMOR WITH AN UNEVENLY BOSSELATED SURFACE. THEY ARE USUALLY
4764
MOBILE OVER THE CHEST WALL DESPITE THEIR LARGE SIZE. THIS TUMOR DOES NOT INFILTRATE THE SKIN. NIPPLE
RETRACTION IS NOT SEEN IN THIS CONDITION. BENIGN LESIONS CAN BE TREATED WITH ENUCLEATION OR WIDE
LOCAL EXCISION. MASSIVE TUMOURS, RECURRENT TUMOURS AND MALIGNANT LESIONS ARE TREATED WITH A
MASTECTOMY.
OPTION D: GALACTOCELE ARE THE MOST COMMON BENIGN BREAST LESIONS IN LACTATING WOMEN. IT IS A
CYSTIC ENLARGEMENT OF THE MAMMARY GLAND CONTAINING MILK. THEY ARE MOSTLY DETECTED DURING
LACTATION OR IN THE THIRD TRIMESTER OF PREGNANCY BUT RARELY, MAY ALSO PRESENT AFTER STOPPING
BREASTFEEDING. CLINICALLY, THE MASS IS USUALLY FIRM AND NON-TENDER AND PRESENTS AS A SOLID
TUMOUR-LIKE LESION ON PHYSICAL EXAMINATION. THE PATIENT USUALLY NOTES THE
LESION DURING LACTATION OR SOME PERIOD AFTER LACTATION. NEEDLE ASPIRATION, FOLLOWED
BY EXCISION SHOULD IT RECUR, IS THE STANDARD METHOD OF TREATING GALACTOCELE.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
A MIDDLE-AGED MAN PRESENTS WITH PROGRESSIVE DIFFICULTY IN SWALLOWING FOR BOTH SOLIDS AND
LIQUIDS FOR 8 MONTHS. BARIUM SWALLOW DONE IS SHOWN BELOW. WHAT OTHER INVESTIGATIONS NEED
TO BE DONE IN THIS PATIENT?
options: UPPER GI ENDOSCOPY AND 24 HOUR PH MONITORING
questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN CLINICAL SCENARIO AND THE BARIUM SWALLOW SHOWING A BIRD BEAK APPEARANCE ARE SUGGESTIVE
OF ACHALASIA CARDIA.
ACHALASIA IS A PRIMARY ESOPHAGEAL MOTILITY DISORDER CHARACTERIZED BY THE ABSENCE
OF ESOPHAGEAL PERISTALSIS AND IMPAIRED RELAXATION OF THE LOWER ESOPHAGEAL SPHINCTER (LES) IN
RESPONSE TO SWALLOWING.
MANOMETRY IS CONSIDERED THE MOST SENSITIVE INVESTIGATION TO DIAGNOSE ACHALASIA AS IT IDENTIFIES
EARLY DISEASE BEFORE ESOPHAGEAL DILATATION AND FOOD RETENTION. THE DIAGNOSTIC CRITERIA FOR ACHALASIA
WITH MANOMETRY ARE IMPAIRED LOWER ESOPHAGEAL SPHINCTER (LES) RELAXATION AND ABSENT
PERISTALSIS WITH AN ELEVATED LES PRESSURE.
ENDOSCOPY IS USEFUL FOR RULING OUT PSEUDO-ACHALASIA.
NOTE: 24-HOUR PH MONITORING IS IDEAL AND MOST ACCURATE IN PATIENTS WITH THE FEATURES OF
GASTROESOPHAGEAL REFLUX DISEASE.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
A 55-YEAR-OLD MAN WITH IHD PRESENTS WITH SUDDEN, SEVERE, GENERALIZED ABDOMINAL PAIN AND
MULTIPLE EPISODES OF VOMITING. ON EXAMINATION, THE PULSE RATE IS 118BPM, RHYTHM IS
IRREGULARLY IRREGULAR, BP IS 90/60 MMHG. THE ABDOMEN APPEARS SOFT, NON-DISTENDED, AND
BOWEL SOUNDS ARE ABSENT. WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING COULD BE A LIKELY DIAGNOSIS IN THIS CASE?
questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN CLINICAL SCENARIO OF A PATIENT WITH SUDDEN ONSET SEVERE ABDOMINAL PAIN WHICH IS
OUT-OF-PROPORTION TO THE PHYSICAL EXAMINATION FINDINGS ALONG WITH ATRIAL FIBRILLATION IS SUGGESTIVE OF
ACUTE MESENTERIC ISCHEMIA.
MESENTERIC ISCHEMIA MAY BE ACUTE OR CHRONIC. THE SUPERIOR MESENTERIC ARTERY (SMA) IS MOST LIKELY
AFFECTED. AN EMBOLUS IS THE MOST COMMON CAUSE OF SMA OCCLUSION. POSSIBLE SOURCES FOR SMA
EMBOISATION INCLUDE:
- LEFT ATRIUM IN ATRIAL FIBRILLATION
- PREVIOUS HISTORY OF ISCHEMIC HEART DISEASE/MYOCARDIAL INFARCTION
- VEGETATIONS ON MITRAL AND AORTIC VALVES ASSOCIATED WITH ENDOCARDITIS
- AN ATHEROMATOUS PLAQUE FROM AN AORTIC ANEURYSM.
OTHER CAUSES OF MESENTERIC ISCHEMIA INCLUDE:
4765
- ATHEROSCLEROSIS OF MESENTERIC VESSELS
- VASCULITIDES
- VENOUS THROMBOSIS IN FACTOR V LEIDEN MUTATION
- NON-OCCLUSIVE MESENTERIC ISCHEMIA DUE TO ALTERATIONS IN SPLANCHNIC BLOOD FLOW.
THE MOST IMPORTANT CLUE TO AN EARLY DIAGNOSIS OF ACUTE MESENTERIC ISCHEMIA IS THE SUDDEN ONSET
OF SEVERE ABDOMINAL PAIN IN A PATIENT WITH ATRIAL FIBRILLATION OR ATHEROSCLEROSIS. THE PAIN IS
TYPICALLY IN THE CENTRAL ABDOMEN AND OUT OF PROPORTION TO THE PHYSICAL FINDINGS.
ASSOCIATED CLINICAL FEATURES INCLUDE NAUSEA, VOMITING, DIARRHEA, ABDOMINAL DISTENSION, PERITONITIS,
AND THE PASSAGE OF BLOODY STOOLS.
THE GOLD STANDARD FOR THE DIAGNOSIS OF ACUTE MESENTERIC ISCHEMIA IS ANGIOGRAPHY, AND
MANAGEMENT IS LAPAROTOMY. THE GOAL OF OPERATIVE EXPLORATION IS TO RESECT THE COMPROMISED
BOWEL AND RESTORE BLOOD SUPPLY VIA EMBOLECTOMY.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION B: A PULSATILE ABDOMINAL MASS IS SEEN IN THE CASE OF AN ABDOMINAL AORTIC ANEURYSM. ACUTE
PAIN AND HYPOTENSION OCCUR WITH RUPTURE OF THE ANEURYSM, WHICH REQUIRES AN EMERGENCY
OPERATION.
OPTIONS A AND D: ACUTE SEVERE PANCREATITIS AND PEPTIC ULCER PERFORATION HAVE NO ASSOCIATION WITH
ATRIAL FIBRILLATION. THEY USUALLY PRESENT WITH PAIN OVER THE UPPER ABDOMEN ASSOCIATED WITH
GUARDING AND RIGIDITY ON EXAMINATION.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
A 15-YEAR-OLD GIRL PRESENTED WITH A SLOW-GROWING, RUBBERY, NON-TENDER SWELLING ON THE SIDE OF
THE NECK AS SHOWN IN THE IMAGE. EXAMINATION SHOWS THE PRESENCE OF FRECKLES AND SKIN PATCHES
OVER THE FACE AND TRUNK. WHAT IS THE MOST LIKELY DIAGNOSIS?
questions.explanation:
A LATERAL NECK MASS IN A PEDIATRIC PATIENT, WHICH IS NON-TENDER AND PRESENT IN ASSOCIATION
WITH FRECKLES, AND HYPERPIGMENTED SKIN PATCHES (CAFE-AU-LAIT SPOTS) IS SUGGESTIVE OF NEURAL TUMOR
I.E. NEUROFIBROMA.
NEUROFIBROMA IS A BENIGN TUMOR ARISING FROM THE CONNECTIVE TISSUE OF THE NERVE CONTAINING
ECTODERMAL, NEURAL AND MESODERMAL CONNECTIVE TISSUE COMPONENTS. IT CAN BE SINGLE OR MULTIPLE. IT
IS THE MOST COMMON INTRADURAL EXTRAMEDULLARY SPINAL TUMOR. NEUROFIBROMAS CAN BE LOCAL,
GENERALIZED (VON RECKLINGHAUSEN'S DISEASE) OR PLEXIFORM TYPES. PATIENTS PRESENT WITH MILD PAIN OR
A PAINLESS SWELLING USUALLY IN THE SUBCUTANEOUS OR CUTANEOUS PLANE WITH TINGLING, NUMBNESS AND
PARAESTHESIA ALONG THE DISTRIBUTION OF THE NERVE. COMPLICATIONS OF NEUROFIBROMA INCLUDE CYSTIC
DEGENERATION, EROSION INTO DEEPER PLANES, CORD COMPRESSION AND PARALYSIS (SPINAL NEUROFIBROMA)
AND SARCOMATOUS CHANGES.
TREATMENT IS EXCISION UNDER GENERAL OR REGIONAL ANESTHESIA. INDICATIONS FOR SURGERY IN
NEUROFIBROMA INCLUDE SYMPTOMATIC PATIENTS (PAIN AND PRESSURE SYMPTOMS), COSMETIC PROBLEMS
AND MALIGNANT TRANSFORMATION (5%).
OPTION A: CYSTIC HYGROMA IS A TYPE OF CONGENITAL LYMPHANGIOMA. THIS SWELLING IS SOFT AND PARTIALLY
COMPRESSIBLE, WHICH SHOWS POSITIVE FLUCTUATION AND TRANSLUCENCY TEST.
OPTION B: CHEMODECTOMA OR CAROTID BODY TUMOR IS A RARE TUMOR, MOST COMMONLY PRESENT IN THE
FIFTH DECADE AND THERE IS AN ASSOCIATION WITH PHEOCHROMOCYTOMA. THESE PATIENTS USUALLY PRESENT
WITH A SLOWLY ENLARGING, PAINLESS LUMP AT THE CAROTID BIFURCATION.
4766
OPTION D: A LIPOMA IS A SOFT PAINLESS SWELLING. IT SHOWS THE CHARACTERISTIC SLIP SIGN AND IS FREELY
MOBILE.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: WHAT WILL BE THE MOST LIKELY ASSOCIATED CONDITION WITH INCREASED TSH AND LOW T4 LEVELS?
questions.explanation:
INCREASED TSH AND LOW T4 LEVELS ARE SEEN IN PRIMARY HYPOTHYROIDISM. HASHIMOTO'S THYROIDITIS IS
THE ONLY CAUSE OF PRIMARY HYPOTHYROIDISM IN THE GIVEN OPTIONS.
HASHIMOTO'S THYROIDITIS IS AN AUTOIMMUNE DISEASE THAT RESULTS IN THE DESTRUCTION OF THE THYROID
GLAND AND GRADUAL & PROGRESSIVE THYROID FAILURE. IT IS THE MOST COMMON CAUSE OF PRIMARY
HYPOTHYROIDISM IN IODINE-SUFFICIENT AREAS. THEY ALSO HAVE AUTOANTIBODIES AGAINST THYROID
RECEPTORS, THYROID PEROXIDASE AND THYROGLOBULIN.
OTHER OPTIONS:
4768
OPTION A: HYPOPARATHYROIDISM IS GENERALLY NOT ASSOCIATED WITH HYPOTHYROIDISM, EXCEPT IN CERTAIN
CONGENITAL MULTISYSTEM DISORDERS SUCH AS DIGEORGE'S SYNDROME.
OPTION C: GRAVE'S DISEASE IS THE MOST COMMON CAUSE OF HYPERTHYROIDISM. IT IS AN AUTOIMMUNE
DISORDER CAUSED DUE TO AUTOANTIBODIES AGAINST THE TSH RECEPTOR. THERE WILL BE ELEVATED T3 AND T4
LEVELS WITH LOW TSH LEVELS.
OPTION B: A TSH-PRODUCING PITUITARY ADENOMA CAN HAVE INCREASED TSH LEVELS, BUT THERE WILL BE
ELEVATED T3, T4 LEVELS AS WELL.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: IN E-FAST WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING BODY PART IS INCLUDED THAT IS NOT INCLUDED IN FAST?
questions.explanation:
E-FAST IS USED TO ADDITIONALLY ASSESS THE PRESENCE OF FREE FLUID IN THE THORACIC CAVITY.
FAST STANDS FOR FOCUSED ASSESSMENT WITH SONOGRAPHY FOR TRAUMA. IT IS A RAPID DIAGNOSTIC
EXAMINATION TO ASSESS PATIENTS WITH POTENTIAL THORACOABDOMINAL INJURIES. IT CAN BE PERFORMED
WITHIN 2-4 MINUTES.
THE SEQUENTIAL ORDER IN WHICH FAST IS PERFORMED: PERICARDIAL SAC, THE RIGHT UPPER QUADRANT
(RUQ), LEFT UPPER QUADRANT (LUQ), AND PELVIS. 4 ‘PS’ ARE EVALUATED IN SEQUENCE: PERICARDIAL SAC →
PERIHEPATIC REGION → PERISPLENIC REGION → PELVIS.
TECHNIQUE:
- FOLLOWING REGIONS ARE SCANNED:
- SUBXIPHOID: ASSESS FOR PERICARDIAL EFFUSION AND LEFT LOBE LIVER INJURIES
- RIGHT UPPER QUADRANT: ASSESS FOR RIGHT LIVER INJURIES, RIGHT KIDNEY INJURY, AND MORISON POUCH
- LEFT UPPER QUADRANT: ASSESS FOR SPLENIC INJURY AND LEFT KIDNEY INJURY
- SUPRAPUBIC REGION: ASSESS THE BLADDER AND POUCH OF DOUGLAS
AN 'EXTENDED FAST OR EFAST' SCAN MAY BE PERFORMED: LEFT AND RIGHT THORACIC VIEWS TO ASSESS FOR
PNEUMOTHORAX AND HEMOTHORAX.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
ACCORDING TO STRASBERG’S CLASSIFICATION OF BILE DUCT INJURIES, INJURY TO THE RIGHT ABERRANT
POSTERIOR SECTORAL DUCT WITH BILE LEAK IS:
questions.explanation:
INJURY TO THE RIGHT ABERRANT POSTERIOR SECTORAL DUCT ASSOCIATED WITH BILE LEAK IS CLASSIFIED
AS STRASBERG’S TYPE C INJURY.
BILIARY INJURY MAY OCCUR POST-LAPAROSCOPIC CHOLECYSTECTOMY. THE MOST COMMON SITE OF BILE LEAK
FOLLOWING CHOLECYSTECTOMY IS THE CYSTIC DUCT.
MRCP IS THE GOLD STANDARD FOR COMPLETE MORPHOLOGICAL EVALUATION OF THE BILIARY TREE. MRCP WITH
MAGNETIC RESONANCE ANGIOGRAPHY IS MORE USEFUL IN CASES OF ASSOCIATED VASCULAR INJURY. A HIDA
SCAN CAN CONFIRM THE PRESENCE OF A BILE LEAK OR BILIARY OBSTRUCTION.
THE STRASBERG CLASSIFICATION OF BILE DUCT INJURY IS WIDELY USED TO ANATOMICALLY DEFINE BILE DUCT
INJURIES.
CLASSIFICATION
4769
- TYPE A: BILE LEAK FROM CYSTIC DUCT STUMP OR A MINOR BILIARY RADICAL IN THE GALLBLADDER FOSSA
- TYPE B: OCCLUDED RIGHT POSTERIOR SECTORAL DUCT.
- TYPE C: BILE LEAK FROM THE DIVIDED RIGHT POSTERIOR SECTORAL DUCT.
- TYPE D: BILE LEAK FROM THE MAIN BILE DUCT WITHOUT MAJOR TISSUE LOSS.
- TYPE E: INJURY TO THE MAIN HEPATIC DUCT; CLASSIFIED ACCORDING TO THE LEVEL OF INJURY
- E1: TRANSECTED MAIN BILE DUCT WITH A STRICTURE MORE THAN 2CM FROM THE HILUS.
- E2: TRANSECTED MAIN BILE DUCT WITH A STRICTURE LESS THAN 2CM FROM THE HILUS
- E3: STRICTURE OF THE HILUS WITH RIGHT AND LEFT DUCTS IN COMMUNICATION.
- E4: STRICTURE OF THE HILUS WITH SEPARATION OF RIGHT AND LEFT HEPATIC DUCTS.
- E5: STRICTURE OF THE RIGHT ABERRANT SECTORAL AND MAIN BILE DUCTS.
MANAGEMENT OF BILE DUCT INJURIES IS SHOWN BELOW:
4770

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
A BUS CONDUCTOR WAS DIAGNOSED WITH VARICOSE VEINS. ON EXAMINATION, SKIN ECZEMA AND
LIPODERMATOSCLEROSIS WERE NOTED. ACCORDING TO THE CEAP CLASSIFICATION SYSTEM, HE WOULD BE
CLASSIFIED AS
questions.explanation:
ACCORDING TO CEAP CLASSIFICATION, VARICOSE VEINS WITH SKIN ECZEMA AND LIPODERMATOSCLEROSIS COME
UNDER THE CLINICAL CLASS OF C4.
THE CLINICAL CLASS OF C4 UNDER CEAP INCLUDES CHANGES IN SKIN AND SUBCUTANEOUS TISSUE SECONDARY
TO CHRONIC VENOUS DISEASE. IT IS FURTHER CLASSIFIED AS,
- C4A- PIGMENTATION OR ECZEMA
- C4B- LIPODERMATOSCLEROSIS OR ATROPHIE BLANCHE
- C4C- CORONA PHLEBECTATICA
RECENT 2020 UPDATE ON THE CEAP SYSTEM:
- C2R FOR RECURRENT VARICOSE VEINS
- C4C FOR CORONA PHLEBECTATICA
- C6R FOR RECURRENT ACTIVE VENOUS ULCER.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING IS THE MOST COMMONLY SEEN TUMOR IN THE RETROPERITONEAL SPACE?
questions.explanation:
LIPOSARCOMA IS THE MOST COMMONLY SEEN TUMOR IN RETROPERITONEAL SPACE.
RETROPERITONEAL TUMORS CAN BE BENIGN OR MALIGNANT. MALIGNANT RETROPERITONEAL TUMORS MAY BE
MESODERMAL (75%), NEUROECTODERMAL (24%), OR EMBRYONIC REMNANT (1%) IN ORIGIN. RARELY IT CAN
BE UROLOGIC OR METASTATIC ALSO. THE ORDER OF FREQUENCY OF PRIMARY RETROPERITONEAL MALIGNANCY IS AS
FOLLOWS:
- LIPOSARCOMA
- LEIOMYOSARCOMA
- RHABDOMYOSARCOMA
- FIBROSARCOMA
- MALIGNANT NERVE SHEATH TUMORS
LIPOSARCOMA IS COMPOSED OF THREE HISTOLOGIC VARIETIES (LISTED IN ORDER OF DECREASING FREQUENCY):
- WELL-DIFFERENTIATED AND UNDIFFERENTIATED LIPOSARCOMA
- PLEOMORPHIC LIPOSARCOMA
- MYXOID/ROUND CELL LIPOSARCOMA
AMONG THE THREE SUBTYPES, PLEOMORPHIC LIPOSARCOMA IS THE MOST MALIGNANT AND OFTEN
METASTASIZES, WHILE THE WELL-DIFFERENTIATED IS THE LEAST MALIGNANT. MYXOID LIPOSARCOMA HAS
INTERMEDIATE MALIGNANT BEHAVIOR.
DIAGNOSIS IS CONFIRMED BY CONTRAST-ENHANCED CT WITH CT OF THE CHEST TO LOOK FOR METASTASES.
4771
SURGERY IS THE MAIN MODALITY OF TREATMENT. WIDE EXCISION WITH COMPLETE EN BLOC DISSECTION IS
DONE. POST-OPERATIVE RADIOTHERAPY AND CHEMOTHERAPY ARE USED AS ADJUVANT METHODS. RADIOTHERAPY
IS GIVEN AT A DOSE OF 5000 CGY, IT CAN BE EXTERNAL BEAM OR INTRA-OPERATIVE RADIOTHERAPY.
CHEMOTHERAPEUTIC AGENTS USED ARE MESNA, ADRIAMYCIN, IFOSFAMIDE AND DACARBAZINE (MAID
REGIMEN).

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
A 50-YEAR-OLD FEMALE PATIENT PRESENTS WITH A 4*3CM IRREGULAR MASS IN THE UPPER OUTER
QUADRANT OF THE RIGHT BREAST, WHICH IS NOT FIXED TO THE SKIN OR THE CHEST WALL. A LYMPH NODE OF
2CM IS PALPATED IN THE RIGHT AXILLA. NO MASS IS PALPATED IN THE OPPOSITE BREAST. WHICH OF THE
FOLLOWING INVESTIGATIONS WOULD YOU PERFORM ON THIS PATIENT?
questions.explanation:
Source note: The source PDF omits the numbered statements or table referenced by this question.

THE GIVEN CLINICAL SCENARIO IS SUGGESTIVE OF BREAST MALIGNANCY WITH LOCOREGIONAL SPREAD WITH
UNLIKELY DISTANT METASTASIS. FOR FURTHER EVALUATION OF THIS LESION, BILATERAL MAMMOGRAPHY, A
BIOPSY OF THE BREAST MASS AND A USG-GUIDED BIOPSY OF THE SUSPICIOUS LYMPH NODE NEED TO BE
PERFORMED IN ORDER TO DETERMINE STAGING AND DECIDE ON FURTHER MANAGEMENT.
STATEMENT 2: PET SCAN IS USUALLY PERFORMED IN ADVANCED CASES OF BREAST CANCER. IT IS NOT ROUTINELY
USED IN THE ASSESSMENT OF LOCOREGIONAL DISEASE.
STATEMENT 1: DIAGNOSTIC MAMMOGRAPHY IS USED TO EVALUATE WOMEN WITH ABNORMAL FINDINGS SUCH AS
A BREAST MASS OR NIPPLE DISCHARGE. MAMMOGRAPHY IS MORE ACCURATE THAN CLINICAL EXAMINATION FOR
THE DETECTION OF EARLY BREAST CANCERS. MAMMOGRAPHIC FEATURES SUGGESTIVE OF BREAST CANCER INCLUDE
A SOLID MASS WITH OR WITHOUT STELLATE FEATURES, MICROCALCIFICATIONS, IRREGULAR SOFT TISSUE SHADOW,
SPICULATIONS AND DUCT DISTORTION.
STATEMENT 3: PATHOLOGICAL DIAGNOSIS OF CARCINOMA IS MADE BY A CORE NEEDLE BIOPSY (TRU-CUT BIOPSY)
OR FINE-NEEDLE ASPIRATION BEFORE ANY TYPE OF TREATMENT IS STARTED.
STATEMENT 4: THE PRESENCE OR ABSENCE OF AXILLARY LYMPH NODE INVOLVEMENT IN BREAST CANCER IS ONE
OF THE MOST IMPORTANT PROGNOSTIC FACTORS FOR DETERMINING STAGING AND TREATMENT.
ULTRASOUND-GUIDED LYMPH NODE BIOPSY SHOULD BE DONE IN PATIENTS WITH SUSPICIOUS OR CLINICALLY
PALPABLE LYMPH NODES.
ULTRASOUND FEATURES SUGGESTIVE OF BREAST CANCER INCLUDE A HYPOECHOIC, IRREGULAR MASS WITH
INDISTINCT, ANGULATED OR SPICULATED MARGINS, ACOUSTIC SHADOWING, DUCTAL EXTENSION AND A BRANCHED
PATTERN OF MASS.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING IS TRUE ABOUT THE TILLAUX SIGN?
options: MASS IS FELT IN THE PERIUMBILICAL REGION
MASS IS MOBILE PERPENDICULAR TO MESENTERY ATTACHMENT LINE
questions.answer: MASS IS MOBILE PERPENDICULAR TO MESENTERY ATTACHMENT LINE
questions.explanation:
TILLAUX'S SIGN IS SAID TO BE POSITIVE IF THE MASS/SWELLING IS MOBILE PERPENDICULAR TO THE MESENTERY
ATTACHMENT LINE. TILLAUX’S SIGN IS SEEN IN A MESENTERIC CYST.
MESENTERIC CYSTS OCCUR EITHER IN THE SMALL INTESTINE (60%) OR THE COLON (40%) AND CAN BE CLASSIFIED
AS THE FOLLOWING:
- CHYLOLYMPHATIC (MOST COMMON TYPE)
- ENTEROGENOUS
- UROGENITAL REMNANT
- DERMOID
- OTHER CAUSES: TRAUMATIC HEMATOMA AND CYST FORMATION, TUBERCULOUS COLD ABSCESS OF MESENTERY
AND HYDATID CYST OF THE MESENTERY
THEY MOST COMMONLY OCCUR IN ADULTS WITH A MEAN AGE OF 45 YEARS. IT IS MORE COMMON IN FEMALES
THAN MALES (2:1). THE MOST COMMON PRESENTATION IS A PAINLESS ABDOMINAL SWELLING NEAR THE
UMBILICUS, WHICH IS SMOOTH AND NOT MOVING WITH RESPIRATION WITH TILLAUX'S TRIAD:
- SOFT, SMOOTH SWELLING IN THE UMBILICAL REGION
- FREELY MOBILE IN A DIRECTION PERPENDICULAR TO THE MESENTERY (TILLAUX'S SIGN)
- ZONE OF RESONANCE AROUND THE CYST
OTHER PRESENTATIONS INCLUDE RECURRENT ATTACKS OF ABDOMINAL PAIN DUE TO TEMPORARY IMPACTION OF A
FOOD BOLUS IN A SEGMENT OF THE BOWEL NARROWED BY THE CYST AND VOMITING.
COMPLICATIONS OF MESENTERIC CYST INCLUDE TORSION, RUPTURE, INFECTION AND HEMORRHAGE INTO THE
CYST.
ULTRASONOGRAPHY AND CT ARE USED TO DEMONSTRATE MESENTERIC CYSTS.
4773
TREATMENT:
- CHLYOLYMPHATIC CYST IS MANAGED BY ENUCLEATION.
- ENTEROGENOUS CYST IS MANAGED BY REMOVAL OF THE CYST WITH RESECTION OF THE ADJACENT BOWEL AS IT
ARISES AS A DIVERTICULUM OR DUPLICATION FROM THE ADJACENT BOWEL.
IN CASES WHERE COMPLETE EXCISION IS NOT POSSIBLE DUE TO THE CLOSE PROXIMITY TO VITAL STRUCTURES,
PARTIAL EXCISION OR MARSUPIALIZATION SHOULD BE PERFORMED.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: MATCH THE CORRECT ANSWER RELATED TO THE NERVE INJURIES IN VARIOUS SURGERIES:
questions.explanation:
A-1, B-2, C-3, AND D-4 IS THE CORRECT OPTION.
A: DURING BREAST SURGERY, REMOVAL OF THE AXILLARY LYMPH NODES IS COMMONLY DONE. THIS CARRIES A
RISK OF INJURY TO THE LONG THORACIC NERVE, WHICH ORIGINATES FROM THE C5-C7 ROOTS OF THE BRACHIAL
PLEXUS. IT INNERVATES THE SERRATUS ANTERIOR MUSCLE. INJURY TO THIS NERVE DURING SURGERY RESULTS IN
PARALYSIS OF THE SERRATUS ANTERIOR MUSCLE LEADING TO WINGING OF THE SCAPULA.
B: THE EXTERNAL LARYNGEAL NERVE IS A MOTOR NERVE THAT SUPPLIES THE CRICOTHYROID MUSCLE. THE CLOSE
RELATIONSHIP OF THE EXTERNAL LARYNGEAL NERVE TO THE SUPERIOR THYROID ARTERY PUTS THE NERVE AT
POTENTIAL RISK WHEN THE ARTERY IS CLAMPED DURING THYROID SURGERIES.
C: EXCISION OF THE SUBMANDIBULAR GLAND RESULTS IN POTENTIAL RISK TO 3 CRANIAL NERVES:
- MARGINAL MANDIBULAR BRANCH OF THE FACIAL NERVE
- LINGUAL NERVE
- HYPOGLOSSAL NERVE
D: THE VAGUS NERVE IS AT GREATER RISK OF INJURY DURING SURGERIES LIKE THYMECTOMY.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
A CHILD IS DIAGNOSED WITH CONGENITAL HYPERTROPHIC PYLORIC STENOSIS, WHICH AMONG THE FOLLOWING
CAN BE SEEN IN THIS CHILD?
questions.explanation:
4774
PATIENTS WITH CONGENITAL HYPERTROPHIC PYLORIC STENOSIS (CHPS) WILL PRESENT WITH NON-BILIOUS
PROJECTILE VOMITING AND VISIBLE PERISTALSIS OBSERVED MOVING FROM LEFT TO RIGHT (NOT FROM RIGHT TO
LEFT). METABOLIC ABNORMALITIES INCLUDE HYPOKALEMIA, HYPOCHLOREMIA AND METABOLIC ALKALOSIS.
CHPS OCCURS DUE TO HYPERTROPHY OF THE CIRCULAR MUSCLE OF THE PYLORUS, WHICH RESULTS IN
CONSTRICTION AND OBSTRUCTION OF THE GASTRIC OUTLET.
- PATIENTS COMMONLY PRESENT BETWEEN 2 AND 8 WEEKS OF AGE.
- FIRST-BORN MALE INFANTS ARE AT THE HIGHEST RISK.
- INFANTS USUALLY PRESENT WITH PROJECTILE, NON-BILIOUS VOMITING.
- CLINICALLY, AN OLIVE-SHAPED MASS IS PALPABLE IN THE RIGHT UPPER QUADRANT OR EPIGASTRIUM. WHEN
THE INFANT IS GIVEN A TEST FEED, VISIBLE PERISTALSIS IS USUALLY OBSERVED MOVING FROM LEFT TO RIGHT (NOT
FROM RIGHT TO LEFT), FOLLOWED BY PROJECTILE VOMITING.
METABOLIC ABNORMALITY:
- INFANTS WITH HYPERTROPHIC PYLORIC STENOSIS DEVELOP A CHARACTERISTIC METABOLIC ABNORMALITY I.E.
HYPOKALEMIC HYPOCHLOREMIC METABOLIC ALKALOSIS WITH PARADOXICAL ACIDURIA.
- PERSISTENT VOMITING RESULTS IN LOSS OF HYDROCHLORIC ACID, LEADING TO METABOLIC ALKALOSIS (DUE TO
LOSS OF H+) AND HYPOCHLOREMIA (DUE TO LOSS OF CL-).
- KIDNEYS TRY TO COMPENSATE FOR ALKALOSIS BY SECRETING NA+ AND HCO3-. HOWEVER, SODIUM LOSS
STIMULATES ALDOSTERONE SECRETION THROUGH THE RAAS PATHWAY.
- ALDOSTERONE CAUSES ACTIVE REABSORPTION OF SODIUM IN EXCHANGE FOR K+ AND H+ IONS LEADING TO THE
DEVELOPMENT OF HYPOKALEMIA AND PARADOXICAL ACIDURIA, SINCE THE BODY INITIALLY LOSES H+ IONS DUE
TO THE LOSS OF HCL, AND INSTEAD OF COMPENSATING FOR THAT LOSS, THE BODY IS LOSING MORE H+ IONS
THROUGH URINE.
MANAGEMENT:
- THE CHILD SHOULD BE REHYDRATED AND THE METABOLIC ABNORMALITY MUST BE CORRECTED BEFORE SURGERY.
- RAMSTEDT PYLOROMYOTOMY REMAINS THE STANDARD SURGICAL PROCEDURE FOR ITS TREATMENT.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: THE COMPONENTS OF QSOFA SCORING INCLUDE:
questions.explanation:
Source note: The source PDF omits the numbered statements or table referenced by this question.

THE QUICK SEQUENTIAL ORGAN FAILURE ASSESSMENT (QSOFA) SCORING SYSTEM DOES NOT RELY ON THE
HEART RATE.
IT IS A BEDSIDE SCORING SYSTEM THAT MAY IDENTIFY PATIENTS WITH SUSPECTED INFECTION, WHO ARE AT
GREATER RISK FOR SEPSIS OUTSIDE THE INTENSIVE CARE UNIT (ICU).
IT USES THREE CRITERIA, ASSIGNING ONE POINT EACH:
- LOW BLOOD PRESSURE (SBP≤100 MMHG)
- HIGH RESPIRATORY RATE (≥22 BREATHS PER MIN)
- ALTERED MENTAL STATUS
THE QSOFA SUGGESTS POTENTIALLY LIFE-THREATENING SEPSIS WHEN AT LEAST TWO OF THE PARAMETERS ARE
MET.
4775
NOTE :
THE PRIMARY METHOD TO EVALUATE THE RISK OF ORGAN DYSFUNCTION (SEPSIS) IN PATIENTS WITH SUSPECTED
INFECTION IS BY DETERMINING THE SEQUENTIAL (SEPSIS-RELATED) ORGAN FAILURE ASSESSMENT (SOFA) SCORE;
WHICH INCLUDES AN ASSESSMENT OF:
- CIRCULATION - SYSTOLIC BP & NEED FOR VASOPRESSORS; PLATELET COUNT
- RESPIRATION - PAO2/FIO2 & NEED FOR MECHANICAL VENTILATION
- MENTATION - GLASGOW COMA SCORE
- HEPATIC FUNCTION - BILIRUBIN
- RENAL FUNCTION - CREATININE
ORGAN DYSFUNCTION IS IDENTIFIED BY A SOFA SCORE OF ≥ 2
THE SOFA SCORE IS LIMITED BY ITS REQUIREMENT OF MULTIPLE LABORATORY TESTS WHICH MAKES IT COMPLEX
AND TIME-CONSUMING. IN ORDER TO SIMPLIFY THE SCORING PROCESS, THE "SEPSIS -3" TASK FORCE
RECOMMENDED THE QUICK SEPSIS-RELATED ORGAN DYSFUNCTION ASSESSMENT "QSOFA" SCORE.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING IS TRUE REGARDING INGUINAL HERNIA?
questions.explanation:
THE MEDIAL BORDER OF THE TRIANGLE OF DOOM IS BOUNDED BY VAS DEFERENS AND THE MEDIAL BORDER OF
THE MYOPECTINEAL ORIFICE IS BOUNDED BY THE LATERAL BORDER OF THE RECTUS ABDOMINIS.
THE TRIANGLE OF DOOM IS BOUNDED
- MEDIALLY BY THE VAS DEFERENS
- LATERALLY BY THE VESSELS OF THE SPERMATIC CORD (GONADAL VESSELS)
- INFERIORLY BY PERITONEAL REFLECTION
THE MYOPECTINEAL ORIFICE OF FRUCHAUD IS AN OSSEO-MYO-APONEUROTIC TUNNEL THROUGH WHICH ALL GROIN
HERNIAS OCCUR.
IT IS BOUNDED:
- MEDIALLY BY THE LATERAL BORDER OF THE RECTUS SHEATH.
- LATERALLY BY THE ILIOPSOAS MUSCLE.
- ABOVE BY THE ARCHED FIBERS OF THE INTERNAL OBLIQUE AND TRANSVERSUS ABDOMINIS MUSCLE.
- BELOW BY THE PECTIN PUBIS AND FASCIA COVERING IT.
4776

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: MATCH THE FOLLOWING:
questions.explanation:
A-3, B-1, C-2, AND D-4 IS THE CORRECT OPTION.
A: URO BAGS ARE USED FOR THE COLLECTION OF URINE. THEY ARE USUALLY ATTACHED TO FOLEY'S CATHETER,
WHICH IS PLACED TO DRAIN THE BLADDER (COMMONLY IN POSTOPERATIVE PATIENTS).
B: NASOGASTRIC TUBE/RYLE’S TUBE IS USED FOR NASOGASTRIC FEEDING/STOMACH WASH/ASPIRATION.
C: AN UNDERWATER SEAL BAG IS USED FOR THE COLLECTION OF DRAINAGE FLUID FROM THE THORACIC CAVITY. IT
ACTS AS A ONE-WAY VALVE ALLOWING AIR TO LEAVE THE PLEURAL CAVITY, BUT IT CANNOT BE DRAWN BACK IN BY
THE NEGATIVE PRESSURE THAT IS CREATED IN THE INTRATHORACIC CAVITY.
D: A METALLIC SUCTION CANNULA IS USED TO CLEAR THE OPERATIVE FIELD BY SUCTIONING SECRETIONS/BLOOD
AND ASPIRATING THE FLUID FROM VARIOUS CYSTS AND IN A PROCEDURE LIKE A HYDROCELE.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
A 40-YEAR-OLD MAN PRESENTS TO THE ER WITH SEVERE ABDOMINAL PAIN. ON EXAMINATION, HIS HR IS
110BPM, BP- 88/60MMHG. ON PER ABDOMEN EXAMINATION, GUARDING IS PRESENT. THE ERECT
ABDOMINAL X-RAY IS SHOWN BELOW. WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING WOULD YOU PROCEED WITH, FOR THE
MANAGEMENT OF THIS CASE?
questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN CLINICAL SCENARIO AND ERECT X-RAY ABDOMEN SHOWING GAS UNDER THE DIAPHRAGM ARE
SUGGESTIVE OF PNEUMOPERITONEUM, WHICH IS MANAGED BY INITIAL RESUSCITATION WITH IV FLUIDS
FOLLOWED BY EXPLORATORY LAPAROTOMY.
PNEUMOPERITONEUM IS THE PRESENCE OF AIR OR GAS IN THE PERITONEAL CAVITY. THE MOST COMMON CAUSE
OF PNEUMOPERITONEUM IS A PERFORATION OF A HOLLOW VISCUS. OTHER CAUSES OF PNEUMOPERITONEUM IN
ADULTS INCLUDE PERITONEAL DIALYSIS, AND MECHANICAL VENTILATION, AFTER PROCEDURES LIKE COLONOSCOPY
AND ENDOSCOPY. IN CHILDREN, IT CAN BE CAUSED BY NECROTIZING ENTEROCOLITIS, HIRSCHSPRUNG'S DISEASE,
MECONIUM ILEUS AND MECHANICAL VENTILATION.
THE PATIENT PRESENTS WITH ABDOMINAL PAIN AND DISTENSION, VOMITING, FEVER, CONSTIPATION,
TACHYCARDIA, TACHYPNEA, HYPOTENSION, AND REDUCED URINE OUTPUT. PER-ABDOMEN EXAMINATION CAN
SHOW GUARDING AND RIGIDITY.
4777
AN ERECT X-RAY ABDOMEN IS HIGHLY SENSITIVE FOR THE DETECTION OF FREE INTRAPERITONEAL GAS. SOME OF
THE SIGNS SEEN IN THE X-RAY INCLUDE:
- CUPOLA SIGN IS THE PRESENCE OF AIR UNDERNEATH THE DIAPHRAGM, GIVING A DOME-LIKE APPEARANCE.
- RIGLER'S SIGN IS WHERE BOTH BOWEL SURFACES ARE SEEN TOGETHER AS A SHARP MARGIN.
- FALCIFORM LIGAMENT SIGN IS THE OUTLINING OF THE FALCIFORM LIGAMENT WITH FREE ABDOMINAL GAS.
- LIVER/GALLBLADDER EDGE SIGN IS WHERE THE SHARP MARGINS OF THE LIVER/GALLBLADDER ARE VISIBLE DUE TO
THE COLLECTION OF AIR.
MANAGEMENT INCLUDES,
- ADEQUATE PREOPERATIVE RESUSCITATION WITH INTRAVENOUS FLUIDS FOLLOWED BY CORRECTION OF ELECTROLYTE
IMBALANCE, INSTITUTING BROAD-SPECTRUM INTRAVENOUS ANTIBIOTICS AND
- EARLY SURGICAL INTERVENTION/LAPAROTOMY TO ADDRESS THE CAUSE OF PNEUMOPERITONEUM AND PREVENT
FURTHER CONTAMINATION OF THE PERITONEAL CAVITY.
4778

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: THE TYPE OF KNOT SEEN IN THE IMAGE IS:
questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN IMAGE SHOWS THE SUTURE MATERIAL EXITING THE KNOT IS ON THE SAME SIDE AS THE ENTRY I.E NO
CROSS-OVER IS SEEN. THIS IS SEEN IN A REEF KNOT.
A KNOT IS A FASTENING MADE OF THREADS INTERTWINED TOGETHER OR ON THEMSELVES. EACH KNOT CONSISTS
OF- 2 HALF-HITCHES PLACED IN SEQUENTIAL THROWS. SQUARING REFERS TO TIGHTENING THE KNOT/HALF-HITCH IN A
MANNER THAT THE THREADS LAY FLAT DUE TO THE ALTERNATING DIRECTION OF HALF-HITCHES IN ADJACENT LAYERS.
4817
TYPES OF KNOTS:
- GRANNY KNOT: HALF-HITCH OVER A HALF-HITCH IN THE SAME DIRECTION. IT HAS BETTER-HOLDING POWER THAN
HALF-HITCH
- REEF KNOT: HALF-HITCH FOLLOWED BY A SECOND HALF-HITCH AFTER SQUARING.
- TRIPLE THROW KNOT: REEF KNOT WITH ANOTHER HALF-HITCH KNOT FOR ADDED SECURITY. KNOTS MADE WITH
PROLENE SUTURES REQUIRE 6-8 THROWS TO PREVENT SLIPPAGE.
- SURGEON’S KNOT: MODIFICATION OF THE REEF KNOT WITH TWO HALF-HITCHES IN THE FIRST LAYER.
- SLIP KNOT: MODIFICATION OF EITHER GRANNY/REEF KNOT FORMED WHEN ONE END OF THE THREAD IS KEPT TAUT
WHILE TIGHTENING THE KNOT.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING DRUGS CAUSES CARCINOMA BLADDER?
questions.explanation:
CYCLOPHOSPHAMIDE (AN ALKYLATING AGENT) CAUSES BLADDER CANCER
THE RISK OF BLADDER CANCER WITH CYCLOPHOSPHAMIDE IS DIRECTLY PROPORTIONAL TO THE DURATION AND
INTENSITY OF CYCLOPHOSPHAMIDE TREATMENT. PHOSPHORAMIDE MUSTARD IS THE PRIMARY MUTAGENIC
METABOLITE THAT CAUSES BLADDER CANCER IN PATIENTS EXPOSED TO CYCLOPHOSPHAMIDE.
PAINLESS, GROSS HEMATURIA IS THE MOST COMMON SYMPTOM THAT IS INDICATIVE OF A BLADDER CARCINOMA
UNTIL PROVEN OTHERWISE.
DEPENDING UPON THE DEPTH OF INVASION, BLADDER CARCINOMA CAN BE DIVIDED INTO
- FLAT, NON-INVASIVE CARCINOMA IN SITU (CIS)
- NON-MUSCLE INVASIVE BLADDER CANCER (70% OF CASES) - DOES NOT INVADE DETRUSOR MUSCLE BUT CAN
INVADE LAMINA PROPRIA.
- MUSCLE-INVASIVE BLADDER CANCER - INVADES THE DETRUSOR MUSCLE.
DIAGNOSIS IS BY CYSTOURETHROSCOPY (DIRECTLY VISUALIZING THE GROWTH) AND BIOPSY. MANAGEMENT IS AS
FOLLOWS:
4818
- NON-MUSCLE INVASIVE BLADDER CANCER:
- TRANSURETHRAL RESECTION OF BLADDER TUMOR (TURBT) FOLLOWED BY INTRAVESICAL CHEMOTHERAPY WITH
MITOMYCIN C OR EPIRUBICIN
- IMMUNOTHERAPY WITH REGULAR INTRAVESICAL INSTILLATIONS OF BACILLE CALMETTE GUERIN (BCG) IN
HIGH-RISK TUMORS.
- MUSCLE INVASIVE BLADDER CANCER: RADICAL CYSTECTOMY ALONG WITH URINARY DIVERSION PROCEDURE AND
LYMPH NODE DISSECTION +/- NEOADJUVANT CHEMOTHERAPY
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION B: CISPLATIN IS AN ANTICANCER DRUG USED TO TREAT TESTICULAR CANCER. IT IS ASSOCIATED WITH AN
INCREASED RISK FOR ACUTE MYELOID LEUKEMIA (AML).
OPTION C: TAXANE IS AN ANTICANCER DRUG AND IS THE MAIN COMPONENT IN THE TREATMENT REGIMENS OF
METASTATIC CANCERS. TAXANE'S ADVERSE EFFECTS ARE NEUTROPENIA AND FLUID RETENTION (PULMONARY
EDEMA).
OPTION D: TAMOXIFEN IS A SELECTIVE ESTROGEN RECEPTOR MODULATOR (SERM) AND IS USED IN THE
TREATMENT OF ESTROGEN-DEPENDENT BREAST CANCER. DUE TO ITS PARTIAL AGONISTIC ACTIVITY, IT IS KNOWN TO
INCREASE ENDOMETRIAL CANCER IN POST-MENOPAUSAL WOMEN.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: THE MOST COMMON SITE OF BRANCHIAL CYST IS ______.
options: JUNCTION OF UPPER AND MIDDLE THIRD OF THE STERNOMASTOID MUSCLE
JUNCTION OF MIDDLE AND LOWER THIRD OF THE STERNOMASTOID MUSCLE
BETWEEN THE TWO HEADS OF THE STERNOMASTOID MUSCLE
questions.answer: JUNCTION OF UPPER AND MIDDLE THIRD OF THE STERNOMASTOID MUSCLE
questions.explanation:
THE MOST COMMON SITE OF A BRANCHIAL CYST IS AT THE JUNCTION OF THE UPPER AND MIDDLE THIRD OF THE
STERNOMASTOID MUSCLE AT ITS ANTERIOR BORDER.
THE BELOW IMAGE SHOWS A LARGE RIGHT-SIDED BRANCHIAL CYST.
BRANCHIAL CYST DEVELOPS DUE TO THE PERSISTENCE OF THE CERVICAL SINUS. THE CERVICAL SINUS IS FORMED
WHEN THE 2ND ARCH MESODERM OVERGROWS THE SUCCEEDING ARCHES AND OVERHANGS THEM AS SHOWN IN
THE IMAGE. THE SPACE BETWEEN THE OVERHANGING 2ND PHARYNGEAL ARCH AND THE 3RD, 4TH, AND 6TH
ARCHES IS CALLED THE CERVICAL SINUS. THE CAVITY OF THE CERVICAL SINUS IS LINED BY ECTODERM AND
4819
NORMALLY GETS OBLITERATED.
BRANCHIAL CYSTS ARE USUALLY LINED BY SQUAMOUS EPITHELIUM AND CONTAIN THICK, TURBID FLUID FULL OF
CHOLESTEROL CRYSTALS. IT IS FLUCTUANT AND MAY TRANSILLUMINATE WHEN IT CONTAINS CLEAR FLUID.
A BRANCHIAL FISTULA MAY BE ACQUIRED OR CONGENITAL. THE CONGENITAL FISTULA IS SEEN AT THE JUNCTION OF
THE MIDDLE AND LOWER THIRD OF THE STERNOMASTOID (OPTION B). AN ACQUIRED FISTULA IS USUALLY SEEN IN
CASES OF INCOMPLETE SURGERY FOR THE BRANCHIAL CYST OR SPONTANEOUS RUPTURE, AND IT IS SEEN AT THE
SAME SITE AS THE CYST.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: DOHLMAN’S PROCEDURE IS FOR:
questions.explanation:
DOHLMAN’S PROCEDURE IS DONE FOR ZENKER’S DIVERTICULUM.
IT IS A TRANSORAL ENDOSCOPIC APPROACH, THAT ABLATES THE SEPTUM BETWEEN THE DIVERTICULUM AND THE
CERVICAL ESOPHAGUS. IT CAN BE USED FOR DIVERTICULA BETWEEN 2 AND 5 CM IN SIZE.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION A: MECKEL’S DIVERTICULUM IS A REMNANT OF THE VITELLOINTESTINAL DUCT AND IS TREATED BY
SURGICAL RESECTION.
OPTION C: BOCHADLEK’S HERNIA IS A CONGENITAL POSTEROLATERAL DEFECT ON THE LEFT SIDE OF THE DIAPHRAGM
DUE TO DEFECTIVE EMBRYOLOGICAL DEVELOPMENT.
OPTION D: MENETRIER’S DISEASE IS A PREMALIGNANT CONDITION WITH GROSS HYPERTROPHY OF GASTRIC
MUCOSAL FOLDS AND IS TREATED WITH GASTRECTOMY.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: PARATHYROID GLAND POST SURGERY IS COMMONLY TRANSFERRED TO:
questions.explanation:
THE PARATHYROID IS COMMONLY TRANSFERRED TO THE BRACHIORADIALIS MUSCLE POST-SURGERY. THIS WILL
FACILITATE EASY REMOVAL IF THERE IS DISEASE RECURRENCE AFTER SURGERY.
4820
PARATHYROIDECTOMY IS INDICATED IN:
- SYMPTOMATIC PRIMARY HYPERPARATHYROIDISM (HPT):
- ASYMPTOMATIC PRIMARY HPT WITH:
- RAISE IN SERUM CALCIUM >1MG/DL OF THE NORMAL RANGE
- >400 MG URINARY CALCIUM IN 24-HOUR URINE TEST
- < -2.5 Z-SCORE OF BONE MINERAL DENSITY
- AGE <50YR AND FAILED MEDICAL TREATMENT
- SEVERE CASES OF SECONDARY HPT
PARATHYROIDECTOMY IS PERFORMED IN NECK HYPEREXTENSION (SEMI-FOWLER POSITION). THE THYROID
GLAND IS MOBILIZED, AND THE PARATHYROID GLAND WITH ADENOMA IS IDENTIFIED AND RESECTED. THE
PARATHYROID TISSUE IS TRANSPLANTED TO THE NON-DOMINANT FOREARM.
POCKETS ARE MADE IN THE BELLY OF THE BRACHIORADIALIS MUSCLE, AND ONE TO TWO PIECES OF PARATHYROID
TISSUE MEASURING 1 MM EACH ARE PLACED INTO EACH POCKET. A TOTAL OF 12 TO 14 PIECES ARE
TRANSPLANTED. THIS IS A TYPE OF HETEROTOPIC TRANSPLANT.
MIAMI CRITERIA (CONFIRM THE ABSENCE OF ANOTHER HYPERACTIVE PARATHYROID): A DROP OF PARATHYROID
HORMONE INTRAOPERATIVELY, TO MORE THAN HALF THE MAXIMUM VALUE AT 10 MINUTES POSTRESECTION IS
CONSIDERED AN ADEQUATE RESECTION IN A PARATHYROID ADENOMA. HOWEVER, IF THERE IS NO DROP IN PTH
LEVEL, THEN A MULTI-GLAND DISEASE IS SUSPECTED AND THE SURGERY IS CONVERTED TO A BILATERAL NECK
EXPLORATION.
COMPLICATIONS OF PARATHYROIDECTOMY INCLUDE:
- PERSISTENT OR RECURRENT HYPERPARATHYROIDISM
- HYPOPARATHYROIDISM (PRESENTING AS HYPOCALCEMIA)
- HUNGRY BONE SYNDROME
- INJURY TO THE RECURRENT LARYNGEAL NERVE

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: WHAT IS THE DRUG USED FOR ESTROGEN DEPENDANT BREAST CANCER?
questions.explanation:
TAMOXIFEN IS A SELECTIVE ESTROGEN RECEPTOR MODULATOR (SERM) THAT IS MAINLY USED FOR ESTROGEN
RECEPTOR-POSITIVE BREAST CANCERS IN PRE-MENOPAUSAL WOMEN.
IT EXHIBITS SELECTIVE AGONISTIC AND ANTAGONISTIC ACTIVITY FOR ER RECEPTORS (ERα AND ERβ):
- AGONIST ACTIVITY AT THE UTERUS, BONE, LIVER, AND PITUITARY
- ANTAGONIST ACTIVITY IN BREAST AND BLOOD VESSELS
USES:
- PART OF THE PRIMARY TREATMENT REGIMEN FOR ESTROGEN RECEPTOR-POSITIVE (ER+) BREAST CANCERS IN
PRE-MENOPAUSAL WOMEN
- ADJUVANT THERAPY AFTER BREAST CONSERVATIVE SURGERY TO PREVENT A RECURRENCE
4821
- TAMOXIFEN ALSO IS EFFECTIVE (A 40%–50% REDUCTION IN TUMOR INCIDENCE) IN PREVENTING ER+ BREAST
CANCER IN WOMEN AT INCREASED RISK.
ADVERSE EFFECTS:
- VASOMOTOR SYMPTOMS (HOT FLASHES) AND SWEATING
- ENDOMETRIAL CANCER
- INCREASED RISK OF THROMBOEMBOLIC EVENTS
- FATTY LIVER DISEASE

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: THE COMMONEST SURGICAL APPROACH TO A RETROSTERNAL GOITER IS VIA:
questions.explanation:
THE COMMONEST SURGICAL APPROACH TO A RETROSTERNAL GOITER IS VIA THE NECK AND THE MOST COMMON
TYPE OF GOITRE APPROACHED IS THE SECONDARY RETROSTERNAL GOITER.
A GOITER IS CONSIDERED TO BE RETROSTERNAL IF AT LEAST 50% OF THE THYROID TISSUE IS LOCATED
INTRATHORACICALLY. THEY CAN BE PRIMARY OR SECONDARY.
RETROSTERNAL GOITER PRESENTS WITH DYSPNOEA, STRIDOR, AND DILATED NECK VEINS. PEMBERTON’S SIGN
(VENOUS CONGESTION OF THE NECK ON THE RAISING OF HANDS ABOVE THE HEAD) IS SEEN.
CONTRAST-ENHANCED COMPUTED TOMOGRAPHY (CECT) OF THE NECK IS PERFORMED TO ASSESS THE LOCATION
OF THE THYROID. THE DEFINITIVE TREATMENT IS SURGICAL EXCISION OF THE ECTOPIC THYROID.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION B & C: MEDIAN STERNOTOMY (VIA CHEST) IS INDICATED IN:
- PRIMARY MEDIASTINAL GOITER
- MALIGNANT RETROSTERNAL GOITER
- VERY LARGE RETROSTERNAL GOITER
- RECURRENCE IN THE MEDIASTINUM

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
AN INTERN PLACED AN INTERCOSTAL DRAINAGE TUBE IN A PATIENT. WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING STEPS IS
INCORRECT?
options: IDENTIFIED 5TH INTERCOSTAL SPACE ANTERIOR TO MID AXILLARY LINE TO PLACE THE TUBE
INSERTED TUBE ALONG THE LOWER BORDER OF UPPER RIB
DIRECTED TUBE POSTERIORLY TO PREVENT INJURY
questions.answer: INSERTED TUBE ALONG THE LOWER BORDER OF UPPER RIB
questions.explanation:
4822
AN INTERCOSTAL TUBE (ICD) IS PLACED ALONG THE UPPER BORDER OF THE LOWER RIB AT THE 5TH INTERCOSTAL
SPACE (ICS) TO PREVENT DAMAGE TO THE NEUROVASCULAR BUNDLE. HENCE, OPTION B IS INCORRECT.
CHEST TUBE INSERTION (THORACOSTOMY) IS INDICATED IN PNEUMOTHORAX, HEMOTHORAX, CHYLOTHORAX, AND
PLEURAL EFFUSION IN ORDER TO DRAIN AIR/FLUID FROM THE PLEURAL SPACE.
THE TRIANGLE OF SAFETY, USUALLY IN THE 5TH INTERCOSTAL SPACE, IS THE SAFEST SITE FOR CHEST TUBE INSERTION,
IT IS BOUND BY:
- ANTERIOR TO THE MIDAXILLARY LINE
- ABOVE THE HORIZONTAL LINE MARKED BY THE LEVEL OF THE NIPPLE
- BELOW AND LATERAL TO THE PECTORALIS MAJOR MUSCLE
CONTRAINDICATIONS INCLUDE PULMONARY ADHESIONS, PULMONARY TRAUMA, COAGULOPATHY, AND
DIAPHRAGMATIC HERNIA.
COMPLICATIONS OF THIS PROCEDURE:
4823
- INFECTION AT THE SITE OF INSERTION
- UNINTENTIONAL INJURY TO THE LUNG - HEMOTHORAX
- INTERCOSTAL NERVE/ VESSEL INJURY
- SUBCUTANEOUS HEMATOMA/ EMPHYSEMA

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: WHAT IS THE SIZE OF THE GIVEN BLADE USED FOR INCISION AND DRAINAGE OF A SUPERFICIAL ABSCESS?
questions.explanation:
THE SIZE OF THE SURGICAL BLADE SHOWN IS THE 11-SIZE BLADE (STAB KNIFE) THAT HAS A TRIANGULAR SHAPE
WITH AN OBLIQUE EDGE AND A SHARP-POINTED TIP.
USES:
- INCISION AND DRAINAGE (I & D) OF AN ABSCESS
- INSERTION OF DRAINS AND ARTERIOTOMY.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION A: THE 10-SIZE BLADE IS USED FOR SKIN INCISIONS. IT HAS A CURVED CUTTING EDGE THAT TAPERS TO A
POINTED TIP.
OPTION C: THE 22-SIZE BLADE IS OFTEN USED FOR ABDOMINAL INCISIONS. IT HAS A FLAT, UNSHARPENED BACK
EDGE AND A CURVED FRONT CUTTING EDGE.
OPTION D: THE 15-SIZE BLADE IS USED FOR MINOR SURGICAL PROCEDURES (LIPOMA EXCISION) AND PRECISE
SKIN INCISIONS. IT IS A SMALLER BLADE WITH A SMALL CUTTING EDGE.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: IN A BLAST INJURY, WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING ORGANS IS LEAST VULNERABLE TO THE BLAST WAVE?
questions.explanation:
IN A BLAST INJURY, THE LIVER IS THE LEAST VULNERABLE TO BLAST WAVE (PRIMARY BLAST) INJURY.
4824
BLAST INJURY IS A COMPLEX TYPE OF PHYSICAL TRAUMA RESULTING FROM DIRECT OR INDIRECT EXPOSURE TO AN
EXPLOSION. PRIMARY BLAST INJURIES RESULT FROM THE RAPID OVERPRESSURE OR SHOCK WAVES PRODUCED BY
AN EXPLOSION. THESE INJURIES RESULT FROM THE DRAMATIC CHANGES IN BAROMETRIC PRESSURE PROJECTING
OUTWARDS FROM THE POINT OF DETONATION. THEY PREDOMINANTLY CAUSE DAMAGE TO AIR-FILLED HOLLOW
ORGANS OF THE BODY FROM RAPID PRESSURE CHANGE (BAROTRAUMA). THIS INCLUDES THE MIDDLE EAR, LUNGS,
AND GIT.
THE MOST SENSITIVE AND MOST FREQUENTLY INJURED HOLLOW ORGANS ARE THE TYMPANIC MEMBRANES >
LUNGS. BLAST DAMAGE TO THE LUNGS IS THE MOST COMMON CAUSE OF LIFE-THREATENING INJURY FOLLOWING AN
EXPLOSION.
SOLID ORGANS ARE THE MOST RESISTANT TO BLAST INJURIES AS THE PARENCHYMAL DISRUPTION REQUIRES VERY
HIGH LEVELS OF OVERPRESSURE.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
A MAN PRESENTS WITH A SLOWLY PROGRESSIVE SWELLING OVER THE PAST 1 AND 1/2 YEARS. ON
EXAMINATION, IT HAS A VARIABLE CONSISTENCY AND APPEARS AS SHOWN IN THE IMAGE. WHAT IS THE
PROBABLE CAUSE?
questions.explanation:
A SLOWLY PROGRESSIVE SWELLING, WITH A VARIABLE CONSISTENCY, LIFTING THE EAR LOBE, IS SUGGESTIVE OF
PLEOMORPHIC ADENOMA OF THE PAROTID GLAND.
PLEOMORPHIC ADENOMA, THE MOST COMMON BENIGN SALIVARY GLAND TUMOR, PRIMARILY AFFECTS THE
PAROTID GLAND, PARTICULARLY ITS SUPERFICIAL LOBE. IT IS ALSO REFERRED TO AS A MIXED TUMOR DUE TO ITS
COMBINATION OF EPITHELIAL AND MESENCHYMAL COMPONENTS. THIS TUMOR MOST COMMONLY OCCURS IN
FEMALES AROUND THE AGE OF 40.
CLINICAL FEATURES:
- PAINLESS, SLOW-GROWING SWELLING
- LOBULATED, FIRM, VARIABLE IN CONSISTENCY
- LIFTS THE EARLOBE
- NO FACIAL NERVE INVOLVEMENT
4825
- CURTAIN SIGN POSITIVE - CANNOT BE MOVED ABOVE THE ZYGOMATIC BONE.
- IN CASE OF DEEP LOBE INVOLVEMENT, TONSILS, AND FAUCIAL PILLARS WILL BE PUSHED MEDIALLY.
- FEATURES OF MALIGNANCY - A SUDDEN INCREASE IN SIZE, ULCERATION OF THE OVERLYING SKIN, FACIAL NERVE
PALSY (INVOLVEMENT OF FACIAL NERVE), PAINFUL SWELLING, AND RESTRICTION OF JAW MOVEMENTS.
FINE NEEDLE ASPIRATION CYTOLOGY (FNAC) IS THE INVESTIGATION OF CHOICE IN DIAGNOSING PLEOMORPHIC
ADENOMA. OPEN BIOPSY IS CONTRAINDICATED DUE TO THE CHANCES OF INJURY TO THE FACIAL NERVE.
ALL TUMORS OF THE SUPERFICIAL LOBE OF THE PAROTID GLAND SHOULD BE MANAGED BY SUPERFICIAL
PAROTIDECTOMY. RADICAL PAROTIDECTOMY IS PERFORMED FOR MALIGNANT PLEOMORPHIC ADENOMA.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION A: ADAMANTINOMA IS A LOW-GRADE MALIGNANT TUMOR THAT USUALLY PRESENTS WITH PRE-TIBIAL
PAIN AND SWELLING SINCE IT MOST COMMONLY AFFECTS THE TIBIAL DIAPHYSIS.
OPTION B: DERMOID CYSTS PRESENT AS FIRM PAINLESS SUBCUTANEOUS NODULES AND ARE OF 4 TYPES:
- SEQUESTRATION DERMOID - SEQUESTRATION OF EPITHELIUM DURING EMBRYOLOGICAL DEVELOPMENT.
- TUBULODERMOID - ACCUMULATION OF SECRETIONS FROM ECTODERMAL TUBE/DUCT
- IMPLANTATION DERMOID - IMPLANTATION OF THE EPIDERMIS DUE TO TRAUMA
- TERATOMATOUS DERMOID - HAVING ALL 3 GERM LAYERS (ECTO, MESO, AND ENDODERM)
OPTION D: SEBACEOUS CYSTS ARE RETENTION CYSTS OF THE SEBACEOUS GLANDS THAT PRESENT AS SMOOTH,
NON-TENDER, NON-TRANSILLUMINATION SWELLING WITH A PUNCTUM (IN 70% OF THE PATIENTS).

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: WHAT IS SHOWN IN THE GIVEN IMAGE?
questions.explanation:
THE IMAGE SHOWS A DARK-COLORED SUMMIT OVER A SWELLING, USUALLY SEEN IN A SEBACEOUS CYST.
SEBACEOUS CYSTS ARE THE RETENTION CYSTS OF THE SEBACEOUS GLAND THAT ARE USUALLY PRESENT ON THE FACE,
SCALP, OR SCROTUM. THEY CONTAIN YELLOWISH-WHITE CHEESY MATERIAL WITH FAT AND EPITHELIUM.
CLINICAL FEATURES:
- THE SWELLING IS PAINLESS, SOFT, AND FREELY MOBILE.
- THOUGH NON-TRANSILLUMINATING, THEY ARE PAGET'S TEST POSITIVE (FLUCTUANT).
- PUNCTUM IS SEEN IN 70% OF THE PATIENTS WITH SEBACEOUS CYSTS. THEY ARE DARK IN COLOR DUE TO THE
ACCUMULATION OF DENUDED EPITHELIUM.
- THEY ALSO HAVE AN UNPLEASANT SEBUM ODOR.
- THE SWELLING CAN ULCERATE AND BECOME PAINFUL (COCK’S PECULIAR TUMOR).
- SOME CYSTS OVER THE SCALP MAY ALSO HARDEN OVER TIME (SEBACEOUS HORN).
- MANY MAY GET INFECTED AND LEAD TO ABSCESS FORMATION.
TREATMENT:
- EXCISION INCLUDING SKIN ADJACENT TO PUNCTUM USING ELLIPTICAL INCISION-DISSECTION METHOD.
- INCISION AND AVULSION OF CYST WALL.
4826
- IN THE PRESENCE OF AN ABSCESS, AN INITIAL TREATMENT WITH AN INCISION LATER FOLLOWED BY EXCISION OF
THE CYST
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION A: DERMOID CYSTS PRESENT AS FIRM PAINLESS SUBCUTANEOUS NODULES AND ARE OF 4 TYPES:
- SEQUESTRATION DERMOID - SEQUESTRATION OF EPITHELIUM DURING EMBRYOLOGICAL DEVELOPMENT
- TUBULODERMOID - ACCUMULATION OF SECRETIONS FROM ECTODERMAL TUBE/DUCT
- IMPLANTATION DERMOID - IMPLANTATION OF THE EPIDERMIS DUE TO TRAUMA
- TERATOMATOUS DERMOID - HAVING ALL 3 GERM LAYERS (ECTO, MESO, AND ENDODERM)
OPTION C: MENINGIOMAS ARE BENIGN TUMORS ARISING FROM THE MENINGOTHELIAL CELLS OF THE DURA. THEY
PRESENT WITH HEADACHES, SEIZURES, OR FOCAL NEUROLOGICAL DEFICITS.
OPTION D: POSTAURICULAR CUTANEOUS MASTOID FISTULA IS A RARE COMPLICATION OF CHRONIC OTITIS MEDIA
THAT HEALS VERY SLOWLY AND NEEDS SURGICAL CLOSURE.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
A FEMALE PATIENT PRESENTS WITH A BREAST ABSCESS. AN ASPIRATION WAS ATTEMPTED UNDER ANTIBIOTIC
COVER WHICH FAILED TO REVEAL ANY ASPIRATE. WHAT IS THE NEXT STEP IN MANAGEMENT?
options: STOP ANTIBIOTICS AS NO ASPIRATE WAS COLLECTED
questions.explanation:
IN A PATIENT WITH A BREAST ABSCESS, THE NEXT STEP AFTER A FAILED ASPIRATION IS TO ATTEMPT ASPIRATION
ONCE AGAIN UNDER ANTIBIOTIC COVER.
INCISION AND DRAINAGE IS NOT PREFERRED, AS IT CAN POTENTIALLY INTERFERE WITH BREASTFEEDING, AND
DELICATE STRUCTURES SUCH AS DUCTS, LOBULES, AND TUBULES MAY BE INJURED, POSSIBLY LEADING TO A
NON-HEALING MILK FISTULA.
A BREAST ABSCESS IS A COMPLICATION OF ACUTE MASTITIS, WHICH IS MORE COMMON IN NEW MOTHERS AT THE
BEGINNING OF LACTATION (LACTATIONAL MASTITIS). NON-LACTATIONAL MASTITIS IS MORE COMMON IN DIABETIC,
IMMUNOSUPPRESSED PEOPLE AND PEOPLE PREDISPOSED BY DUCT ECTASIA AND PERIAREOLAR INFECTIONS.
CLINICAL FEATURES OF A BREAST ABSCESS INCLUDE:
- FEVER AND MALAISE
- LOCALIZED PAIN AND TENDERNESS
- REDNESS AND SWELLING OF THE AFFECTED BREAST
- POSITIVE FLUCTUATION TEST.
4827
AN ULTRASONOGRAM OF THE AFFECTED BREAST IS PERFORMED TO CONFIRM THE ABSCESS, AND TREATMENT
PROCEEDS AS FOLLOWS:
- ANALGESICS, ANTIPYRETICS, AND BREAST SUPPORT FOR PAIN AND FEVER RELIEF.
- ASPIRATION IS PERFORMED UNDER ANTIBIOTIC COVER, AND THE PUS IS CULTURED. IF ASPIRATION PROVES
UNSUCCESSFUL, IT SHOULD BE REATTEMPTED AFTER A FEW DAYS.
- INCISION AND DRAINAGE SHOULD BE CONSIDERED IN CASES OF:
- MASTITIS UNRESPONSIVE TO ANTIBIOTICS FOR 48 HOURS.
- BRAWNY INDURATION.
- PROGRESSIVE MASTITIS WITH PERSISTENT FEVER

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: WHICH NERVE IS INVOLVED IN FREY’S SYNDROME?
questions.explanation:
THE AURICULOTEMPORAL NERVE (V3 NERVE) IS INVOLVED IN FREY'S SYNDROME (GUSTATORY SWEATING).
FREY’S SYNDROME IS ALSO KNOWN AS DUPUY SYNDROME OR AURICULOTEMPORAL SYNDROME. IT COMMONLY
DEVELOPS AFTER PAROTID SURGERY. IT IS CAUSED BY AN ABERRANT REGENERATION OF POST-GANGLIONIC
PARASYMPATHETIC NERVE FIBERS CROSSED ALONG THE SYMPATHETIC PATHWAYS TO THE SWEAT GLANDS NEAR THE
PAROTID REGION.
CLINICAL FEATURES ARE DUE TO THE RESULT OF SALIVARY STIMULATION (BY THE SMELL OR TASTE OF FOOD) LEADING
TO THE SWEATING AND FLUSHING OF THE PERIAURICULAR REGION ON THE INVOLVED SIDE OF THE FACE. A STARCH
IODINE TEST IS USED FOR DIAGNOSIS.
TREATMENT RANGES FROM ANTIPERSPIRANTS (IN MILD CASES) TO TYMPANIC NEURECTOMY OR BOTULINUM
TOXIN INJECTION (IN SEVERE CASES). IT CAN BE PREVENTED BY INCORPORATING CAREFUL EXTRACAPSULAR
DISSECTION AND CLOSURE OF THE SUPERFICIAL MUSCULOAPONEUROTIC LAYER DURING PAROTIDECTOMY.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTION A: FACIAL NERVE IS THE 7TH CRANIAL NERVE THAT SUPPLIES THE MUSCLES OF THE FACE, AND RESULTS IN
FACIAL PARALYSIS IF INJURED DURING PAROTIDECTOMY
OPTION B: OCULOMOTOR IS THE 3RD CRANIAL NERVE WHICH SUPPLIES THE EXTRAOCULAR MUSCLES. IF INJURED
DURING OPHTHALMIC SURGERIES, IT RESULTS IN OCULAR PARALYSIS AND THE EYE POINTING DOWN AND OUT.
OPTION D: GLOSSOPHARYNGEAL NERVE IS THE 9TH CRANIAL NERVE AND ITS INJURY CAUSES LOSS OF TASTE
SENSATION FROM THE POSTERIOR 1/3RD OF THE TONGUE.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING STATEMENTS IS FALSE REGARDING DEEP VEIN THROMBOSIS (DVT)?
options: MOST COMMON CLINICAL PRESENTATION IS PAIN AND TENDERNESS IN CALF
SOME CASES MAY DIRECTLY PRESENT AS PULMONARY THROMBOEMBOLISM
questions.explanation:
MOST CASES OF DEEP VEIN THROMBOSIS (DVT) ARE UNILATERAL. IT IS BILATERAL IN ONLY 30% OF THE
INDIVIDUALS.
DVT REFERS TO THROMBOSIS OF THE DEEP VENOUS SYSTEM.
4829
CAUSED BY:
- POSTOPERATIVE THROMBOSIS (MOST COMMON CAUSE)
- ORAL CONTRACEPTIVE PILLS (OCPS)
- AFTER CHILDBIRTH
- IMMOBILITY
SITES:
- PELVIC VEINS—COMMON
- LEG VEINS—COMMON IN FEMORAL AND POPLITEAL VEINS (COMMON ON THE LEFT SIDE).
FEVER IS THE EARLIEST SYMPTOM, WHICH IS ALSO MOST COMMONLY ACCOMPANIED BY PAIN AND TENDERNESS
IN THE CALF AND THIGH (OPTION C).
THE FOLLOWING SIGNS COULD BE ELICITED:
- POSITIVE HOMAN'S SIGN: RESISTANCE OF CALF MUSCLES ON PASSIVE FORECEFUL DORSIFLEXION OF THE FOOT.
- MOSE'S SIGN: GENTLE SQUEEZING OF THE LOWER PART OF THE CALF FROM SIDE TO SIDE IS PAINFUL.
- NEUHOF'S SIGN: THICKENING AND DEEP TENDERNESS SEEN ON DEEP PALPATION OF THE CALF MUSCLES.
SOMETIMES, THE THROMBUS MAY GET DISLODGED AND PRESENT AS PULMONARY THROMBOEMBOLISM (OPTION
D) WITH FEATURES OF DYSPNOEA, TACHYPNOEA, AND CHEST PAIN.
CLINICAL FEATURES ARE UNRELIABLE FOR MAKING A DEFINITIVE DIAGNOSIS (OPTION A), AND A VENOUS DOPPLER
IS THE BEST MODALITY FOR CONFIRMING DVT. IT REVEALS A NON-COMPRESSIBLE DILATED VEIN. THE LIKELIHOOD
OF PULMONARY EMBOLISM CAN BE PREDICTED USING MODIFIED WELLS CRITERIA.
PATIENTS WITH DVT SHOULD BE IMMEDIATELY STARTED WITH SUBCUTANEOUS LOW MOLECULAR WEIGHT
HEPARIN (LMWH). IF CONTRAINDICATED DUE TO RENAL INSUFFICIENCY OR THROMBOCYTOPENIA-RELATED
CONDITIONS, THEY SHOULD BE STARTED ON FONDAPARINUX (INDIRECT FACTOR XA INHIBITOR) OR BIVALIRUDIN
(DIRECT THROMBIN INHIBITOR). ANTICOAGULANTS SHOULD BE ADMINISTERED FOR A MINIMUM PERIOD OF 3
MONTHS. VENA CAVA FILTERS ARE USED IN PATIENTS WITH BLEEDING RISKS (LIKE HEMOPHILIA).

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
A TRUCK DRIVER PRESENTS WITH DILATED, TORTUOUS VEINS OF 4 MM IN THE FOOT. WHAT IS THE STAGE OF
CLINICAL CLASSIFICATION ACCORDING TO CEAP(CLINICAL-ETIOLOGY-ANATOMY-PATHOPHYSIOLOGY FOR
CHRONIC VENOUS DISORDERS)?
questions.explanation: DILATED TORTUOUS VEINS OF 4 MM INDICATE VARICOSE VEINS, SO THE STAGE IS C2.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING STATEMENTS IS FALSE REGARDING RECTAL CARCINOMA?
options: HARTMANN’S OPERATION IS DONE IN ELDERLY DEBILITATED PATIENTS
ADENOCARCINOMA IS A RARE VARIANT OF RECTAL CARCINOMA
EARLY MORNING SPURIOUS DIARRHOEA AND TENESMUS CAN OCCUR

questions.answer: ADENOCARCINOMA IS A RARE VARIANT OF RECTAL CARCINOMA
questions.explanation:
ADENOCARCINOMA IS THE MOST COMMON VARIANT OF RECTAL CARCINOMA.
COLORECTAL CANCER IS:
- THE SECOND MOST COMMON MALIGNANCY GLOBALLY
- THE SECOND MOST COMMON CANCER IN WOMEN
- THE THIRD MOST COMMON CANCER IN MEN
4830
- THE FOURTH MOST COMMON CAUSE OF DEATH DUE TO CANCER.
SYMPTOMS OF RECTAL CARCINOMA INCLUDE:
- PAINLESS BLEEDING - EARLIEST AND MOST COMMON
- ALTERATION OF BOWEL HABITS - CHANGE IN FREQUENCY AND CONSISTENCY OF THE STOOL
- TENESMUS - UNABLE TO PASS A MOTION EVEN WHEN THERE IS THE SENSATION OF NEEDING TO EVACUATE THE
BOWEL. IT IS SUGGESTIVE OF A TUMOR OF THE LOWER HALF OF THE RECTUM
- EARLY MORNING BLOODY DIARRHEA (OPTION C) - PASSAGE OF BLOOD AND MUCUS IN ADDITION TO FECES. PAIN
AND WEIGHT LOSS ARE USUALLY LATE SYMPTOMS
ABDOMINAL EXAMINATION AND DIGITAL RECTAL EXAMINATION ARE USED FOR THE PRIMARY EVALUATION. RIGID
SIGMOIDOSCOPY IS PERFORMED TO OBTAIN A BIOPSY. A SYNCHRONOUS TUMOR (PRIMARY TUMOR WITH A
DIFFERENT ORIGIN THAN THE ONE CURRENTLY INVESTIGATED) IS EXCLUDED BY PERFORMING A COLONOSCOPY.

OFFERED TO ONLY THOSE PATIENTS WHO HAVE A COMPLETE CLINICAL RESPONSE TO NEOADJUVANT.
THE TYPE OF SURGERY DEPENDS ON MULTIPLE FACTORS (SIZE, LOCATION, AGE OF THE PATIENT, ETC). HOWEVER,
THE GENERAL CONSENSUS IS:
- EARLY CANCER (T1 AND A FEW T2) IS LOCALLY EXCISED VIA THE TRANSANAL APPROACH.
- MOST RECTAL CANCER IS TREATED BY ANTERIOR RESECTION AND COLORECTAL/COLOANAL ANASTOMOSIS.
- LOW EXTENSIVE TUMORS ARE TREATED BY LAPAROSCOPIC ABDOMINOPERINEAL RESECTION(APR) AND
PERMANENT COLOSTOMY.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: A GASLESS ABDOMEN IS SEEN IN:
questions.explanation:
A GASLESS ABDOMEN IS AN X-RAY FEATURE THAT CAN BE SEEN IN ACUTE PANCREATITIS. PATIENTS WITH ACUTE
PANCREATITIS CAN HAVE SIGNIFICANT VOMITING AND DIARRHEA THAT MAY PRODUCE A GASLESS ABDOMEN.
COMMON CAUSES OF GASLESS ABDOMEN INCLUDE:
- HIGH OBSTRUCTION: GASTRIC OUTLET OBSTRUCTION, CONGENITAL ATRESIA
- SMALL BOWEL OBSTRUCTION
- BOWEL ISCHEMIA
- ASCITES
- ACUTE PANCREATITIS
- GASTROENTERITIS
- LARGE ABDOMINAL MASS - DUE TO DISPLACEMENT
- POST-SURGERY FOLLOWING TOTAL COLECTOMY, ESOPHAGOGASTRECTOMY, GASTRECTOMY, AND LOW ANTERIOR
RESECTION
- A PAUCITY OF SMALL BOWEL GAS MAY BE A NORMAL FINDING IN SOME ADULTS
NOTE: IN INTUSSUSCEPTION, AN X-RAY SHOWS SMALL BOWEL OBSTRUCTION, A MASS, AND A PAUCITY OF GAS IN
THE RIGHT ILIAC FOSSA.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: GALL STONE CHEMISTRY MOST COMMONLY SEEN AMONGST THE FOLLOWING IS:
questions.explanation:
THE MOST COMMON GALLSTONE CHEMISTRY SEEN IS CRYSTALLINE CHOLESTEROL MONOHYDRATE.
TYPES OF GALLSTONES:
- CHOLESTEROL STONES (75% OF GALLSTONES) HAVE >70% CHOLESTEROL BY WEIGHT AND ARE COMPOSED OF
CRYSTALLINE CHOLESTEROL MONOHYDRATE. THE MAJORITY OF CHOLESTEROL STONES HAVE A MIXED COMPOSITION
WITH BILE PIGMENTS AND CALCIUM, IN ADDITION TO THE CHOLESTEROL. THEY ARE THE MOST COMMON TYPE OF
GALL STONES WORLDWIDE AND IN INDIA.
4832
- PIGMENT STONES HAVE <20% CHOLESTEROL AND ARE DARK DUE TO THE PRESENCE OF CALCIUM
BILIRUBINATE AS THE MAJOR CONSTITUENT.
- BLACK PIGMENT STONES (20% OF GALLSTONES) - ARE FORMED DUE TO SUPERSATURATION OF UNCONJUGATED
BILIRUBIN (SEEN IN HEREDITARY HEMOLYTIC ANEMIA (LIKE SICKLE CELL AND HEREDITARY SPHEROCYTOSIS)
- BROWN PIGMENT STONES (5% OF GALLSTONES) - FORMED SECONDARY TO INFECTIONS (LIKE E. COLI, AND
ASCARIS LUMBRICOIDES)
NOTE: PURE CHOLESTEROL STONES ARE UNCOMMON AND ACCOUNT FOR <10% OF ALL STONES.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
A 56-YEAR-OLD PATIENT SUFFERING FROM ALCOHOLIC CIRRHOSIS RECEIVES A HEALTHY LIVER FROM HIS
BIOLOGICAL SON. WHAT IS THIS TYPE OF TRANSPLANT KNOWN AS?
questions.explanation:
TRANSPLANT OF AN ORGAN/TISSUE FROM A SON TO A PARENT IS AN EXAMPLE OF AN ALLOGRAFT.
AN ALLOGRAFT IS TRANSPLANT OF CELLS/TISSUES/ORGANS FROM A GENETICALLY NON-IDENTICAL DONOR OF THE SAME
SPECIES.
ISOGRAFTS ARE ALLOGRAFTS IN WHICH CELLS/TISSUES/ORGANS ARE TRANSPLANTED FROM A DONOR TO A GENETICALLY
IDENTICAL RECIPIENT. (MONOZYGOTIC TWINS)

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
ESOPHAGEAL ENDOSCOPY OF A PATIENT REVEALS THE PRESENCE OF SERPIGINOUS ULCERS. THIS FINDING
INDICATES:
questions.explanation:
THE IMAGE SHOWING SERPIGINOUS ULCERS IN THE OTHERWISE NORMAL MUCOSA OF THE DISTAL ESOPHAGUS IS
SUGGESTIVE OF CYTOMEGALOVIRAL ESOPHAGITIS.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING IS NOT A PART OF REVISED TRAUMA SCORE (RTS)?
questions.explanation:
PULSE RATE IS NOT A PART OF REVISED TRAUMA SCORE.
4833
THE REVISED TRAUMA SCORE IS MADE UP OF 3 CATEGORIES: GLASGOW COMA SCALE, SYSTOLIC BLOOD
PRESSURE, AND RESPIRATORY RATE.
THE SCORE RANGE IS 0–12.
A PATIENT WITH AN RTS SCORE OF 12 IS LABELLED DELAYED, 11 IS URGENT, AND 3–10 IS IMMEDIATE. THOSE
WHO HAVE AN RTS BELOW 3 ARE DECLARED DEAD.
4834

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: WHICH OF THE FOLLOWING IS TRUE ABOUT THE FLAP GIVEN IN THE IMAGE.
options: PEDICLED TRAM BASED ON SUPERIOR EPIGASTRIC ARTERY
FREE TRAM BASED ON SUPERIOR AND INFERIOR EPIGASTRIC ARTERY
DIEP BASED ON DEEP INFERIOR EPIGASTRIC ARTERY
LOWER ABDOMINAL FAT BASED INFERIOR EPIGASTRIC VESSELS
questions.answer: DIEP BASED ON DEEP INFERIOR EPIGASTRIC ARTERY
questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN IMAGE SHOWING ONLY SKIN AND FAT MOVED TO THE CHEST IS SUGGESTIVE OF A DEEP INFERIOR
EPIGASTRIC ARTERY PERFORATOR FLAP (DIEP), BASED ON THE DEEP INFERIOR EPIGASTRIC ARTERY.
4844
DIEP IS A VARIANT OF TRAM FLAP AND FREE FLAP WHERE ONLY THE SKIN AND FAT ARE MOVED TO THE CHEST.
A MICROVASCULAR TECHNIQUE IS USED IN WHICH NO MUSCLE IS TAKEN AND THE PERFORATING VESSELS ARE
DISSECTED OUT.
AS THE MUSCLE IS SPARED IN DIEP, THERE IS A REDUCED RISK OF ABDOMINAL WALL WEAKNESS AND ITS
ASSOCIATED COMPLICATIONS.
OTHER OPTIONS:
OPTIONS A AND B: THE PEDICLED TRAM FLAP IS BASED ON THE SUPERIOR EPIGASTRIC ARTERY AND THE FREE
TRAM FLAP IS BASED ON SUPERIOR AND INFERIOR EPIGASTRIC ARTERIES (SUPERCHARGED TRAM FLAP);
HOWEVER, THE GIVEN IMAGE DEPICTS A DEEP INFERIOR EPIGASTRIC ARTERY FLAP. IN TRAM FLAPS:
- THE SKIN, FAT, AND MUSCLE ARE MOVED TO THE CHEST.
- IT PROVIDES GOOD COSMESIS AND BULK SINCE IT HAS A SOFT TISSUE CONSISTENCY SIMILAR TO THE BREAST.
- DISADVANTAGES INCLUDE EPIGASTRIC BULGE, PARTIAL FLAP LOSS, FAT NECROSIS, ABDOMINAL WALL WEAKNESS,
AND HERNIAS.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt: WHAT IS THE MOST COMMON SITE OF GASTRINOMA IN MEN 1 SYNDROME?
questions.explanation:
THE MOST COMMON SITE OF GASTRINOMA IN MEN 1 SYNDROME IS THE DUODENUM.
GASTRINOMA IS THE MOST COMMON PANCREATIC ISLET TUMOR IN MEN 1 SYNDROME, ARISING FROM THE G
CELLS OF THE PANCREAS. GASTRINOMA, ASSOCIATED WITH MARKED GASTRIC ACID PRODUCTION AND RECURRENT
PEPTIC ULCERS, IS CALLED ZOLLINGER-ELLISON SYNDROME. THE MAJORITY OF GASTRINOMAS OCCUR IN THE
GASTRINOMA (PASSARO'S) TRIANGLE.
IN MEN 1, THEY OFTEN OCCUR IN PATIENTS <30 YEARS. PATIENTS PRESENT WITH ABDOMINAL PAIN (THE
MOST COMMON SYMPTOM), DIARRHEA AND STEATORRHEA.
MANAGEMENT:
4845
- MEDICAL MANAGEMENT FOR TUMORS <2 CM WITH PROTON-PUMP INHIBITORS.
- SURGERY FOR TUMORS >2 CM.
- PROTON-PUMP INHIBITORS WITH SOMATOSTATIN ANALOGUES FOR ADVANCED LOCOREGIONAL DISEASE OR
METASTASIS.

questions.subject: General Surgery
questions.prompt:
A 50-YEAR-OLD MALE WHO IS A CHRONIC SMOKER PRESENTED TO THE HOSPITAL WITH INTERMITTENT
CLAUDICATION PAIN OF BOTH THIGH AND BUTTOCK REGION ON WALKING ABOUT 500 M. WHICH OF THE
FOLLOWING IS A LIKELY DIAGNOSIS?
options: ARTERIAL DISEASE INVOLVING THE SUPERFICIAL FEMORAL ARTERY
ARTERIAL DISEASE INVOLVING THE PROFUNDA FEMORIS ARTERY
questions.explanation:
THE GIVEN CLINICAL SCENARIO IS SUGGESTIVE OF ARTERIAL DISEASE WITH AORTOILIAC INVOLVEMENT. CLASSICALLY,
THE MUSCLE GROUP AFFECTED BY CLAUDICATION IS ONE ANATOMICAL LEVEL BELOW THE LEVEL OF ARTERIAL
DISEASE.
INTERMITTENT CLAUDICATION IS A FEATURE OF CHRONIC ARTERIAL DISEASE OR OCCLUSION OF THE ARTERY.
AORTOILIAC DISEASE AFFECTS THE INFRARENAL AORTA AND ILIAC ARTERIES.
MANAGEMENT INVOLVES SMOKING CESSATION, LIFESTYLE MODIFICATIONS, AND TREATMENT OF UNDERLYING
DIABETES OR HYPERLIPIDEMIA IF PRESENT.
FOR CLAUDICATION, CILOSTAZOL OR PENTOXYFILLINE IS USED. CILOSTAZOL IS SUPERIOR TO PENTOXYFILLINE.
SURGICAL OPTIONS INCLUDE AORTOILIAC BYPASS, AORTOBIFEMORAL BYPASS, PERCUTANEOUS TRANSLUMINAL
ANGIOPLASTY (PTA), WHICH CAN BE WITH OR WITHOUT STENT PLACEMENT, AND THROMBOENDARTERECTOMY.
